review_title: Fun and simple, but not for speeders
review_text:
I love the simplistic design, nice colors, and compact design of this puzzle!  It is almost like a "fidget-spinner" = relaxing just to play with!  Stickers are good quality and mechanically it never pops (at least for me). 

 Having solved many twisty puzzles, I was surprised at the difficulty.  Perhaps because of the deceptively small number of colors and facets? 

 Great fun for intermediate players, especially considering the low price!!  Also nice collectible due to unique shape.  I think it would be too hard for beginners, but what do I know? 

 My only complaint is it will often "mildly" jam when twisting.  A small re-alignment or moderate brute-force will get you through the jams.  I never had any pieces pop.  I would give it 5 stars except for that jamming. 

 Heck, for the price I should probably give it 5 stars anyway... 

 Oh well, if you like twisty puzzles, this is a good one!

Other than the hard catching it is a great and very delightful Cube,, I never had it offer to pop and would say all about the cube is well made except the catching of the center turning and would recommend this for all to learn it and enjoy it!!! May never be a favorite cube but glad I got one!!!!

I'll give it two stars, rather than one, because the puzzle it could have been seems interesting. If they remade one at a decent quality I'd buy it in a heartbeat, because it seems like it's at that perfect sweet spot of difficulty where you could figure it out yourself, but not right away. 

 Alas. 

 The turning quality is hoooorrrible. I feel like I'm going to shatter the plastic just doing basic moves -- not a pop, but an internal break. I can feel the strain on the parts. And the little wheel thing in the middle needs to pick a lane. If it's supposed to spin freely, it needs to be much easier to spin; if it's supposed to be locked to one of the layers, it needs to be better locked. As it is I can't figure out which way it's supposed to be, only that it gets frequently misaligned and it's very annoying to fix. 

 I tried adding some lube but didn't get much benefit. Maybe somebody else could mod this into usability, but if so, why didn't it come that way from the factory? 

 Alas. I see it's out of stock. Hopefully that's a sign that they're going to fix it up and make a better version -- I'd welcome that and buy a new copy.

review_title: Great Economy 6x6, Just Shy of Pro Performance
review_text:
I bought the Diansheng 6x6M pretty much immediately after it was announced, hoping to find something to replace my Yuxin Little Magic 6x6M, which has been my main for approximately 10 months.  

 Out of the Box, this cube has the lightest turning of any 6x6 on the market. Absolutely astounding that the cube can turn with so little resistance on all layers while being one of the highest order WCA Puzzles.  

 This works perfectly while solving centers, which comprises the bulk of your solving time, and I throughly enjoy that leg of all of my solves. 

 However, this in conjunction with its medium-weak magnets, makes the cube lockup with annoying consistency during LL of the 3x3 stage - which is the exact reason I wanted it to replace my Little Magic. There’s been numerous times I’ve almost broken the 3-minute barrier on this cube, and every single time without fail a last layer lockup would dash my hopes and land me somewhere in the 3:01-3:09 range, depending on the severity of the lockup. 

 Outside of that, other small annoyances are: 

 A) The cube’s green side is unexpectedly dark, which leads to lower contrast and poor recognition in sub-par lighting conditions, and 

 B) The frosted plastic (that’s becoming the industry standard for some unknown reason) has shown no signs of smoothing to a glossy finish like GAN puzzles or the RS3M 2020. For reference, I’ve solved it 10-15 times per day since it arrived about a week ago.  

 If this is your first 6x6, or even your first magnetic 6x6, I have no doubt you’ll be pleased with this $20 purchase. If you’re more experienced in the event (around the sub-2:40 range or so) - this cube is a novelty at best and a hinderance at worst. 

 In any circumstance, you’re most likely better off shelling out the extra $5 or so for the MGC, which I’m also likely to do within the next few weeks.

review_title: The first Gan 3x3 I actually enjoy using
review_text:
This cube, unlike the Gan 14, actually manages to stay together and even on factory settings pops are rare to come by (at least for me). This cube is extremely light, airy, and fast. For me, the default magnets that came with the cube were perfect, though it comes with weaker magnets and stronger magnets if you prefer them. If you want a cube that comes as close as possible to turning literal air, then this might be the perfect cube for you, if you are willing to spend the money. I tend to have a more aggressive turning style, and this cube is best used for people who turn fast, but also light and accurately. My turning style is aggressive, fast, and not always super accurate. The cube is still usable despite this, but you may experience weird catches or lock-ups if you are an aggressive turner. It's not going to replace my main, but I'll still use the cube often or if I want to use something light.  

 I'd say my biggest pet peeve with the cube is having to use the tool to remove the center-caps. It's not a big deal for me, but it can be annoying if you adjust your cube tensions often.

 I will be keeping the cube and like going back to the setting that felt good until the 16 comes out this month, and then I'll retire this one. review_title: Setting up is a chore, but good once its done
review_text:
I haven't owned any Gan cubes before this.  It has all been Moyu and YJ for the most part.  But I invested in this to see what all the hype was about. 

 The immediate first thing noticed was how light it is.  Way lighter than most of my other cubes, yet it's sturdy.  It does have a cheap feeling to it, IMHO.  The Maglev is truly a different animal.  There are no springs, just all magnetic interaction.  Once set up, it was surprisingly controllable for something so fast. 

 The bad part to me was the way the adjustments are made.  It's temperamental at best, and too delicate.  The middle tension and travel adjustments aren't well documented, and the numbers are incredibly hard to read without some kind of magnification.  And the corner piece magnets are very delicate - especially the green ones.  Almost immediately, one of the magnets got stuck in the tool where I needed pliers to get it out.  And then with very little effort, the claw end of a green magnet broke off in a corner and I spent about 20 minutes taking it apart and digging it out.   

 Overall, it's a nice cube.  But the adjustment options really need some work, IMHO.  They need to be made more durable and easier to see what you're doing.  It's certainly not up to the level of quality I expected from the price.

 However, this cube marks a good direction for GAN, and i hope GAN 17 will be even better (as of Feb 2026).

I would suggest adjusting the spring compression to about 4 or 5 to slow it down at bit. I have my magnets on 3 for a more snappy and controllable feel.  If you don't have any lube I would suggest buying some because the tensions do not slow down the cube that much. I personally put about 5 drops of SILK and 2 drops of DNM-37. Now the cube feels closer to my X-Man Tornado V2. With lube this cube is very controllable. Corner cutting and reverse corner cutting are amazing. The cube is flexible and does not catch often. The purple internals are a great cosmetic desgin and do not affect your color nuetrality at all. As expected with a maglev cube there is no spring noise. The cube is still a bit loud so maybe not ideal if your cubing in a place with lots ofc people. The only thing I would change with the cube would be to have moyu start implementing a new spring adjustment system because the current system is very hard and confusing for new cubers. If you don't plan on actually setting up this cube then expect a very fast, loose, and uncontrollable cube. Otherwise it's a 5/5 cube. Another great release from moyu.

review_title: Excellent vs. X-Man Design Spark 7x7 M
review_text:
I bought this cube to use over my X-Man Design Spark 7x7 M. I’ve been very happy with its 6x6 cousin (AoShi 6x6 WR M), so I was hoping for something similar in a 7x7, and so far, I am not disappointed. The X-Man, which is overall a great cube, would occasionally lock-up and/or pop pieces. I got to the point where I could solve the X-Man carefully enough that this was relatively rare, but still, I’ve always been a little timid while solving it, and therefore hesitant to go as fast as I can. I've never had these problems with the AoShi 6x6 having now logged approximately 1400 solves on it. Although I’ve only solved my new AoFu 7x7 eight times since receiving it the other day, it appears to be living up to my expectations. 

 I often time my scrambles as a measure of raw turning speed, and the AoFu appears to be coming in on the low end (i.e., faster scrambles) of what I achieved with the X-Man, and I’m not even completely adjusted to the AoFu yet, so I’m expecting my average solve time to come down a bit too, say by maybe 10-15%. (I keep a running 100 solve average, so it will take me a while to know for sure, but so far, these 8 solves are at least as good as some of the best sets of 8 consecutive solves I’ve had on the X-Man). 

 The smaller size of the AoFu is also appealing to me. The inner layers are a bit narrow, but in the end it’s worth having a slightly smaller 7x7, especially to narrow the spread in size in going from 3x3 on up to 7x7. The only issue I’ve had with the AoFu 7x7 is that an orange cap has come off a couple times. Both times it was on an inner 3x3 corner piece. I’m not sure it was the same one both times, but given that it was orange both times, it may have been. I also don’t know if this is just a piece that is slightly out of spec or if the problem will become more frequent? Nonetheless, it is a small nuisance compared to the issues I had with the X-Man, sometimes even sliding an entire piece onto another face.

I would suggest adding plastic washers under the screws to alleviate this, lubing the core, adding weak core magnets, and stacking extra magnets in the second layers, then doing a fast setup with tight tensions. product_name: MoYu RS3 M V5 3x3 (PiCube Matte Special Edition)
review_title: Picube's interpretation of the RS3M V5 delivers a fresh reimagining of one of the best 3x3s availabl
review_text:
Review is for the matte version 

 Setup:
 Screw(center travel): 180⁰ looser (half-turn counterclockwise)
 Spring compression: (0 is most loose setting, as well as the stock setting) 1 

 Lube(applied in order listed to 1 edge piece at a time between break-in solves) About 200 solves were done over the course of 2 days for break-in
 Track: Angstrom Gravitas
 Track: Angstrom Dignitas
 Piece: Angstrom Dignitas
 Track: 2 drops Mystic
 Piece: 2 drops Mystic
 Piece: Fz-Stealth for additional speed until A-Perms felt good and aligned with my natural turning speed.
 No lube was applied to the core, and I have experienced 0 spring noise after 11 days of ownership. YMMV 

 Review:
 Cube arrived safely with the box in great condition, with all expected MoYu RS3M V5 accessories, and no blank center cap (comes in clear 2-piece MoYu storage box, and no robot). 

 Out of the box, the turning was slightly fast, sandy, and blocky-feeling during algorithms. I found it to feel too tight at stock screw tension, so I loosened the screws by 45⁰ (¼ turn). The magnetic snap upon alignment is noticeably stronger compared to my standard RS3M V5 ball core.  

 I thought it did not turn well initially, as the small corner-cuts felt too forced while I was mid-algorithm. I enjoyed its tactility however, and wanted to set it up. I wanted to give my Yoo lube bundle II a try, and decided to try it on this cube, as I was not immediately warm and receptive toward it. I already had prior experience with doing my own Angstrom(Gravitas/Dignitas/DNM-37) setups in the past, and thought it would transform my opinion on this cube, as it has in the past with other cubes I felt lukewarm toward.  

 Thankfully the setup (and most likely, the break-in) transformed this cube into a main-worthy contender for me. I further loosened the yellow side as it did not do the big >45⁰ forward cuts(I don't do these cuts in solves, but it is a great test to set screw tensions in a uniform way across multiple cubes). Since this set the yellow side much looser than the white side when doing the double opposite edge pull test, I further loosened the rest of the sides to match the adjustment I did to the yellow side. The big corner cuts are able to be done, both forward and reverse, and I have experienced 0 pops so far. 

 The magnetic alignment feels nicely locked in at this point; A-perms and other RUD 3-gen algorithms (Ra Perm R U' R' U' R U R D... most 😡 alg ever)tend to be my weakest algorithms, and the relative strength allows the cube to stay together in these instances, and I feel very confident with this cube, surprisingly. It gives a nice tactile snap during fidgety turning/hand scrambling, and the laggy overcorrection snapback sensation that happens when the magnets correct an overturn does not appear to be a problem at all. I'd say the new magnetic sensation is an upgrade compared to the default RS3M V5 ballcore.  

 Having said that, I don't consider this a better puzzle than the default RS3M V5, as the default version is still a world-class puzzle. In an objective review, I'd consider this adjacent in quality to the default RS3M V5. 

 M-slices: 
 I only have CFOP H and Z perm to go off of, but the m slice does not snapback, nor does it feel like I need to overexert to move it.  

 Matte plastic: 
 I enjoy both worn down smooth matte plastic and UV(oops MoYu cube, I mean Magic Clothes). I'm about 700 - 1000 solves in, and it still feels like there's more breaking in to do. It started feeling good just when I started warming up to it after setting it up, and it is not a problem at all. 

 Features: 
 The tried-and-true classic 9-click MoYu dual-adjustment from 2019 is still a 5/5⭐️ system. Magnet strength stopped feeling bad after slowing the cube down, and I don't feel that adjustable magnets would make the cube better, especially not at the risk of increasing the price of this line of cubes. Primary internals do make this feel different than the regular V5, but I attribute the slight softness to the lube I used, and not the plastic in the puzzle. 

 What do I dislike?: 
 The RS3M V5 is notorious at this point in its life for having very fragile corners, and it becomes apparent when you drop it. I feel slight anxiety when taking this cube with me on the go, as I'm scared of dropping it, but highly enjoy the turning sensation and love to have it alongside me. Thankfully I haven't dropped it yet, but I only need to drop it once to feel the heartbreak (RIP my first V5). 

 It's pretty loud and clacky at full speed, something to note for cubers living with parents, significant others, or infants. 

 I do NOT need another pamphlet of the stackable cube box that MoYu no longer includes with their puzzles since the WRM 2021.. 

 So, who can benefit from buying this?:
 Cubers who are somewhat dissatisfied with their [possibly broken corner piece /s] RS3M V5, and may want something similar. 

 Cubers with prior knowledge of cube setup. 

 Anyone that may want ...

review_title: Flagship level performance and feeling for budget value!
review_text:
This is a wonderful cube which feels very nice to turn and use. The piece to piece contact is very nice, and feels soft and buttery smooth in between and start and end of each turn. The part between each turn gives tactility and crispiness to the overall experience, leading to turns which are smooth but very distinct. You get softness, but not a too-smooth feeling.  

 I set this cube up with dignitas and gravitas. Prior to adding lube to the pieces, I added gravitas to the plastic core for a longer lasting puzzle and light silicone to the springs for smoothness, and set the cube at tension 1, compression 1 because it felt somewhat flexible and not that losse. The cube feels very blocky out of the box, and has some lockups. But the feeling is very light, and if you turn light, the cube is not as blocky. But when I added gravitas, the break in process was very fast. The cube began to feel less stiff, unbelievably flimsy and loose, and pretty uncontrollable. Gravitas made sticky lock-ups happen, too. I changed the setup to 3,3 for the moment  Dignitas made the cube feel less clacky. I changed the tension and elasticity in combinations that had each reaching up to four clicks for about a week. After many combos, I found that Tension 1, Compression 3 worked best for fluidity with  minimal lockups, but stability capable of holding the cube together. 

 People wonder why the magnet strength is stronger on the non-ball core versions. I have probably figured it out. Considering how the 8-magnet ball core and especially 20-magnet ball core versions are pretty flimsy out of the box with added stability and just a little bit weaker of magnet, I think the standard version needed extra support to be usable. But Moyu's justification for weaker ball core versions magnets is consistency and freedom to turn. I can see this, the 8 and 20 magnet ball core versions have more distributed magnet strength and have control, but fluidity compared to the standard version, which has enhanced blockiness. 

 One issue, as I have stated, is the holding back of options. The v11 needs somewhat precise, but very light turning. This version has stability issues and may still be flimsier and lockier than the MAGLEV version on some settings. I have to tighten the cube to make it stable, then loosen It for flexibility. I could find almost no options that gave flexibility and space to turn, but not much flimsiness. If you don't care about fluidity and are advanced enough for a light and accurate turning style to be present, you can probably live with Tension 2, Compression 4 or Tension 4,Compression 2 or some other combination. 3,3 is generally optimal for people that don't really turn fast enough for lockups or want stability or tighter turning. But Tension 1, Compression 3 is my favorite, but not most recommended setup.  

 I find the lock-ups making this cube not as beginner-friendly, but more premium and high-performance, compared to the v10 and v9. Also, I think that the v9 is better than the V10 because the V10 is like the v11, but more catchy, irresponsive, and cheap in plastic quality, and less fluid. The v9, however is flexible but still stable. A little bit older and more gummy in plastic, if I do say so myself. But still flexible.  

 So yeah, if you want more space to turn, get the ball core versions. But note that edges are not hooked in as well and can turn a bit, and also shake.

review_title: The question is... why? Overpriced, fragile, pointless, and overpriced.
review_text:
The Redi Cube, while having much potential to become a WCA event, is still quite niche and rather unpopular among the cubing community. No one really talks about it these days. So whyever Moyu would go out and make one that has a freaking BALL-CORE is just wild to me. Oh, and it also has a pretty advanced adjustment system inside. 

 Anyway, the way the cube is cut makes finger tricking tricky, so you can't really go that fast. So why bother going for one that's THIS expensive when other models at half the price or even less will suffice? Besides, this doesn't even FEEL expensive. It's *very* light and hollow-sounding. It's one of the cheapest feeling cubes in my collection of non-WCAs. The Yuxin 8-petals cube is still magnetic and WAY cheaper. It's the same cube, just with curvy cuts. That'll probably be enough for you, so I'd go for that one instead. 

 Oh, one last thing. I got it on sale for just under half the price listed here. That's a little more reasonable. I would NOT recommend buying this cube for 33$. 

 Edit: Don't twist two corners opposite each other on a side, whether by accident or intentionally. If that happens, an edge WILL pop off from its leaf-shaped internal piece and will literally be near impossible to replace because of the hollow structure of the cube. Trust me, this is a real issue due to how slippery the cube is to handle. This has already happened twice now, and this time I'm not even gonna bother fixing it. Changed from 3* to 2*. 

 Hey, and if you really want a premium-feeling corner turning cube, I'd wholeheartedly recommend the Super Ivy Cube. It feels at least 3x more premium than this. It is weighty, it turns like a real speedcube, it's 10x more fun, and is half the price. But just don't waste your money on this.

review_title: Best For Its Type, but Overpriced
review_text: I applied a thin, fast silicone lube, but that made it slow down somehow. Finger flicks were more effortless and satisfying before lubing. I recommend using Lubest XMT 10; it worked much better than the other lube. I put it on the largest travel distance and lightest spring compression, and I've had no popping issues. I find it can be pretty catchy, though. I'm not sure how different the dual-adjustment settings are, but I think I have fewer catches/lock ups on the smallest travel distance (6) and tightest spring compression (9). It is a little difficult to finger trick sledge hammers, but I think it's the easiest on this cube compared to other corner-turning puzzles (e.g., the Dino cube and the YuXin 8 Petals). Lining the corner caps to put them back on is a little difficult. review_title: Genuinely the best cube I’ve had the pleasure of using.
review_text:
My last cube was the limited Peacock Gan 12, but my toddler smashed it while I was working… imagine magnets and pieces scattered around the house. 

 This cube, compared to the Gan12 is more stable and less fast (still very fast, but more usable). I’m not experiencing any catching, or weird flexing issues. 

 Out of the box: Incredibly smooth. The magnets make it feel tactile, but they’re not controlling. It reminds me of a high quality tactile switch on a keyboard. I could have kept it un-lubed and been perfectly satisfied. 

 After I lubed it with Gravitas, Dignitas, and DNM (I know, I’m basic) it made the cube sound so beautiful and correct. Honestly, any lube preference would make this cube shine. Lube made it feel correct.  

 Genuinely annoyed by the clunky 2-piece Cube box… but lucky for me, I have a clear Peacock Green Gan 12 box that I can use! 

 10/10, I would get it again if I wasn’t weird about choosing a different cube every time.

However, if you have a rougher, more inaccurate turning style, you’re gonna lock up and not have an incredible time. I use this cube over a wrm v9, and I think it’s an upgrade for me. review_text:
I average 22 seconds so this will be the bias of the review 

 This cube is one of the best (if not the best) speedcube in it's price. when I first saw the cube on the cubicle I was a little worried that the performance wouldn't be all that good because it's only $26.99 and It doesn't have any flagship features other than UV, But when I used the cube for the first time, I was blown away by It's amazing performance, but there are some cons that come with the good features. 

 Pros
 1. the cube is very fast yet controllable.
 2. the corner cutting is amazing. 

 cons
 1. center pieces fall off every now and then when you loosen the screws to much. 
 2. this cube is more prone to corner twists than most modern cubes.
 3. it is very loud when you turn it. 

 so... since the cube is fast it makes it easy to turn and have good corner cutting, on top of the fact that it's controllable, but the center caps fall off easier when the screws are loosened more because the center caps are shaped like circles it it corner twists a little more than the average speedcube, as well as it is pretty loud. So, if you don't mind the cons and the pros sound good to you, you should get the cube. (this cube is my main, and although I am only averaging 22 seconds,I don't think the cube's performance would hold anyone back from reaching sub-15 or even sub-10) I hope you found this review helpful.

review_title: Amazing cube, would recommend over 8 magnet ball core/special edition.
review_text: This cube has the speed of the original 8 magnet version and the smooth and controllable feel of the special edition, with a few extra bonuses. My main issue with the 8 magnet ballcore is the corner-core magnets are way too strong and aggressive, and the turning feels robotic. The special edition is good and was my main for a good while, but the lack of maglev/edge repelling magnets means that it does lack in speed that is seen with other flagships. The 20 magnet version has the best of both worlds: the speed of the original and the stability and control of the special edition makes this a very good cube to main. The 20 magnets in the core really helps to stabilize the cube when turning at max TPS. It does require setup though, straight from the box the cube is very uncontrollable, but with the proper lube combinations, compressions, and tensions, this cube will not disappoint. The only real issue I have with it is that, like all variants of this cube, it is very "squishy" and deforms a lot if you aren't good with your turning. Surprisingly, I hardly every corner twist on this cube, but I am also on rather tight tension settings, so maybe that is why. Additionally, it is on the rather expensive side, and compared to other cubes like TV3 Pioneer it does lack in some crucial features like adjustable magnets, but overall I would highly recommend this cube if you can afford it, and enjoy fast, effortless turning.

review_title: Simple once you figure it out
review_text:
The puzzle can turn quite rough depending on how you hold it, which is the only real drawback. 

 As far as the actual puzzle itself, this is basically like a Dino Cube except it's a pyramid, and I happen to have a Dino Cube so I was able to sort of make the connection. The instructions in the book were a bit difficult to follow, mostly because the instruction manual labels the corners as if you had a corner facing you instead of a face. I eventually figured out a different and honestly much simpler way to solve the puzzle: Solve any one face first, then put that face on the bottom. Then turn the top corner so you have 2 edge pieces that need to be flipped. After that you hold the puzzle so the face with three different colors is facing you, then do a left hand algorithm (L R' L' R) and you'll be one turn away from solved.

It’s not too big at 120 mm (4 3/4” for the people who don’t understand mm). It is somewhat pillowed, so setting it on the table to align the layers isn’t possible. Would I buy it again? Absolutely I would, it’s a great puzzle from a company that’s been around for years. Would I recommend it for people who are just starting out and have a small collection? Absolutely not, this definitely is not a beginner puzzle, but 10/10, if you’re up for the mental challenge and can pay the $320 cost, go for it

This is a good cube. Everyone says it is small, but I was still surprised by how compact it is. At the narrowest part, the edge length is similar to that of a Pyraminx, and it is around 10 millimeters larger at the center. It is fairly heavy, at 1,080 grams, or about 12 times the weight of a GTS3 M. The size improves solving comfort, but it is still fatiguing due to the weight. Turning is okay, but not great. It is fairly stiff, but it gets better with use. The main issue regarding turning is that the puzzle is quite rigid, so the layers need to be aligned before other turns can be made. This combined with the pillowed shape means that some lockups are to be expected. I have gotten two pops so far, but both were due to inaccurate turning and could have been avoided. Solving this puzzle is enjoyable, but also repetitive. It is not something most people will solve often. This cube is extremely well-built. I have no concerns about durability, but the stickers chip easily, so I do recommend the stickerless version. There are slight blemishes on some edge pieces, but nothing very noticeable. There are also unsightly seams on the innermost edge pieces, but the stickerless version avoids this due to the adjusted mold. Overall, this is a good puzzle, but it does have some issues. I do recommend it, but only to people who enjoy very long solves. I would suggest that most people opt for the YuXin HuangLong 11x11. It is much cheaper, turns better, and is much less tedious to solve.

product_name: MoYu WeiLong V11 3x3 (8-Magnet Ball-Core + Spring + Edge-Repulsion + UV PiCube SE)
review_text:
I don't usually do reviews, but this cube needs to be talked about. Normally sacrifices have to be made for a good balance on a 3x3, but this cube has all of the qualities you would want in a 3x3 without compromise. I'm normally not a fan of modern 3x3s, but I've still used a lot of them so I have a lot of comparisons to make: 

 Feel: The simplest way I can describe this cube is if you took a Tornado V3 Flagship, removed the blockyness of it, and made it lightweight and airy like a Gan cube. It even sounds super similar to how the Tornado V3 sounds, so if you like quiet cubes, this won't disappoint. My complaint with a lot of cubes such as the Tornado V3 is the blocky rigid feel. Thankfully, MoYu cubes are notorious for their gentle corner cuts that aren't snappy. This cube definitely continues that trend, which is a breath of fresh air in the current cube market.  

 I average 9.9s-10.2s, and for the first time in my life it feels like I don't have to adapt my turning to a cube. I just pick it up and everything flows. I got an 8.69 PB avg as soon as I got this cube.  

 OOTB vs Setup: I'm normally one to put great care into cube setup, but I genuinely do not know where to start with this cube because it is perfect out of the box. Side note - if you like ridiculously loose settings, you'll be pleased to know this cube actually handles those wonderfully. My previous two mains could not (Gan 13 and Picube RS3M V5) as the internals would often become slightly dislodged if I turned inaccurately. I tried this thing on the loosest and softest settings and it was great, though I eventually gravitated back to the factory settings of 3 and 3 because it felt like the best and most reliable balance. If you don't like setting up cubes, just use it the way it comes and you'll be fine.  

 Closing thoughts on performance: The magnet strength feels quite strong, but surprisingly not in a bad way. Somehow it doesn't feel like it impedes my turns on this cube like it would on others. Corner twists have been fairly rare for me on this cube. The corner cutting is what you'd expect in a modern 3x3. I'm not a great OH solver but I have come to prefer this cube for OH as well because of how light and reliable it is, though it is slightly fast for OH unless you turn lightly. If you've done OH with modern cubes, you know how hard it can be to control the overshooting typically. Overall, Picube struck a great balance of mag strength, forgiveness, and reliability.  

 Versions: I would caution anyone considering the maglev version, as the spring version with edge repulsion is already quite fast naturally, and since this cube doesn't have screws it's incredibly easy to core lube without worrying about tensions being lost during reassembly.  

 10/10 cube
 Btw, the internals are beautiful.

review_title: So frustrating... 5*+ puzzle idea, 2* mechanical implementation
review_text:
In terms of raw puzzle design, I think this is the most fun, challenging shape mod. If it was as good mechanically as the idea, it would be a very easy 5* from me.  

 It's deceptively challenging. One thing people may not realize, and I sure didn't at first, is that you can do 1/4 turns, so it makes some very striking shapeshifts. That's when things get interesting. You can have different pieces in different orientations, so you can't tell where the original pyramid edges are supposed to go, because a bunch of adjacent "edges" (which are actually the center pieces, from the perspective of the internal mechanism) are rotated 90 degrees and seem to indicate "faces" pointing in directions that the correct solution doesn't actually have. 

 The problem is how often I mess up a solve because to say this thing doesn't corner cut at all isn't putting it strongly enough. It catches all the time, you have to spin it and twist it back and forth to try and free up whatever is caught, and by the time that's done, good luck remembering where you were in a series of moves or even what face you were trying to turn. The mental gymnastics necessary to keep seeing the 3x3-ness of this weird mod require focus, if you have to interrupt yourself to hunt for what's catching, you're going to lose where you were at.  

 So it's complex, and you really want to be able to focus and not get tripped up. It's a very fun mod when you can just do that.  

 I hate to be so critical—it's an ingenious puzzle, well worth owning, and it might even be my favorite 3x3 mod bar none, when the catching doesn't trip me up, which isn't even all *that* often... but just often enough to frustrate me. So, minus two stars for that. I'd pay decent money for a slightly better-made one with the pieces a bit more rounded or some other mechanism to allow you to turn without locking when the layers are only in 99.9998% perfect alignment.

From a design standpoint, if you're interested in 3x3x3 shape mods, this is a good one to start with.  You have to learn to solve corners and the red/blue/green/orange edges with one fewer colors for reference (so you need to learn the basic color order on the cube), and the red/blue/green/orange centers also have orientation (so you need to develop/learn an algorithm/rule to rotate them, both in increments of 180 and 90 degrees).  You also have to handle the skewed nature of the cube and not let it disrupt your usual 3x3x3 algorithms.  These are surmountable challenges, even for someone new to 3x3x3 shape mods (or shape mods in general)!  On top of getting a puzzle that pushes you to grow a little, you get a puzzle with a fun checkerboard pattern (looks like a pinwheel). 

 There are some downsides: the cube will be a little tight at first, but it will loosen up tremendously with use and lube.  The cube will also catch and may also send you into some unwanted turns that make you lose your place in the solve.  Finally, on my cube, a counterclockwise turn of the yellow layer gives a metal (spring?) sound.  It's not enough to ding a $6 puzzle a full star.  With a little patience, you can manage these issues, and while I wouldn't argue that suffering through managing construction problems is a good thing, it does help prepare you for 3x3x3 shape mods that (regrettably) have bigger problems. 

 In all, it's a loveable cube.  It construction might break your heart a bit at first, but it's a good puzzle to learn after nailing down a 3x3x3, and it will make other (harder) shape mods more accessible for you.

review_title: WHEN QIYI UPGRADED THEIR FLAGSHIP 5X5 TO A WHOLE NEW LEVEL...
review_text: Before I get into the good stuff and downsides about the cube, I want to point out that my version of the Valk5 is a Pro Shop version, which is professionally set up by staffs from the Cubicle office. The Valk5 is a 62mm 5x5 that costs 50 US dollars (stock version) and comes in Black, White, and Stickerless plastic. The size of this cube is the same as the WuShuang 5x5, a former flagship 5x5 from QiYi. When I unboxed this cube, this cube is slow and very loose out of the box. With some tensioning, breaking in, and minor lubing, this cube is surely the best 5x5 on the market. I said that because after I did the basic maintenance of the cube, it has a buttery smooth turning with a crispy and stable feel that I personally enjoy. Outer layers are phenomenal and inner layers are a little sluggish to my liking, but that does not allow me to despise this cube. The stability is very nice. The mechanism is mostly derived from the WuShuang, but with minor adjustments to the anti-pop spots to make the cube more flexible while remaining stable. In comparison with the Aochuang GTS, which is inconsistent and flimsy and the Wushuang, which is blocky and slow, the Valk 5 really fixes those problems. If you are serious about 5x5, this cube will surely fit your likings. After breaking multiple PBs, I am confident to reccomend this puzzle.

review_text:
I heard about the hanoiminx, which has been discontinued (and was very expensive). But now shengshou has made a Legally Distinct Product with a new name and a better price point and now I've got one. 

 It's a neat solve, first of all. The solutions guide describes a LBL algorithm which is very intuitive until the very last bit, and which is pleasant to figure out on your own. The algorithms required on top are not too bad, either, although I have yet to memorize the permute-corners equivalent. 

 The only dig I'd put in against this thing is the motion. It doesn't pop (good!) or lock up (mostly), but it's just really stiff. I haven't found a screw to mess with, either; and if there was, I'd be worried about pops, although I'd still try it. 

 Still, it's a good cube at a good price, so I'd recommend it. But I wish the motion was nicer.

review_title: Pretty Easy, But Still Pretty Fun
review_text:
When I first got this puzzle, I didn't know what to expect. All I knew was it was basically a Master Pyraminx Duo.  But even then, I wasn't sure of how much more difficult it was compared to the regular Pyraminx Duo (which is notoriously easy). But after playing with it for a bit, I realized its just a pyraminx with centers and without tips. And after realizing that the centers can be easily swapped with some sledgehammers, I solved the puzzle with minimal difficulty. The only slightly hard thing was getting used to recognizing the pieces when solving the pyraminx edges. And once they're solved, there's a possibility of the centers being out of place. But like I said earlier, they can be easily swapped with a few sledgehammers. Overall, the solve isn't too difficult, but it's still pretty enjoyable. This thing also turns pretty good all things considered. It's smooth, but also a little clicky due to the ball bearings. The only problems with the turning is when you try to speedsolve the puzzle. It locks up a lot when speedsolving. And me at least, this thing begs to be speedsolved. It is just a pyraminx with a potential extra step and no tips after all, and it still turns pretty good. But I also don't devalue the puzzle because of it's problems when speedsolving, since it wasn't meant to be speedsolved. 

 Overall, I really enjoy this puzzle. The quality is great. The solve is pretty short, making for a good cube to pick up, do a few solves, and put back down. And it just looks great in a collection due to it's unique look. I highly recommend this puzzle. QiYi did a great job with this one. 

 (Also, fun fact: After looking at this puzzle closer, I realized that it's just a weirdly-shaped Jing's Pyraminx. And as someone who always wanted to get one, it was really cool to know I finally got one after all this time, & didn't even realize it.)

review_title: Great little cube - a real pocket cube!
review_text:
This is a nice little cube and good for practising CLL and/or corners-first methods in places you can't take larger cubes.  It's about 34mm at it's widest point. 

 You won't set any speed records on this, despite Mats Valk photo on the box and Qiyi calling this a speed cube.  Finger tricks will be very hard as well due to the pillowed nature and the side.  In my hands, I get a sensation that the cube will slip out. 

 It came pre-lubed, and spins very well.  I've been through 50+ solves and it's gotten a little more flexible.  It's pretty quiet.  Corner cutting is very limited to just a few millimeters in either direction.  That's OK, as one might have trouble getting more than 1-3 tps anyway. 

 The clasp is interesting.  It's not a key chain by itself, but can be attached to a key chain or backpack zipper or something else.  The larger clasp could hold a 2-3 keys, but not much more.  The other end of the chain is a smaller clasp such that you can detach from the cube to make solves easier, leaving a little nub on the white/blue/orange corner.  Detaching the chain is easiest removed when the clasp is flat against the cube.  Doing any other position might cause some plastic loop wear and increase breakage. 

 Where can you ideally use this cube?  Thought of a couple places...
 - backpacking trip where space and weight is crucial
 - the men's lounge area of women's fitting rooms
 - any line you are standing in
 - subway or bus 

 It's a real pocket cube that turns pretty smoothly.

review_text:
Was way over-lubed out of the box, and there was a lot of spring noise and clicking during slice turns. the clicking was just the plastic nut in the core shifting side to side during turns. I flipped the core spring, and most of the noise went away. 
 There are magnets in the slice with a subtle feel, which is nice.  After cleaning and lubing it with weight2 it turns pretty smooth. I added 4 more magnets to the middle layer to strengthen the slice alignment. Now it's perfect.  

 Fun challenge. Turns and solves like a regular square 1, but by shape instead of color. Algorithms are little tricky since nothing is shaped the same, and recognition is hard. Nice addition to a collection for a sqaure 1 or mirror cube fan.

review_title: Cube performs great, app is meh, corner magnet loose on arrival
review_text:
I'll preface this with saying this is my first new cube since the Weilong GTS2M back when it came out. 

 I tend to not be big into lubing my cubes, so the out of the box feeling is really important to me, and it definitely surpassed my expectations. I was expecting something that didn't turn on par with flagship cubes (and I can't really compare it to modern flagships), but I think I like it better than the GTS2M. Its a little too fast for me so I'll probably have to slow it down. If I just picked it up and started turning there's no way I'd guess it was a smart cube.
 I also do really like the look of the cube with its UV coating and am glad I got this over frosted. 
 One unfortunate thing was that my cube arrived with a loose corner magnet which made the cube super noisy. I had to take apart the corner and glue it in to keep it in place, and now the cube is pretty quiet compared to my other 3x3s. 

 Now for the app, since if you just want a 'dumb' cube, there are far better and cheaper options. After taking a while to first connect to the app, it now connects really quick, and rarely disconnects for more than a second or so. The online multiplayer features are essentially dead and really buggy, so don't expect to be using that, although the one time I did find a lobby it was pretty fun for a bit. 

 The algorithms training is useful, although I could see myself pulling up a tutorial on youtube on the side as well to learn the finger tricks, since the app doesn't show that. 

 As for the timer, its ok. It does function fine for starting and stopping the timer, and its relatively accurate on the breakdown of steps, although there are mistakes with the breakdown of inspection vs execution time for each step. 
 **** The really really annoying feature is that it is just completely wrong in its calculation of my PB averages. The graph of averages of 5, 12, and 100 over time are correct, but then the table with my PBs is just completely wrong, and not by a small amount. It says my PB average of 5 is 16s but I can clearly see on the graph the lowest it gets is 21s. Its a massive issue in my opinion, but surprisingly I haven't seen any mentions of this issue online. It just means that in order to read off your averages, you need to look at the graph and estimate the minimum, which is pretty dumb.

Overall, it's a nice cube, The UV Coating is much better than the frosted finish, 
  it connects consistently and rarely causes an issue. The app is great and has many options and will help you improve. However, it is very clacky, and since there are no tension or magnet strength adjustments, even with lube you can't change it to be smoother.

I know it’s too expensive. But I don’t care. I wanted max purple internals, and the BC version had a different texture, whereas this one is textured and smooth, like the Meilong 3M. I love that cube, and this one is like a mix between that and the Weilong V9.  

 When setup properly, without a doubt this is the smoothest cube I’ve ever tried, and I’ve spent hundreds in the last few years on every flagship cube. The cap design allowed for maximum purple internals compared to other cubes with the split piece design, which I love. I’ve only had the caps come off once, when I dropped the cube by accident.  

 Conclusion: it may not be the best performing cube in the market today, but if it was released 5 years ago before the GAN 11 M Pro, it could have been considered one of the best in the world. product_name: MoYu Super RS3 M V2 MagLev UV 3x3
review_title: Looks good, but flimsy and more difficult to take apart and put together than others
review_text:
I like the purple internals, but other than that, I can't say I'm a fan of this cube, and I normally like MoYu. My RS3M v5 Ball Core and WeiLong v10 are much better.
 Even on the loosest tension, it's surprisingly difficult to take apart and put back together compared to most (maybe all) of my other cubes. That first/last edge piece is a bear. The piece caps also fall off easily (center, edge, corner... it doesn't matter), and that's virtually certain to happen during assembly/disassembly.
 Something else that's strange about this cube over my others: Even when applied sparingly, I've found that all but the thinnest lubes in the tracks give it a heavy, gummy feeling when aligning. (The RS3M v5 has this to an extent, too, but I don't think it's as bad.) It's less noticeable in mid-turn, but then the side lines up and suddenly there's a gummy resistance, like hitting a speed bump with mushy shock absorbers. It's weird.
 I had to clean out the cube a few times before I landed on a setup that works: Traxxas 50K for the core and Traxxas 200 cst for the tracks and sides. (In the tracks, I had also separately tried Angstrom Gravitas, Traxxas 900 cst, and FZ Glide -- each of which led to that alignment gumminess.)
 So, outside of the core, I would stick with thin lubes.

review_title: MoYu WeiLong V11 SE 3x3 (20-Magnet Ball-Core + MagLev + UV)
review_text:
I had the cube Premium Serviced with FZ. I ver y much like quick and fast cubes, and this cubes does it well. With it being serviced, the breaking in was phenomenal and smooth. I do have my cube on the looser settings, and even then I have not had it pop. I have only gotten corner twists when hand scrambling it, not in a solve or timed scramble. The cube corner cuts quite well and the magnets help the twisting from one alg to the next be very smooth and slick. I have my settings on 3,1. Even on tighter settings I had no issues with lock ups, corner twists or pops. As with any cube, the tighter it is, the more nudging you need to do on the corner cutting. That said, even on the tighter settings while solving i did not really run into this issue often, maybe 1 out of every 200, 300 solves. My turning is more on the accurate side with light finger tips and fast flicking.
 If possible I would recommend to get the cube serviced, the breaking in process is quite fun when you can start solving right out of  the box!

I have not lubed or tensioned yet, although compared to my old and unused Zanchi it is very light and airy, like a combination of FangShi speed but a Gans Air weight, which makes a combo that I really quite enjoy. This is a great puzzle for newer cubes and cuber son a budget, and I highly reccomend it to those people, while this with, say, a Gans Air master of The Valk/The Valk M might not find any reason to buy it. If you're already purchasing some cubes from The Cubicle it can't hurt to just tack this onto the order since it's only $4, you won't regret it!

 Corner cutting was decent. 45 with force for forward cutting and about 1/2 a piece reverse. I think the only problem is that the cube has a slight locking problem (this is probably due to my inaccurate turning).

Turning is great and solve is very fun! My one problem with it is that the inner Curvy Copter corners have colors on them as if they are actually visible, instead of them all just being one color. 

 This means that instead of being a Clover Cube + 2x2 hybrid, it is a Curvy Copter + 2x2 hybrid without overhang bandaging. Solving the inner corners isn’t hard if you know how to do it on Curvy Copter, but by doing a double-sledge like algorithm, you can swap them similarly to an A Perm (which you can’t do on CC because of the overhang bandaging).

review_title: Underrated and dual adjustment feature for cheap.
review_text:
I bought this cube from another online store, got it cheap and was blown away by it.
 Of course it appears cheap and feels cheap. But other than that, it's fantastic for it's price. it's cheaper than rs3m2020 and rs3mv5 and still has dual adjustment feature and surprise surprise, you can easily adjust it by hand without hurting your fingers (like moyu) or needing any tools. Feature and pricewise it's definitely better than rs3m line, but for it's turning it's somewhat slow and I find the magnets a bit on the stronger side. The springs are also considerably stiff, and for me 4 clicks are too slow and I prefer only 2 clicks. It's also very stable.
 As it came before the warrior m, I thought it's a successor to warrior s, but the piece design is different and more like rs3m with squared off center skirts and separate corner and edge feet. As I don't have qiyi m pros, but I think it's more of a budget version of m pro than a successor to warrior s.
 I maybe more careful with my cubes, but ever since getting it in late March or early April and till now after many solves it's going very good and there are no breakage or magnet dislodging issues like 2 other reviewers have mentioned.
 Overall, highly positive, different turning feel than every other cube especially moyu cubes.
 TL DR
 Good for it's price, has hand adjustable dual adjustment but with a different feel.

I would recommend to beginners or anyone looking for a good budget cube. This puzzle is not actually a mirror cube. If you do any kind of algorithm, the puzzle stays the exact same. The corners and edges on the top are all the same size, meaning that it is not actually solved like a square-1. While the puzzle does turn very well (much better than my 3D printed mirror sq-1), it is not an actual mirror cube. I’m disappointed. I’m rating 2 stars instead of 1 because the puzzle turns very well and is nice to fidget with, but regardless, this is not an actual mirror cube - it is simply a force-cube square-1 with a different thickness on the top and bottom layers, not actual size differences. I’ve attached a photo and a video that shows the puzzle doesn’t actually behave like a mirror cube.

As I have seen stated in other reviews, this is NOT actually a mirror sq1. The puzzle has cs and obl, but no pbl since the "colored" sides all have the same depth. In addition to this, the screw will get stuck to a point where turning it tightens/loosens the cube. If I could give this 0 stars, I would.

Really disappointed in this cube, for $33 I expected it to be at least as good as my $23 Swift Block Super Maglev, but it's not close. Scratchy & slow turning, even with the lube advice from support. Worse, some of the corner & edge pieces catch on each other whe they are aligned - the plastic faces are not all flush with the frames they snap into. Maybe mine is an anomaly.

### Setup Experience
 Was some lubricant inside when I got it.  Based on its slightly yellow color, odorlessness, and viscosity I believe it was a very thin layer of 10k differential oil.  I redid it with my own lube setup and broke it in over about 10 minutes with the default settings.  The forwards corner cut was about 55 degrees with minimal torque.  I turned the screws until the minimal torque forwards corner cut was down to just over 45 degrees, and changed the compression dials from 3/9 to 6/9.  Dial took a minute to understand but very usable.  Hand-adjustable without fingernails.  There's no adjustment options on the magnets except for the edge-repelling magnets which you can switch out for the traditional kind. 

 ### Visual Inspection
 On first pass, there is no visible defects on my cube specifically, including on the UV coating and the internal pieces.  The cubicle did not have an option available to purchase an extra no-logo center cap, but I have no idea if that's something the manufacturer controls or if the cubicle just sells those for high-demand cubes.  The centers have eight holes on them and I think it looks pretty cool and distinct, but its a little busy looking, especially on the white side with the logo.  Overall I'm glad its there, its a cool touch, but would work even better with a logoless cap. 

 ### Feel & Performance
 Overall turning is very stable and blocky.  The magnets are quite strong but not very inertial.  I don't find it difficult to start turns, even M slices and I'm really weak.  It gives tactile feedback and so its not hard to feel the difference if you do U2 flicks too close together for example, which was a problem I had with the tornado v3.  Its moderately loud, so you can also hear the difference for audio feedback.

Sometimes the "magic" bits pop out. It's a lot more common than I'd like. They're easy to put back in, though; I haven't seen a total collapse or anything, just a single piece that pops out. It's fairly annoying but it sticks right back in. 

 The puzzle itself is nice. I admit I got overwhelmed trying to solve it myself and checked the attached solution, and in hindsight I wish I hadn't; there is quite an elegant solution to the "magic" bits on there, and I probably could have found it if I had been more patient. 

 Either way; it's a nice little puzzle, so long as you're patient with the pops, and it's not a long solve once you learn the steps.

review_title: A good even layered big cube, but far from perfect
review_text:
The 14x14 cube had VCube 6 style misalignments. That problem seemed to be fixed with the 16x16. However, this cube is nowhere near perfect. The first solve or so requires shimmying the layers when making wide inner layer turns, due to out of the box stiffness and lockups.  

 Also, extra care is required when making turns because the pieces tend to drift apart slightly. I recommend patting down the cube after every few turns to prevent lockups. About one or two pops happen every solve, yet they are much easier to fix compared to 7x7s, 8x8s, 9x9s, etc.  

 My best solve so far is 1 hour 57 minutes and the turning quality has improved with every solve. Also the pillowed shape, though I was initially skeptical, actually helps with these marathon solves.  

 Do I recommend this cube? Absolutely not, unless you're a hardcore big cube collector.

review_title: Fun solve, turning is smooth but can be catchy
review_text: This puzzle looks clean and sleek and is essentially what is to a 5x5 as a 5x5 is to a Gigaminx (5x5 megaminx). The solving process is fun and anyone who understands commutators and how algs work should pick it up quickly without needing a tutorial. While its turning is normally smooth and fluid with a bit of lube, it quickly starts feeling like a Rubik’s brand cube as soon as the layers are misaligned even by the slightest amount, making turning the corners and doing those commutators really annoying. This misalignment issue is something I see a lot on many of Shengshou’s non-WCAs, so, honestly, I’m not too surprised.

It's more fun because I know there's never a chance for parity and it's easier to turn than the 4-layered version. But the centers make it a little less fun for me. Because each face is a triangle, there are certain cases that don't work like they do on a square face, so sometimes I end up just trying a bunch of things until I get the right case on the last 2 centers. The edges don't change my enjoyment too much since they're very easy. Overall, this is a fun puzzle, I might consider getting the 6-layered and 7-layered versions of this puzzle in the future.

review_title: Better than the WeiPo V5 AI, but is still probably not worth it
review_text:
tl;dr: Performs great, has cool features (wireless charging and a numerical IPG), is ridiculously fast (similar in speed to the V100 Maglev), and experiences some minor catches which can be fixed with slowing lube and tensioning. Probably shouldn't buy it though as the practicality and utility of a smart 2x2 is limited. 

 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 

 I had a chance to try this cube at GAN's offline Shanghai store, and I've owned this cube since August 2025 so I've also had plenty of time with this cube. If you want an in-depth look at the hardware of the puzzle you can view my video review below. 

 This cube retains the same corner design as the outgoing 251 series, with the internal edges having their torpedoes flattened and widened to increase stability  (which is important, especially for this cube as I'll talk about later) and fit the larger ball core that houses the electronics. The cube has 2 key new features: wireless charging and a numerical IPG, the latter we'll probably also see in GAN's next generation of non-smart 2x2s. The plastic on the 251ui does feel harder than the plastic on my 251 M Pro, even after setup and lube, making the ui's handfeel much more clacky and tactile. The turning in the Pro feels much more vague, while the ui has more crunchy turning. 

 The cube is bone-dry (at least mine was, not sure if they started lubing them for global market releases), causing it to be ridiculously fast. The cube also ships with the loosest axis distance and the second-loosest spring compression setting. There are a total of 3 axis distance settings, and 4 compression settings. It being super loose on the loosest setting does not concern me, but what does concern me is it being uncontrollable on the middle-lowest compression setting. If you want the cube to be more controllable, I'd suggest using some heavier lube (I like to use XMT10 to retain a faster feel, but some W5 or super honey might also work). 

 The outgoing 251's piece design already is prone to minor catching, although not much of a problem. However, due to the speed and looseness of the 251 ui, the catching issue becomes much more prevalent (see 5:41 in the below video). Part of this catching issue demonstrated in the video is also because it was on stock settings (the loosest axis distance, 3 out of 3), and I have found out that this can be mitigated as you make the cube tighter. This is also where the wider torpedoes come in; I think that this cube would be pretty much borderline unusable without the wider torpedoes. The cube has pretty good corner-cutting, about the same as the outgoing 251 series and the best out of any other 2x2. But the speed and the minor catches definitely makes this a cube that requires light or accurate turning. 

 The major question then, taking in account all of this and the price (which at $80 USD is cheaper than the WeiPo V5 AI but still insanely expensive), is if it's worth it. Unlike 3x3s, where the data helps you optimize F2L solutions, analyze your pauses and rotations, 2x2 solves are so short (often sub-3 for even moderately advanced CLL users) that the app's analysis is frequently overkill. This cube is a great release, no doubt. It's a good cube for what it is. I wouldn’t recommend most people buy it, just purely out of value and the practicality of a 2x2 smartcube alone. But if you’re trying to collect GAN smartcubes, you have disposable income, or you just really want a 2x2 smartcube, then I don’t think you would regret your purchase. 

 Video Review: https://youtu.be/L4mESiBrlSk

review_title: My Honest Opinion on the GAN 251 UI 2×2 Smart Cube
review_text:
Disclaimer: This is my opinion and my opinion only. 

 I do not like the GAN Cube GAN 251 UI 2×2 Smart Cube. 

 A big part of my disappointment comes from the Cube Station app. It clearly caters to 3×3 users, and the 2×2 feels like an afterthought. The app itself is fairly basic, and it was frustrating just trying to download it. I attempted multiple times before finally realizing the app was already installed on my phone. 

 Once connected, the app found the cube easily and worked fine—but that’s where the positives ended. The font is too small, the toggle switches are tiny, and for someone with big hands like mine, the interface is uncomfortable. The overall experience was frustrating. I don’t like products that don’t strive to make the user experience outstanding, and this one missed the mark. That was a real shame. 

 As for the cube itself, it’s not terrible, but out of the box it was way too fast. I believe it came set around position two or three. The tension system only has four settings, which is very limited. I moved it to the highest tension to slow it down, and that turned into another bad experience. 

 The adjustment tool is poorly designed. It barely fits and requires stretching the pieces apart to use it properly. That’s not good design—plain and simple. A flathead screwdriver-style tool would have been much better. To me, it feels like this cube was rushed through the design process just to get it to market. 

 I’m also unimpressed with the charging setup. The port feels mundane, and the wireless charging feature seems useless. I can do the same thing with my MoYu Super AoLong AI 3x3, which uses its charging stand as a travel case. That’s smart, practical design. GAN’s wireless charging, in comparison, feels like a gimmick. 

 Overall, I’m highly disappointed. I was extremely hyped for this cube, and that hype led to a hard crash back to reality. 

 If you love this smart cube and the app, that’s great. I’m genuinely happy for you. But for me, this product fell short in too many areas. I believe there are better—and cheaper—options available.

tl;dr - outer layers = fast, inner layers = a little sluggish, parity = bad, puzzle = fun! 

 I received this puzzle from GAN, and I can tell you that it's an amazing 4x4! Specifically, the outer layers are extremely fast, to the point that you feel like you're solving a 3x3. Now, this puzzle probably won't become your main - it has a tendency to lock-up a little if you aren't accurate, and the middle layers are a little sluggish compared to the outer layers. It has a bumpy feeling, contrasted especially by the WuQue M, which is extremely smooth. So while the WuQue M is still my main, this puzzle is just plain fun to solve! If I'm doing casual 4x4 solves, I really enjoy solving with the GAN 460! 

 Even when I am solving for speed, the GAN works really well! I average just under 50 seconds with it (compared to 45-ish with my WuQue M). There's just one problem: parities. Specifically the OLL parity. Because it locks up a little and is slightly sluggish with the middle slices, the OLL parity becomes very tedious and can kill an otherwise amazing solve. But if you get no parities, the GAN 460 is amazing! I have the stickerless variant, and while the color scheme is nearly identical to the WuQue M, the green is a darker, almost forest green, which I really like! 

 So yeah, this puzzle may not be the best 4x4 on the market for everyone. It's certainly not my best 4x4. But you know what? This puzzle is fun to solve! Maybe it's the bumpy feeling. Maybe it's the darker green. Maybe it's the stickerless look with the dark internals. Maybe it's the lightning fast outer layers. Maybe it's the visible magnets, which just look amazing! I'm not entirely sure, but I like this puzzle. Again, not my main, but a fun puzzle to solve! 5 stars.

review_title: Fit me perfectly, instantly made me sub-3
review_text:
Before I got this cube, I was failing multiple sub-3s because my 3x3 stage on the Aofu WR M was slow. But then when I got this cube, I instantly became sub-3 on my favorite event which made me SO happy. Now, onto the actual cube. 

 Out of the box, this cube is very usable and fast, with extremely light and fast (but controllable) outer layers. Several big cubers who have tried my cube have mainly commented on how good the outers are. But that isn't to say that the other layers are bad. They're amazing. One can easily tell the notable increase in magnet strength as you go from outside in. However, I do still think that the magnets are ever so slightly on the weaker side, but not to the point that the cube is unusable. The recommended setup for the cubes includes the angstrom lubes, and it's for a reason. I was initially hesitant on these lubes because I thought they would make it too slow. Luckily, it made my cube more controllable and smooth WHILE retaining the amazing out-of-the box feel. Also, this cube practically never pops! Out of the 70ish solves I've done, I can count the pops I've had on one hand. I know many of you might not be the biggest fan of the matte finish, but I like the feel it gives to the cube. Plus, it wears out/breaks in over time. Finally, I want to address the size. Big cubes have always been my favorite events (especially 7x7) but I could enjoy them fully because they were often too big for my tiny hands. This cube solves that problem perfectly, and even if you have bigger hands, I'm sure you can eventually get used to the size(for reference, it's slightly smaller than the GAN 5x5). 

 The one slight issue that I've had is putting a piece back in when it pops, but maybe that just happens 'cause I keep my cube at relatively tight tensions.  

 Amazing, a must-get!

I'm astonishingly satisfied with the performance of this cube. It's absolutely blown me away.

review_title: Not what it used to be (+ potential fix for reported turning and popping issues)
review_text:
I had the original version when it came out around 2020, and at the time I thought it was the best 4x4 on the market (and still is), so much so that I've used it as my main 4x4 despite its comically miniature size for my hands, so I was extremely excited to try the ball core version.  

 Unfortunately it seems with time, wear of the injection molds, plastic being used, quality control, or any number of probable factors related to the cube itself, it just doesn't have the same magic as the original batches. The cube was extremely hard to turn initially, and had some very uncharacteristic catches, and for whatever reason the plastic didn't seem to respond well to whatever lubricant I used even after a thorough break-in. When I took the cube apart though, I noticed many of the screws were straight-up not aligned with the core. They were crooked by at least a full degree, and I found the only real remedy was to take the screws back out and screw them back in manually as straight as possible. And it turns out doing this solved most of my issues, which was a relief, but also underlined my whole disappointment with the cube in general, because this much setup to make a cube perform well shouldn't be necessary for any cube, and really is a disservice to the designer of this cube, because if the factory workers were provided with the means to put the pieces together right the first time, the overall product would be much more successful. After I fixed the screws though, the end result was not necessarily bad, the increase in auto-alignment from the ball-core was noticeable, but not enough overall to make me switch from my original. 

 Summary for possible turning and popping fix:  

  - Take a misaligned screw out and screw it back in carefully to ensure proper alignment (repeat for all 6 screws).
  - Use tighter than factory tensions (corner cutting will improve up to a certain point).
  - Lubricate properly.

review_title: Great puzzle, great turning, great price!
review_text:
Difficulty: 4.5/10
 Playability: 10/10
 Quality: 9/10 

 OVERVIEW: I look for two things in a twisty puzzle: I want them to be fun to play with, and I want them to look nice when they're sitting on my shelf. The YJ Petal Pyraminx does both those things very well, and for only $7. The solve is similar to a Pyraminx, but there are rotating middle layers on each face that can exchange pieces, adding a layer of difficulty. Since the puzzle has only four faces, and the rotating pieces aren't all the same size, traditional algorithms and strategies for swapping center pieces don't work, requiring time and thought to go into how to solve the cube. While it isn't crazy difficult, it's a good puzzle for someone looking to take their cubing to the intermediate level. My first few solves took about ten minutes as I figured out how to efficiently swap centers, but now I take about three minutes to solve it. 

 PROS: The cube looks nice, the turning is good, and the solve challenge is perfect for someone looking to pick up and play with a cube, but not spend too long solving it.
 CONS: None! Occasionally the center circles will need to be properly aligned, but this is so rare that it doesn't take away from the solve.

 I bought this 4x4 from TheCubicle.com vendors at a competition over the weekend and I do not regret my purchase. For $12, you get a magnetic 4x4 that performs better than any other 4x4 in its price range. Its outer layers are very fast and smooth with a medium-strength magnetic bump. The inner layers are a little bit sluggish without proper lubrication. The inners also have a medium magnetic bump. Corner cutting is decent - about 1 piece forwards on outers, 1/2 of a piece reverse on outers, 3/4 of a piece forwards on inners, and 1/3 of a piece reverse on inners. Corner twisting, pops, and lockups are not an issue. My only complaints with this cube are the size and catching. At 62mm, this cube is bigger than most other 4x4s and may not be suitable for people with smaller hands. I personally prefer smaller 4x4s. Catching is a relatively minor issue, which happens during slight layer misalignments, and is mitigated with the magnets. While it has the best performance in its price range, it isn't the best 4x4 on the market. If you're willing to spend the money, I suggest a higher end cube (AoSu GTS2 M, Valk 4, WuQue M).

review_title: YJ is actually becoming a decent 3x3 brand
review_text:

Out of the box, the YJ YuLong V3 UV feels fairly dry and slightly scratchy. After adding some lubricant, the cube becomes significantly faster and smoother. I recommend tightening the tensions slightly because the cube can become overly fast when lubricated. 

 The magnets feel moderate and provide good layer alignment without being too strong, which helps maintain a controllable turning feel. Corner cutting is solid for a budget cube and handles typical speedsolving angles well. 

 One nice detail is that the logo can be removed easily if you prefer a cleaner look or want to add your own logo. Overall, this cube offers excellent performance for the price and is a strong budget option—personally, I think it performs better than the RS3M in terms of speed and feel.

Stick with the non-UV version of this cube if you want more speed (hence the 4 stars).  I also like this cube because you can remove the center cap sticker and put your own.  This cube is a great cube for beginner speed cubers who want a controllable cube that doesn't get overly fast.

The Examinx is a fun puzzle to solve most definitely. I spent at most 5 hours solving it, but there are some things worth mentioning. This puzzle is small in size which is very helpful to get a grip for it while solving it. Turning is decent for the outer layers, but the inner layers are the best. The material is the same as the other Sengso puzzles, so if you've had the 14x14 or 12x12, or any puzzle by Sengso, then you'll know that it has a rather unusual texture on the surface, but I guess that it's to help grip the puzzle. I would say you should be careful with this puzzle when it comes to turning. Misalignment can be an issue, thankfully no pieces popped out for me, but I did have occasional misalignments. They were easy to fix, just needed something hard and small to put the piece back into place. My only complaint is that the puzzle had gaps in it, which was a bit annoying to deal with while solving, but that's what you get for buying such a big puzzle. Also, some of the corners and edges had gaps in them where the pieces connect, but they were not an issue. Despite the complaints, the puzzle works as it should, and I would recommend this if you are a fan of Minx puzzles.

review_title: Good shape mad for any cuber who likes a challenge!!
review_text: This cube is an interesting puzzle to solve.  I got mine from PuzzlCrate, and it was a little crunchy out of the box, but 2-3 drops of DNM-37 did the trick.  The big problem I had was it popped on my first solve.  This was not a big pop, just like 5 or 6 pieces came out.  This is just a note, the puzzle can restrict some moves but overall it is the best shape mod I own and have a great time trying to solve it.

Silky smooth turning, never falls apart after hundreds of solves ,forces you to think hard, this puzzle is a bargain! There are more than one way of solving this, and some ways are more complex than others. The idea is to find the fastest and most efficient solve. This leaves room for creativity! You should like this puzzle.

Build quality is fine, it works, it’s whatever. My complaint is with the solve itself, which is tedious. 

 If this is your first shape mod, you don’t have an axis cube or mastermorphix or mirror cube or anything like that, you might be blown away a bit — the shape changes! Wow! What will they think of next? 

 But I’ve got a few like that. You get used to it — the corner isn’t a new shape, it’s just a different way than colors of telling if you’ve got it in the right orientation. 

 So that’s all fine, I’m not opposed to a mirror cube or etc, in concept. But the problem here is that the pieces are very small, and distinct, but very very similar. So it’s quite likely you’ll get to the last layer and have some impossible parity. What this means (well, depending on the parity; I don’t want to spoil the solve for you) is that two seemingly identical pieces aren’t, and need to be swapped; OR two actually identical pieces need to be swapped, arbitrarily. 

 It’s fine, as a concept, but the reality of solving the puzzle is just so fiddly and tedious. It’s the only one I skip when I scramble the whole collection, because I just can’t be bothered to go through it again. 

 If you’re curious about this kind of mod, I would recommend going for a cube shapemod — there are plenty of them with the same gimmicks, but less tiny pieces.

This is probably the best pyraminx on the market, but only after setup. My setup follows.  The center magnets are not glued well so I recommend disassembling the puzzle (the tips pull straight off) and adding additional glue to the center magnets. Mr. Ms are assembled randomly, so there is a chance that they will have an incorrect color scheme. If you have this issue, switch two caps on every center and tip. After reassembly, some of the tips may click in the middle of turns. This is due to defects on the center caps. There are bumps in the middle of the caps. Use a plastic razor blade to scrape them off or sand them down. I use moderate-tight tensions. For piece lube, I used a bit of Weight 5 on the tracks and XMT-10 and Mystic on the pieces. At this point, do some solves on the puzzle to make sure you like the tensions. If you do, I suggest removing the tips, adding a bit of super glue to one of the corners of the primary tip cap and putting them back on the puzzle. After gluing the tips on it is still possible to tension it, but it is more difficult. If you need to adjust the tensions after gluing the tips, remove one colored cap from the tip of the side you need to tension.  There is a hole in the primary cap into which you can put a screwdriver.  However, you must be careful doing it this, as it is easy to strip the screws.  This setup yields a fast but controllable and stable puzzle.  John Gaynor used a Mr. M with my setup to win U.S Nationals this year.

review_title: Great candidate for WCA, Awesome Puzzle.
review_text:
This is an awesomely fun puzzle. The Shengshou Kilominx turns well, corner cuts, is high quality, and very fun to solve right out of the box. I really think this puzzle has the potential to be a great candidate for WCA competition. Its solution is fun, and can be done in a time frame that seems to be perfect for competition. At least, if the 2x2 cube can be in WCA, this should be too! 

 Anyway, aside from it being a great candidate for competition solving, it's an amazingly fun puzzle, great for starting out on 12 axis puzzles, and isn't super trivial like a 2x2 cube. The puzzle turns well, almost too well, sometimes I drop it because the whole puzzle just WANTS to move, and it's easy to grab it wrong and have 3 layers spin at once while it flies out of your hand! 

 At its core, this is really just a Megaminx with tiny, black centers and edges, and huge corners. I bet you could even sticker the centers and edges with tiny little stickers, I might try that. then you'd just have a really unique megaminx that turns really well. 

 If you like Minx puzzles, your collection would not be complete without this puzzle, and I hope ShengShou has set the stage for a solid Kilominx design, for other companies to try to make even better versions!

I got this as my first big cube (8x8+) because I wanted a challenge and wasn't expecting it to be great as it is the cheapest 15x15 on the market. I was very wrong. Even though it doesn’t have magnets, this cube can be used to do intermediate solving. I have done 3 solves in the past 3 days of having it and they averaged to about 3 hours each. 

 This cube can do finger tricks very easily as it is absolutely tiny compared to other big cubes. I have provided an image for size comparison between the 15x15 and my main 3x3 for anybody wondering how big it is. The turning is pretty smooth and can compare to some Moyu meilong products. The turning quality of all the layers is almost identical. 

 Doing patterns on this big cube is great and the superflip look phenomenal. The standard checkerboard also looks great. The colors are very similar to Moyu’s which is great if you are  expanding your line of big cubes and want to have some budget friendly options. The cubicle look to the cube makes it easier to handle and makes lining up the layers easy. The square look also makes it great for pixel art. 

 (TL;DR) This 15x15 is amazing for the price and the turning quality is great. The colors are similar to Moyu’s which provides a budget option for big cubes. 

 Overall, this is an amazing 15x15 and I am looking forward to Shengshou releasing even bigger cubes in their mosheng line. I hope that this review shows that budget cubes don’t mean bad cubes and that you should buy this cube.
