A nice, smooth-turning, pillowed puzzle with new algorithms to learn to fix center parities, but are still fun to execute. It takes time getting used to initially, but you’ll get the hang of it after 10 or so solves, as I did. I now find myself picking it up every day for a solve.

All you need to do is tighten it a bit. Then it becomes better. So, here’s the story. One time I got the shengshou mastermorphix. It was the same brand, but I LOOSENED IT. When that happened, a pop occurred but it wasn’t only a pop, it was an explosion. So that’s why you never want to loosen shengshou morphix puzzles! (I eventually saw that the screw was broken in my mastermorphix.)  

 It still works fine when it’s tightened. It would be crazy if I got a pop on this thing! I’m not very good fixing pops... Anyways, It’s still working fine on my desk. It’s not too pricey for a puzzle like this. So, it’s worth it if you tighten it. (Do about a little more than a half twist.)
this needs to be tensioned out of the box, my one arrived really loose

review_title: Not the best but it's ok
review_text: I got it for my birthday and I did first turns and it wasn't that good, also it had the wrong color scheme but that doesn't matter, anyway the cube is ok.

As with most shape mods I wasn't expecting top of the line turning, the puzzle did turn fairly well. sometimes alignment is a bit of an issue but if you're not trying to fingertrick it there shouldn't be a problem. 

 One thing that maybe worth noting is that the color scheme is different from all my other morphix puzzles. assuming the line between yellow/red is facing you the lefun pyramorphix (2x2), the shengshou pyramorphix (2x2), the mofang mastermorphix (3x3), and the shengshou gigamorphix (5x5) all have green on the bottom and blue in the back, but the shengshou megamorphix (4x4) has green in the back and blue on the bottom. It isn't really a big issue but something to think about if you have your collection in any sort of display.

review_title: If you love stickerless puzzles, add this to your collection
review_text: I have the Moyu Megamorphix stickered one and it has been my favorite because of the multiple challenging scenarios that come up like last 2 corners that need to be rotated, last 2 corners need to be swapped, and of course the shape shifting aspect. I have been recently staying away from stickered puzzles because stickers peel and chip so I have been waiting for a stickerless Megamorphix that isn't pink for a long time now. Once I saw this, I quickly pulled the trigger. Out of the box, it is really smooth. I like the bright colors too. As much as I like the 4x4 Aosu mechanism, this new(?) Shengshou mechanism turns great too. The only minor issue I have is one of my yellow edges didn't come with a cap. It doesn't affect the turning, just the look when it is scrambled. Other than that, I will keep playing with this for a while hopefully. If you love stickerless puzzles, add this to your collection.

As others have mentioned, the puzzle can be somewhat difficult to align, but with patience, and not tying to go fast, it really isn’t that bad. I’ve had mine for over a year and have never had a pop, and I’m not one to adjust puzzles. I didn’t notice the scheme difference mainly because my Mastermorphix has the old shengshou colors and doesn’t match anyway. Either way that doesn’t bother me much, but that’s up to you

review_title: Good quality but inconsistent color scheme
review_text:

My pyra, master, and gigamorphixes all follow the same scheme but the mega is different.  ...Which is particularly devious when you're solving them all in a row and you use the normal color scheme to position the 2x2 centers on the megamorphix and then later can't figure out why the first layer corners aren't fitting right. 

 The puzzle itself is good though.  Good quality and turns smoothly.

When I received this puzzle, it already had a good amount of wear on it. It has scratches and scuffs on all side and the pieces dont seem to fit very well together. On top of all of that, it has a different color scheme than my Gigamorphix and Master morphix (both ShengShou and Qiyi) This one has yellow and green flipped. Would not recommend.

HOWEVER, it has popped on my twice now in the week or so that I've had it, and so the real challenge is not solving the puzzle but rather rebuilding it after a pop. I find the rebuild to be fun, if unexpected, but it's hard to do without a friend to help hold it. 

 I highly recommend the *morphix family of puzzles, as well as the Moyu Axis puzzles. In this case, I'd recommend going for the Moyu Aosu puzzle with a set of replacement stickers. 

 Have fun!

review_title: Buy a set of washers to go with
review_text:
First off, the gold looks great, like a Klimt painting, and is more fun to scramble than other puzzles are to solve. I am starting to understand 3x3x3 algs more from solving this because the recognition of shapes feels different from colors. Because of the brushed metal look you also have to pay attention the centers rotation to fully solve.  

 I recommend that you start popping the center caps and disassemble this cube before you turn it for the first time. The puzzle has *NO WASHERS* in the centers and during my first couple solves before I added washers the spring ends started shredding the plastic something awful. Additional lube/cleaning right away also might have saved it from some scratching on the sides of the cubies. It's not a big deal but it does look so good that I want it to look perfect. 

 The turning is obviously pretty catchy with the weird shaped pieces but loosening the tensions helps a lot. The two narrowest faces can't be tensioned as loose as I would like though because there is little to no space to back out the screws under the caps.
Turns smoothly, solves using the same algorithms as a regular 3x3 and looks even more impressive when solving. The scrambled cube itself looks like art.
This cube is very challenging, but fun to solve. The stickers are very good (as opposed to the FangGe 2x2 Mirror). I think every cuber should have this.

 The mirror stickers are not super glossy, they are reflective but have a "brushed" texture which makes them look slightly cheap in person. The stickers also dent and scuff easily.
Very good cube. Has good corner cutting. My algebra teacher has one...

This cube is great! It turns amazing right out of the box and there is no lube need. There were a few scratches on the the sticjers, but other than that, I would highly recommend this cube. This is so good, it is almost as if ShengShou made a speed cube for the mirror blocks! Out of the box the turning was very smooth and fast. After lubing it, it was amazing. It is pretty easy to solve, but you need some time to get used to it. Overall, great and fun cube.

I finally learned how to solve the Square-1 after putting it off for a long time and it was more fun than I expected. So when I saw this version, I knew I had to try it. As expected, it was very similar to solving a Square-1 with a few extra moves thrown in. I was able to figure out the extra moves somewhat intuitively, but it's a little bit of trial-and-error so I'm trying to figure out an algorithm to solve it more efficiently. 

 Overall construction feels solid. The slice turning is super smooth but perhaps a bit too loose. The horizontal turns are decent, but you can feel the magnets as each piece turns past the slice layer which gives the turning a bit of a bumpy feeling. But since this helps make the slice turning a lot easier I think it's a worthwhile tradeoff. 

 Because you're not blocked by bandaging you can also do some patterns. Definitely worth getting.

review_title: Newfound Square-N enthusiast who realized that this puzzle can do a lot of cool things
review_text:
I only recently learned how to speedsolve Square-1, so I figured this would be the logical next step. I find the solution pretty simple: I just pair up the pointy corner pieces until they're like regular corners, then solve it like a regular Square-1. The turning on this is pretty smooth even out of the box, and although it's pretty dry-feeling I haven't lubed it yet so far. The slice isn't magnetic, which I don't mind. I'm not a super huge fan of how there's magnets in every single top and bottom layer piece, though, because you can just feel that cliclicliclicliclick with every turn and it sort of bothers me. However, Square-2 isn't a super competitive market so there aren't many other options you can go to.  

 Some fun things you can do with it:
 -Literally any bandage mod you want: Since this cube has smaller "piece increments" than a Square-1, you can make a lot of fun bandage challenges. I taped every other piece together in the layers to make what I call a "Square-6" because it has 6 pieces per layer. I haven't been able to solve that particular challenge yet, but I peeled the tape off and invented a bunch of other cool things. You can also make a Square-0 where you bandage each full 60-degree corner with its adjacent edge (although this can be done on a regular Sq-1 too) or some sort of "Square-0 dino cube" where you stick together a 30-degree corner wedge with another edge piece and its opposing corner wedge, basically making it all edges. 
 -Flip the color scheme: You can intentionally put the corners together incorrectly so it seems like the top and bottom are flipped. For example, instead of making a corner with yellow on top, red on the left, and green on the right (how it would be normally) I can pair the corner wedges so that the red is on the right and green on the left. I do this with every corner in the cube and then flip the middle layer like how you can do it on a normal Square-1 so that two opposing sides are switched. The end result is a solved cube with the color scheme flipped.
 -Anything else you can think of!
 At first I thought this was going to be lame because it's just a Square-1 with spicy corners, but now I realize that there's no limit to what you can imagine with this cube!!!

review_title: The performance, feel, and overall cube is great, but this cube is just too similar
review_text:
Ok, I need to be very clear here. This cube is absolutely FANTASTIC. Very customizable, larger range of settings, adjustable magnets, very light, more modern feel, faster and smoother turning, everything…
 But honestly…it just needs something more. Don’t get me wrong, it is a great cube, but it just isn’t unique enough. It feels a lot like a V3, just much, much lighter and more responsive. But if you want a lighter V3, you can always buy it and set it up with light lubes and looser tensions or literally ANYTHING else that may work for you. And the adjustable edge and corner magnets…this makes the Tornado series have even more options to make the V5 your own. But we just don’t need this. People will buy this cube and then potentially change the magnets once or twice, but after that this cube is no more customizable than the V4 or V3. This cube doesn’t have a humongous difference from the V3 Premium anyway, so why advertise it as a new flagship with so much more to offer?And just generally…nothing makes this unique. Cubers that want a light and fast cube probably have a WRM V11, Gan V100, Gan 12/13/15/16, Tornado V4/V3/V3 Premium, a Superweilong V2, or something else. If that many cubers already have a light, smooth, and responsive cube, they don’t need to get another cube unless it has something that you need and don’t have. And that’s the issue with this cube! It is a bit different from the V3, but the performance is similar and the feel is too. And just generally…it takes all the standard metas in 3x3 and puts it in one puzzle. This makes the cube something that isn’t unique. It like is any other light cube with a ball core, and this cube is being released a year after something like the V11. It doesn’t have anything that makes the performance better for YOU, or any other cube, for the fact. It is light and fast and blocky, yeah, but is it more flexible? More controllable? More balanced? More stable, airy, rounded, soft, smooth, or any other characteristic? No, it’s just a cube which has the general idea of what a good cube should be! I suggest that most people don’t buy this cube, not because the performance is bad, as it is actually excellent, but because there are various other puzzles like this one that have many of the same characteristics as the V5, but they have something special about them, something which makes it better or worse than a different cube, and not neither. For example, the V100 is smaller, softer and crunchier than other cubes on the market and features black internals and a more flexible GAN handfeel. Or the Weilong V11 is an extremely fast, fluid, light, responsive, and forgiving cube which is still easy to make controllable.
 See what I mean yet? This IS a good cube, but it can always be beaten by another cube because this cube is just NOT unique enough and just doesn’t have anything that makes it its own cube. 
 So generally, I would say only buy this cube if you want a Tornado and need every ounce of adjustability and performance you can get. Otherwise, pick something else.

review_title: I have a V5, I have a Wrm V11, and I have a V100, and I like all of them better than this cube.
review_text: Ok for starters I purchased three 3x3s in the last 4 months. Those three are the Moyu RS3M V5(Ball Core UV MagLev, of course), The Moyu Weilong V11 20 Magnet BC Maglev, and the GAN V100(anyone else notice all the cubes have V as in version in the name?). I think all of these cubes are pretty much better. The V11 is a complete fluid TPS demon of a speed cube and I love it. The V5 is great for beginners and intermediate solvers and is blocky, tactile, stable, light, and responsive, and yeah pretty much great. The V100 is soft, crunchy, and flexible and simply feels and performs amazing for only $40 honestly. But the V5 doesn’t seem like it’s better. Good for Tornado-Lovers, but EVEN FOR THEM I think recent GAN or Moyu cubes are the better option in terms of both pricing AND performance. The V5 has good features, like a more extensive dual adjustment system, but I personally didn’t use it much and found the GAN 16’s adjustment settings to be much better. Also I don’t think the whole adjust-the-cube-with-hands thing even makes any sense. The idea of this hand adjustment system is that you can adjust the cube anywhere by hand. But once you have settings you like and know you might main this cube, WHAT KIND OF PERSON IS GOING TO OPEN THE CUBE UP AND CHANGE THE SETTINGS DURING A SOLVE OR SOMETHING? I don’t think that it is really that difficult to bring a tool with you, especially if you are actually in need of changing the settings when you aren’t at home. So yeah. The feel is fine, nothing special, V100, V11, and pretty much 100 other cubes feel just as good if not better in my opinion. And I lock up sometimes too by the way on this cube. It’s 5 dollars more than the V11 and the V11 has all the features on this cube that matter PLUS nicer feel and better performance and just generally is also pretty good. I’d say don’t get it if you already have a Weilong V11 cuz yeah. If you love Tornado or just really really want it, you might love it and it may still perform the best for you regardless of what I said so still consider this cube in that situation so yeah. Thx for reading my essay.

review_text: I really want to love this cube, but I can’t. Once you get it set up it feels great, and I’m getting great times. The problems reside in the setup. The numbers on the corner magnet adjustments are unreadable. Completely unreadable. I’ve used a magnifying glass and light and can tell there’re numbers but you can’t read them. The other issue is the core adjustment. There is no longer a handle like previous Tornadoes. It is very difficult to turn the dial clockwise as the tension increases. I end up pushing down too much and the center nut comes out and the whole maglev just goes flying. Other times, instead of moving to the next setting, the entire center piece turns. This is a horribly designed product. But then once you get the settings right, it is a great cube. So buyer beware.

product_name: X-Man Tornado V3 M Flagship 3x3 (Magnetic Core)
review_text: Overall, this is a great cube. It corner cuts enough for it to never be a problem, which is the main goal. It’s a very fast, but stable cube. If you plan on getting this, make sure that you have a slower lube for the tracks. Out of the box, the cube had a couple scratches (barely noticeable), but stuff you wouldn’t see on a higher priced cube. This wasn’t a problem given that a bit of use would result in more noticeable wear, and I think it’s worth it for the price. The customization is great, not too much, or too little. I’ve had a bit of trouble getting the center caps on and off, but I don’t plan on  changes tensions once I find the right ones. Overall, phenomenal cube, especially for the price. I have tried every notable Gan and moyu cube, and I would definitely use this cube over those.

review_text: For some context, I was using a very old and worn out Gan 356 X before I got this cube, so it is possible that my experience with upgrading to this cube is a little inflated because of how it compares to my previous cube. The dual adjustment system and changeable magnets are also really cool features, although I haven't had to mess with them much because the puzzle performs as well as I would like it to out of the box. That's all, I just wanted to share my incredible first impressions.

Unless you have a long fingernail your skin is going to have a dent in it. I don't think that using a prying tool would work just because we are talking about plastic and it's not that durable. 

 For the magnet system it's a little time consuming so what I suggest doing is try all the settings that you want to try on only one side then the one you like best you put it on all the sides. But one of the corner red circles popped off. I'm honestly not sure how it popped off but I think that it popped off when I dropped it once.

product_name: X-Man Tornado V3 M Flagship 3x3 (Magnetic Core)
review_text:
I've had the Tornado V3 for over a year, and despite the new GAN cubes and almost every MoYu release, it is still one of the best cubes on the market. The feeling, the quiet sound, and my results on it have been spectacular.  

 However, there's been one glaring issue that's been haunting me ever since: its durability. and no, I'm not talking about the core durability (which got fixed a long time ago). It is about every other part of the cube. I've gone through 5-6 different Tornado cubes and every time, something breaks. A corner-core magnet falls out and can't go back in. The corner tile breaks apart and can't be put back together. A corner-edge magnet falls inside the cube and is irreparable. Every cube I've used long-term has broken in one way or another. This is not due to my own negligence: I've made sure to keep it in a cube bag, not to drop it, not put heavy weights under it, etc. But without fail, this cube finds another way to break. 

 TLDR; If you want a quiet cube, get this one and be extra careful with this cube. Otherwise, please get the RS3M V5 to save yourself $8 and the headache of not being able to use your cube every other month. The V5 performs just as well if not better and will not break on you.

product_name: X-Man Tornado V3 M Flagship 3x3 (Magnetic Core)
review_text: I bought this cube to find out if the hype was legit. It did not disappoint. It has a unique elastic and flexible, yet snappy feel to it which is slightly better than the Gan 14 crunchy feel. The 0.5mm size difference is surprisingly helpful as well. I use Weight 5, angstrom combo, mystic, and a drop of dnm-37 for the lubes. One issue though I have noticed that I've seen multiple other people have with this cube is its durability. When I first received it and dismantled the cube to clean it, the plastic extension from the core to the red center came out of place as if it had not been glued in place properly. I was able to carefully reinsert the plastic and add some super glue to fix it. However, I have noticed some corner magnets are also coming loose, and there's no telling if or when the core will snap again. Perhaps I got an older version that is less durable? If so, I would appreciate it if I could receive an updated version and send this one back, or just buy another one that is the updated version. Despite these setbacks, the cube is still the best performing cube I've tried so far and look forward to using it at an upcoming competition.

review_title: Mid at first, GODLY with SETUP
review_text:
I know corners having magnets pushed in is a common issue on this cube. One of my corner magnets was pushed in slightly but no effect on performance. Mine also came with spring noise, and although I did manage to lube the springs, it was VERY difficult to do (you have to match the holes in the spring container with those in the center caps and then stick a syringe tip thru the holes, or just take out the springs which is also hard. However, I hadn't heard of others with that problem so I guess mine was just a bit faulty.
 After setup (I would only recommend lubing tracks, not pieces, since there's not much piece contact anyway and lube seeping out is disgusting), this cube is GOATED. Super CUSTOMIZABLE, SOFT, and FORGIVING (if you corner cut reasonably it's very lenient, if you corner cut >45 or line-line it'll take some effort). 

 TLDR: Most versatile cube on the market, not for people who don't have lube or are too lazy to setup.
 Play around with the 125 settings. I bet you'll find one you didn't think you would like.

product_name: X-Man Tornado V3 M Flagship 3x3 (Magnetic Core)
review_text:
The cube is amazing. Really. For 2 weeks, that is. 
 Out of the box, the cube felt amazing. With some lube and tensioning, my times were down 2 to 3 secs with this cube.
 Just a few days ago, I felt something strange on the blue side, it was extremely loose, so I took all the centre caps off, and to my surprise the blue centre had a strange feel to it. The adjustment system was almost floating above the centre piece and did not respond to any tensioning. Even on tensions 5 and 5, the tension system did not respond. Upon further inspection, I found that the core had stripped, cracked, and was now fully unusable. When doing just a couple solves, the blue side would eventually unscrew itself and come off. On top of that, it was extremely loose.  

 AlI can say is that the cube deserves the hype, and that it feels better than all the GAN cubes. Though I do not know if one would like to spend 30 dollars on a cube that only works for a week. I don't know if qiyi will be fixing this, making a new design, or perhaps they will just leave that cube as it is, but I believe it's not worth it. Many people have experienced this issue on Reddit and on here too, and I believe qiyi needs to make some sort of fix.  

 It's your choice, take the the risk if you wish, perhaps this would not happen to your cube. I just believe it's not worth taking the risk.  

 I hope this helps.

review_text:
This cube is AMAZING. The unboxing was very premium except one of the magnets on my case wasn't glued in properly. Whether it worked or not I am still going to end up throwing away the case because I don't need the packaging. With the out of the box settings the cube turned fairly well. It feels similar to the RS3M, just a lot more smooth. The corner cutting is good enough and only a few times have I had bad lock-ups. The cube is the perfect speed and maintains a lot of stability even while turning fast.
 On my first day using the cube I set some insane PBs. I got an 11.98 ao5 (pb by over a second) and my first sub-14 ao12. I decided to set up the cube today and settled on the mystic setup for the Tornado v2. This is axis distance and spring compression set to 2 and magnets set to 3. Then I added mystic, weight 5 (I don't have 4) and dnm-37. The cube is about the same speed but is smoother and a little gummy. I would definately reccomend this setup.
 My only complaint other than the lack of magnet glueing in the case is the corner twists. Since I got the cube I have already had 2 corner twists. It is not a huge deal but can be annoying when it happens. Also, I can't seem to notice the core magnets doing anything. I am sure they are helping stabilize the cube but they don't add to the magnetic click after each turn.
 Overall, I would highly reccomend this cube and it has become my new main over the wrm 2021 maglev.

review_text:
Really wanted to try an Xman cube and glad I got this. Definitely not disappointed as I wasn't planning on this being my main. Solved pretty decent on it, but nothing to write home about. 

 Pros
 - Cube is really smooth and stable. Kind of crunchy feeling and fairly quiet. And it corner cuts fairly well. 
 - Setting it up was a breeze (especially compared to the GAN15 I main)
 - Honestly I like the frosted plastic. I'm not as partial to UV as I thought 

 Cons
 - Pretty blocky feeling. Definitely an X-man trait that just isn't for me.

review_text:
This cube is amazing and is one of my 3x3 mains. The turning is very fast, and for me I prefer the Pioneer over the Flagship, because the maglev gives the cube an extra burst of speed that is more suited to my turning style, so that is something to keep in mind. As for the cube itself, it is very stable, and the cube deforms way less than other cubes like the WRM v9. Combined with lube, TV3 Pioneer is probably the most satisfying to turn out of all the cubes that I have. It is quiet, smooth, buttery, and still very fast with the right lubricants and settings. Speaking of settings, the dual adjustment system is incredible, and you can very easily find good settings that will suit your needs, without compromising the stability and reliability of the cube. There is very little to dislike about how the cube turns, but shifting towards the cube itself there are a few issues I have with it. For one, the magnet capsules crack easily, and if you mess with them too much they will start to break down a bit. Corner twisting makes me feel very uncomfortable because the sharp corners dig themselves into the edge magnets, and if you do it enough times the edge magnet capsules will break. Be sure that your turning is accurate and not too aggressive, because the cube does tend to corner twist if you do. Additionally, the hollow plastic makes this crunching sound when you do certain corner cuts, and it almost sounds like something is breaking inside of the cube. I am a little hesitant to go my top speed while using this cube out of fear that I will severely damage it, and compared to the v9 it is not as fast. It is also less controllable than the Flagship, so if you are satisfied with that version the Pioneer might not be for you, as the maglev increases the speed by a huge margin, and controlling it might be difficult if you are accustomed to the springs. 
 But as long as you turn accurately, take good care of the cube, and have good settings, TV3 Pioneer will not disappoint. It is easily one of the best cubes on the market, and I would highly recommend getting it. I got my current PB while using this cube. The UV also adds a nice shine to it, so if you want to fork over the extra dollars for the coating definitely go for it. 
 Again, great cube!

The TV3 I bought from the cubicle had some quality issues, and from what I've heard the TV4 has fixed that. But it's a very weighty cube. Especially coming from Gan cubes or recent Moyu releases. Now, the TV4 has it's place. It got me my first 3 or 4 sub 10's in comp and has been through thousands of solves without any breakage. That is something I could say about most Mains (beside the TV3) but oh well. The TV4 is in no way a bad cube and can still be used at the top level. It's just not totally for me. But it is going to be a cube that most if not all intermediate to advanced solvers can use to get good times. It's reliable and that's all you really want out of a main 3x3. All in all, the Tornado V4 was a bit of a let down but it was not a Gan 14 Pro let down. It has gotten many good times and is a solid cube. As such it will probably be forgotten as it was not revolutionary like the TV3 or the Gan 11M Pro, but it will always hold a special place in my heart and the hearts of many in the community/

review_title: X-Man Shadow V2:  Long Wait, But Worth It
review_text: I am a proud owner of the Shadow V1  that was my main for over 2 years. Now that the cube is starting to lose its good performance because of wear, I decided to grab the Shadow V2 instead of the MGC since I really trust the reliability of Qiyi puzzles.  I have been waiting for a new flagship 6x6 from Qiyi for awhile now ever since the MGC started to make the Shadow V1 felt obsolete. When I took the Shadow V2 out of the box, the cube is noticeably lighter and smaller than the previous version of the Shadow. Turning out of the box is very effortless because of the extra grooves that make the cube low friction along with very fast and stable layers throughout the cube. Stability is also very phenomenal. I had 1 lockup and no pops when I am turning aggressively, but there is a little bit of catching involved. While the cube is still stock, I decided to lube the cube in combination of DNM, Lubicle Speedy, and Lubicle Silk to prevent the cube from dying out quickly. That resulted in a very buttery smooth turning along with a very fast inner layers and outer layers. Stability is still preserved after the setup. My times are very consistent in a very good way. I get very good results on this cube, but didn't break any PBs yet. Despite the imperfections of lockups and catches, it is pretty understandable that 6x6 hardware isn't perfect, but this cube is surely an improvement over other 6x6s including the MGC. As long that it is more stable and more satisfying to turn than its predecessor, I can say it is better. Overall, this is a great 6x6 and will be used by world class solvers. Recommend it? Yes.

 All that being said, the X-Man Shadow V2 is a good, noticeable step in the right direction for 6x6 engineering. We may never have a perfect 6x6, but this puzzle is pointing us in a good direction. Definitely worth the price tag! Can and do recommend for any intermediate-to-advanced 6x6 solvers (I average mid-4 minutes)

review_text:

 Original review: This is an amazing 5x5, Its quite dry out of the box and needs break-in and lube (similar to X-Man Tornado V3). But after lubing and break-in, it feels amazing. It is very stable and controllable. I have never had it even come close to popping in my solves and I only ever got it to "pop" after 2 failed attempts to force a pop. Corner twists are not too hard to do, but I doubt they will ever happen in a solve. The outer layers are similar in speed to an MGC, but the inner layers are a bit slow. Corner cutting is good (see pictures for R' corner cuts). The cube is very quiet for a 5x5, it is quieter than my DaYan TengYun V3 3x3, which is a cube famous for its quietness. Turning is very smooth. That being said, my cube had what I assume was a manufacturing defect. Out of the box, if you orient the cube with white front and red top, performing a sexy-move will cause the blue-red-white corner to catch really badly and completely lock the U face. It mostly went away after breaking it in, and I decided it was a defect that's not worth returning or replacing. I attached a picture of the lock up. it is not as bad as it used to be, but on all other corners and/or orientations, the wing pieces always stick with the corner instead of getting caught internally.

READ before judging. Honestly, I actually like this more than the AoFu WRm and the Meilong 7M.
 .

 .
 I heard some people reviewing this say its similar to the Hong, but describing how this cube came out of the box, it had some lube already in it, and a bit on the outside. It was also really tight, which I didn't like at first because I was so used to the AoFu, but after some silicone lubes and some DNM, this cube is still not faster, but it moves at a pace where you can solve fast, and stays in shape which may or may not have to do with the corner-to-core magnets (very controllable).
 .
 Unlike the Hong, which I found the inner layers to be so sluggish, the inner layer(s) on this cube actually feels extremely consistent on all layers, with both inners just being barely slower.
 .
 Regarding popping, honestly, the Spark v1 no matter what people said about it, I always found that it pops due to its second-outer layer's wing design, which is small and does not hook to any of the layer on the outside which catches, and pops which is very annoying unlike the AoFu. This cube however, the v2, has the same wing design as the v1, but somehow, (I'm not an engineer so I am not 100% sure), the wing ratio to pieces seem somewhat larger, and it hardly ever catches on the outer layers, which I found extremely good and I hardly ever popped. In fact, I popped on this cube less than the AoFu somehow, though I still think the wing design on the AoFu makes more sense.
 .
 Texture - Unlike the v1, this cube does NOT have primary internals just as the pictures. It starts out with the classic QiYi sandiness, but after lubing, it still feels cohesive, but not as sandy. Holding the cube, it has NO UV coating, but rather the normal QiYi semigloss feel. I didn't like it at first, but now I kinda do.
 .
 It all comes down to personal preference, but if you prefer cubes that are more stable and controllable, this is THE 7x7 for you.

I took the time to set up this cube by lubing the core and slice layer with 50k and Lubicle silk on the U and D layers. To top it all off, I tightened up the tensions a bit. That resulted in a more controllable Square-1 with good speed on the top and bottom layers along with a smooth, yet responsive feel. Although I tightened up the tensions, the good corner-cutting ability was not sacrificed at all, resulting in a fluid turning and good responsiveness while performing algorithms. Lockups are largely reduced and I managed to get sub-25s constantly. Compare with a Volt V2, which is blocky and doesn't corner-cut well, leading to lockups and the cube would just fly out of my hands. Overall, its corner-cutting abilities and good speed led to a responsive turning that everyone needs in their Square-1. Well done YJ and I highly recommend this puzzle.

review_title: Not perfect, but still the best Square-1 on the market!
review_text:
This cube is not perfect; the frosted plastic, lack of edge magnets, strong slice magnets, and overall poor magnet job are disappointing for a cube that was teased this long.  However, the raw speed and corner cutting of this puzzle completely blows any other Square-1 out of the water.   

 This cube out of the box is too loose, so YOU HAVE TO TIGHTEN THIS PUZZLE A LOT MORE THAN YOU DO FOR ANY OTHER SQUARE-1.  If not, you get the problem a lot of people are complaining about: pops and big lock-ups.  However, on my tensions, which still provide insane corner cutting and speed, I have not had a single pop or bad lockup in my 5000+ solves.  I have attached a picture of my tensions. 

 I average sub-10 and have done over 5 thousand solves with this puzzle, and I can't go back to the Volt v2 (let alone the YLM).  My setup currently is just a generous amount of Lubest XMT-10 (everywhere), which makes it extremely fast and smooth.

review_title: Best square one on the market.
review_text:
The YJ MGC is by far the best. Out of the box, there are small catches on some of the edges. This is probably because there are small pieces of plastic jutting out. However, after learning how to solve it and doing a few solves, it completely went away. My first impressions is that this puzzle was fast and clacky. After a little while, the fast feeling ,I d of went away, similar to Moyu cubes’ sandy feel out of the box. It also was able to pop a lot. You could tighten the tensions, but I didn’t like that. (Just my opinion don’t take it too seriously.) After lubing it with Weight 5, Lubicle Speedy, and DNM, I can confirm that this makes the puzzle so much better. The insanely smooth feel that Lubicle speedy gives kind of goes away after break in (I heard Lubicle silk helps with that), but it retains that fast, quiet feeling. I also installed maglev in the core later on, and it makes this cube a lot faster and gives it an effortless feel.  

 If you are installing maglev to your square one, make sure to not put the screw into the blue thing on the other side all the way until you can feel it. This works fine with the screw mechanism, but with maglev, you cannot turn the slice with that. Just do a few turns counterclockwise after feeling the screw and that will be excellent. 
 Another fun part about the maglev is that it is close to impossible to pop on this. Even with the seemingly looser tension, it is very hard to forcefully pry out the edges. (I can’t actually do it on the maglev. Please don’t try, though.) 

 Overall, amazing cube! Best square one on the market as of early December 2023.
 Also someone else bought this for me so this is not a verified purchase.

Only rating 3 stars though because of how much it pops. I get that square 1 is not the most structurally sound cube, but THIS much popping is absurd. I average 1 pop every 2 solves. Competing with this cube and hoping this doesnt happen.

review_title: The best cube for all skill level🏆
review_text: This is I think the best cube for beginners and professionals. I'm currently a beginner for sq1 but I'd say I'm almost at pro level for 3x3 so I think it's still fine to judge professional hardware👍 One thing for sure is definitely the slice move. The slice move is literally the best. Since it has core to edge magnets it's perfectly strong and smooth. The u, d layer was a bit dry at first but it became alot better after breaking in. But obviously since it doesn't have additional magnets for the u, d layer alignment it's not as good as the slice move and the magnet is pretty weak too. But the reason why I think it's still the best for all skill level is because of how good it performs for the price. When I first considered buying a sq1 I chose between the picube v1 or this one. Obviously the maxed out picube version is much better but it's almost 2 times the price. But the performance of the v2 is definitely not twice as bad. And also the breaking issue is completely gone. I had a few times where I turned the cube with force without the layer aligned to do the slice move. And the cube popped(obviously). But it didn't break even though it looked like it should have broke. And it was pretty easy to put the pieces back together. The uv coating is really nice as well. I personally like matte better usually but the uv coating on this one for some reason just feels better than other cubes. Overall the cube is like a 9.5/10. Not a 10 just because the u, d alignment magnet is just a bit weak. But it's probably a 10 if you count the price. And definitely a 100 for the fact that a sq1 is compatible for all skill level. And one small advice for those who are starting sq1 for the first time. Sq1 is a lot harder than you think. The beginner method is easy but if your thinking of actually speedcubing sq1 you should think carefully before buying an expensive cube. That happened to me and I'm so glad I didn't buy the expensive picube version. I think I'm better with 3x3 and 4x4😅

review_title: Best 2x2 on the market! (but requires setup)
review_text: Ootb the cube was very bubbly and quick. Corner twisting was rather frequent, although the turning was nearly effortless. Spring noise was also present, but lubing the core with any lasting silicone will fix the problem. I've done about 300 solves so far, and have set up the cube with FZ-Glide and Silk, which made the corner twisting less and the cube more buttery-smooth. Corner twisting is still a problem, but lubing causes it to be a bit more mitigated. The ball-core and UV didn't really change anything for me respectively, besides the UV coating making the surface more durable. I got a PB of 0.81 seconds with this cube and would recommend it for any intermediate/advanced 2x2 solvers!

I got one of the prototypes of this puzzle (white) and it is not that bad. There was some issues like corner twisting, slowness, and sometimes pops (with my tensions), but the corner cutting was good.  

 My statements why it is good: this 2x2 made me get a sub 1 personal best (unofficial) and a sub 4 personal record (official) and it inspired me to get faster, and I learned some cll (still progressing). 

 My statements why it is bad: their were some lock ups and corner twisting but there were other things. The hard magnet felling made my turning style change and this putts an affect on my other events I do, the lube I used (DNM37) would only last a little more than a week, and a corner broke...

review_title: Best on the market, room for improvement
review_text: With the MGC, 6x6 hardware has made a huge leap forward. It came with 3 sets of springs, and I had to sort the 2 that were not installed in the cube by threading 6 springs on a toothpick and seeing which ones compressed differently when I squeezed all 6. Only the firmest set of springs is really any use (it came with medium springs installed). Firmer springs yet would not be out of place, to limit flex. Contrary to other reviewers, I find this puzzle to be both stable and very fast. Magnet balance is good. I wouldn't mind stronger magnets, but I generally prefer my magnets just about as strong as possible. Excellent puzzle, highly recommend, really excited to see where 6x6 hardware goes from here.

Why would I get a flagship 6x6 as my first though, you might ask. Look at the price. $25. Half the price of the Shadow. This and the Shadow are considered the best 6x6s on the market, most claiming the MGC is better, and for half the price. The flagship 2x2s are only $5 less than this, and the flagship 3x3s, 4x4,s and 5x5s. The quality and feel of this cube is fast, yet stable (at reasonable tension). I can solve a 2x2-5x5, and this cube definitely feels great, and makes me want to learn 6x6. I got this cube a year ago as my first 6x6, and I really loved it! All the layers were very smooth, the magnet strength was perfect, and I had no issues turning it despite my inexperience with 6x6. But, the cube came too loose out of the box, and that caused it to pop. After fixing the pop, some of the innermost layers became terrible. When you turn them, it feels like you're grinding the pieces against the internals and they and catch constantly at the end of a turn. I've researched this issue online, and so far nobody seems to have an answer on how to fix this. I thought an internal piece popped, so I partially took the cube apart to see if I could find anything out of place. I found nothing, so I put it back together... the innermost layers were still terrible. I decided to take the cube fully apart and reassemble it, and that worked for a while, until it popped again. I've tried so many different things, I've tried tightening the screws, because I thought, "maybe they were too loose and the screw head is rubbing against the pieces." That didn't work. I've tried using different lubricants to try and reduce the friction and grinding in the inner layers. That didn't work. I've tried fully taking apart and reassembling this cube 4 SEPARATE TIMES. That didn't work. I have no idea what to do, and I'm very ticked off that nothing I try seems to fix anything. The only reason I'm not giving this 1 star is because of how good the performance was initially. If anyone at TheCubicle has any idea on how to fix this, please let me know.

review_title: WHAT WHAT WHAT NO NO YOURE KIDDING ME
review_text: This is epic the best 6x6! Half as much as the shadow- Twice as good! Comes with factory lube, I would reccomend getting rid of that and lubing it yourself. Let me get this out of the way. The YJ MGC 6 is the best 6x6 I've ever used. It's the first 6x6 that didn't make me feel like it was fighting against my turning, it doesn't catch often, and it is dirt cheap. It's an amazing 6x6. But some major issues with it make it hard for me to recommend, the biggest one being that the center edges are ridiculously fragile. They pop out all the time and putting them back in is almost impossible without messing it up. Every single time they pop out and I put them back in, there is always a horrible noise when I turn the innermost layers. The issue can be fixed by bending the piece back, but that's a very risky move because one wrong move will break the piece. It's such a shame because the MGC 6 is revolutionary in so many other ways, and its potential is squandered by some fragile pieces. So if you want the best of the best, this is the 6x6 for you, but you'll have to be really careful with those center edge pieces. If you don't want to take that risk, I'd say you should go for the Shadow instead of this cube.

I have no idea who would be buying this cube in 2024, but I've had this for a while and I'd like to give my thoughts on it. 

 Pros:
 This cube looks and feels very premium for a budget cube, with its primary plastic internals and vibrant, well contrasting sticker shades. Despite the rounded corners, I basically never get corner twists, which is nice to see. The turning also has one of the nicest and most unique feelings of any 3x3 I've ever tried; it's very quiet and has a very distinct smoothness that only this cube has, (from what I've tried.) This cube is incredibly stable and the weaker magnets mesh well with the more slow/moderate speed it has. The price (at the time) was ridiculous, $15 for a magnetic 3x3 of this quality was unheard of! 

 Cons:
 This cube is very stable, but because of that, corner-cutting is not great. The cube can barely do 45°, and reverse cuts cap out at under half a piece. The corner-cutting also takes a pretty decent amount of effort to do. However, this hasn't proven to be that huge of an issue for me. I just prefer more flexible cubes that I can spam TPS on. I'm not a fan of how slow this cube seems at times. The MF3RS2, which a lot of other people complained about being slow, the MGC is much slower than that. On top of that, this cube really eats through lube. My cube came extremely terrible out of the box, the tensions were uneven, spring noise on a few sides and the factory lube wasn't great. I recently picked up this cube again and decided I was going to set it up properly. I wanted it to be fast, so I used Mystic on the surface and tracks of the pieces and put in a few drops of DNM-37. I should've lubed the core with weight-5 to reduce friction and spring noise, but I didn't. The cube did improve a lot, however, after a few solves, it already seems like it's starting to slow down again. On top of all of this, there seems to be some quality control issues. My cube had some scratches/defects on the pieces/stickers, the glue on the magnets was weak which caused some of them to get dislodged, and the stickers are absolutely abhorrent. Some sides look decent, while others look awful. The stickers on this have gotten chewed up more than any other stickered cube I have, despite me not using it nearly as much as other 3x3s. I ended up just taking all of the stickers off, and I'm hoping to get a replacement set soon. 

 In conclusion, this cube is interesting, but definitely not the best. It has a very unique feeling, but it's too slow with too many quality control issues for me to recommend it. Personally, I would've settled for a Cubicle Pro Shop Yuxin Little Magic M. That would've been slightly more expensive, at $20 compared to $15. However, it has far better performance, and it would be completely tensioned and lubed for you. Now, with the RS3 M 2020 revolutionizing the market for budget cubes, the value of this falls flat. There is no reason to ever get this today besides to see where the MGC line started.

My MGC is set up with lubicle black in the core and a mix of QiYi M-Lube and Silk on the pieces. 

 Unlike what the review mentions, this cube is actually around 56mm, about the size of the YueXiao pro.  

 The puzzle is indeed very fast and magnets are somewhat noticeable. The plastic does seem to be very soft and plush, and the cube has a very quiet and muted sound. The cube has no resemblance to most moyu cubes in terms of plastic feel. 

 Turning this cube is an absolute joy. Even without lube, this cube manages to retain very smooth and tactile turning, even with the presence of magnets, which serve to further control this cube. It's like a more compact and blocky Valk power, and kinda like a softer version of the TangLong. However, the MGC has a more tactile and crunchy (still soft) feeling, which for me is a good thing. Not to mention, the feeling of the cube doesn't severely change once lube wears out, which is a big plus. 

 I have yet to experience any lockups, twists, or pops on this cube. However, overshooting can happen when you first pick it up. You get used to it after 20 or so solves. However, if you aren't into very fast cubes, I would give this cube a pass and look at its more controllable cousin the YueXiao Pro.  

 As for my own experience with this cube, I'm very happy with my MGC, and bumped my YueXiao Pro down to backup main status. I love the tactile nature of this puzzle, and the primary internals just look amazing. I'm pretty sure this cube isn't leaving my main list anytime soon.

review_title: YJ NEVER CEASES TO AMAZE ME
review_text: It seems to me like every time I buy a cheap or expensive cube from YJ it is suuuuuper good and normally at reasonable prices. This is such a good Megaminx and a good upgrade from my old D-Fantix. 5 stars!

The Yuhu is interesting, it came out during the dayan time and was considered not great even on a budget. Interestingly now the v2 and Dayan v2 came out during the Covid era of cubing. But it is definitely deserving of the v2 name. The Yuhu v2 is a compact mega with interesting circular ridges that have great and cinsistent grip that doesn't feel like it hinders your turning. Compared to old megas like the galaxy v2 where the ridges were so small that your fingers actually may be to big. You won't find that problem here. It has a large and very round grip that feels amazing to hold.  Out of the box however it actually felt like it was gonna flop like the first yuhu. It was very dry, had uneven tensions and worst off all barely any magnetic speed. It felt terrible, but after hearing it was great after setup I decided to give it a fair shot. And I'm really glad I did, the setup was a a angstrom setup with Mystic  instead off dnm-37 to give a super smooth feel. After break in it now has great balance between speed and magnet strength. And after some tension adjustments it became very close to an ideal mega. But I actualyl wouldn't recommend it to everyone. As stated previously, this mega takes a lot of time to setup which means it can be difficult for inexperienced cubers to understand what is wrong or how to fix it. For new cuber's I would recommned the Dayan Megaminx v2 instead since it feels amazing out of the box. Having that said I would recommend the Yuhu to people who want A megaminx that is moderately fast with subtle magnets and large size. Or for anyone who wants a great Megaminx but maybe don't have the money for a Gan or dayan v2. Which honestly all perform about equal but has different qualities. It has the best price to performance and is the safest bet for anyone who wants a megaminx as you aren't risking overspending on a Dayan or Gan. The main Selling point is the price to performance after all.

Simply superb 4x4. It will not hinder you in any way; it is just as useable as any other flagship, and far cheaper.  

 Dry OotB but gets better immediately. I don't setup my cubes until I've broken them in a bit and for me at least the problem fixed itself, I only had to re-lube about a week and a bit in. People tend to go overboard with their setups as soon as they get their cubes for some reason, I encourage you to allow the cube to come into itself a bit before you drown it in lube. You can't break it in properly when it's coated in Silk and Martian and all the other things you guys bathe the plastic in. 

 Tensions were fine OotB. Inner pieces pop occasionally but not often enough to be a problem. Have never experienced any unusually persistent lock-ups myself, I assume those that have are operating on a far looser setting. Cube comes with two sets of spare springs: stronger and weaker. I've tried them all and prefer the ones it comes with. 

 Inner layer magnets are stronger than outer layer ones, which makes those double-M slices super easy. Spare magnets are included of both strengths, though not many.  

 Size is fine, and the cube is quite light, which is nice. I will never understand the mindset that a 1mm size difference is at all significant, as I can achieve my average (sub-40) no matter the cube size, but some people do, and I guess that's down to hand size. If you have smaller hands, are an elite, high-level competitor, and are hypercritical about your hardware, *maybe* consider buying a different cube. If not, I wouldn't worry about it.  

 I bought both stickered and stickerless versions to test them out. No noticeable difference in terms of feel. Sticker shades are fine, I struggle to tell apart red and orange usually, but had no complaints here. 

 Overall, if you're thinking about buying your first decent 4x4, buy this one. If you're reading cubicle reviews to inform your decision, that's of course fine, but you probably don't need a more expensive puzzle than this. A five-star cube with no significant drawbacks that can be customised significantly to your liking. It's perfect for improvement, and perfect for getting yourself hooked on the event.

This cube is amazing, it's extremely stable for a 4x4, very controllable, and has very quick outer and inner layers. Corner cutting is decent, could be better but won't stop you from getting fast times with the cube. The outer layers can corner cut with an entire edge piece misaligned, the top layer can corner cut down the middle when misaligned by 3/4 of an edge piece, and the center layers can corner cut when misaligned by half of a center piece. The cube comes with fairly strong magnets that certainly help the cube's stability and controllability. Out of the box, tensions are a bit tight so be sure to use the provided screw driver to adjust them to your liking. Lastly, out of the box, the cube is very dry and scratchy when turning. This can be fixed by adding lube into the cube. On mine, I put weight 5 on the pieces and now turning the cube feels amazing. I would recommend this cube to people with a decent amount of experience in 4x4, specifically people averaging under a minute looking for an upgrade to drop their times further on a budget. If you're just starting 4x4 for the first time, I would advice getting the MFJS Meilong instead due to it's greater appeal to beginner's and quality for its price.

review_title: I've had this cube for 1 month
review_text:
Out of the box, my cube had medium-tight tensions and it was fast. There was quite a bit of friction in between the layers, but after loosening it a little and adding 8 drops of Lubest XMT, the layers were much easier to turn and it had a smooth feel. The magnets on the cube are very strong. I have not experienced a "5x5 style lockup" or pops on this cube. As long as you have a light turning style and let the magnets do their thing, catching and lockups are nonexistent. I can definitely achieve a high TPS on this cube with no problem. The cube feels solid and premium; it doesn't feel airy and it certainly doesn't feel cheap. I recommend it on medium-tight tensions with a fast lube. 
 If you're looking for the best possible 5x5, you cannot go wrong with the MGC.

Corner cutting is pretty standard, it has a maximum of just past 1 piece, in both reverse and normal corner cutting. The greatest feature of this cube is its magnets. The magnets help to slow down the cube when turning outer layers. In the event of a pop, the magnets would help you to reassemble this cube. It is definitely worth the price, even without a discount code/sale. it's worth it. If you want a basic cube for a lower price, this isn't your go-to, but if you are looking for a very nice and premium feeling cube for a reasonable price, buy it. I would definitely recommend this to be used with DNM 37
  
 Overall, this cube is great if you want a premium feeling 5x5 for a reasonable price, that performs well. If you want a very budget magnetic 5x5, consider something a little cheaper.

review_title: Excellent cube still plagued by YJ's QC
review_text:
This cube is really really good. At least it was after about 400 solves. I'd sum it up as a much more solid and slightly clunkier cousin of the RS3M v5, which it shares its piece design philosophy with. I'd say it's better than that cube because despite the extra heft, it doesn't feel like it's about to crumble under your fingertips like the v5. All in all, turning is fluid albeit slightly hampered by the strong magnets. 

 Overall the cube has moderately hard plastic that has a deep sound and a hint of softness that comes with the cube being quite hollow. It's blocky and pretty stable, although most of the blockiness comes from the reverse corner cutting. At higher compressions (where I believe it works best), the reverse corner cutting is effortless up to a point, before becoming quite harsh. Forwards corner cutting ranges from effortless to fairly snappy depending on the compression setting. Piece magnets are definitely on the stronger side and definitely noticeable, while the core magnets are there but not super prominent.  

 The whole QC issue I and a couple of others have had stems from poor quality moulding of the edge feet. After about 30 solves, this issue reared its ugly head in the form of horrible scratchiness at the beginning and end of each turn. If this happens to you, either return the cube or just push through until it finally breaks in. The issue doesn't seem extremely common, but it is something to be aware of. 

 Overall, I like how it turns and it's definitely a cube I recommend to people looking for a controllable and blocky cube. You can check out my section on it in my comparison video linked below:

product_name: YJ MGC3 Beta 3x3 (8-Magnet Ball-Core + UV Coated + MagLev)
review_text: For a midrange cube, the beta is very good. This is the best YJ 3x3 ever. However I’ve only had this cube for about 3 days, already have around 1,000 solves and the UV coating has already started flaking. I’ve had this happen on higher quality cubes such as my WRM V9 but that cube has over 13,000 solves and it just barely visible on a couple sides where the beta is flaking on almost every side. This cube has a super satisfying turning feel when set up, and I’ve gotten close to PB numbers in the limited time I’ve had to use it, however the quality control leaves a lot to be desired. YJ has introduced a new feeling as far as midrange priced cubes go, and as someone who’s used the RS3 v5 (in my opinion the main competitor in this price range) I prefer the softer plastic feeling and speed of this cube. But with quality I’ve seen so far, it makes it a tough recommendation.

This 5x5 is my new main 5x5.  It has a light and buttery smooth feel with lockups being very rare due to its very good corner cutting.  The magnets keep the cube in a relatively cubic shape while you are executing algorithms, as well as stopping the pieces from separating as you turn them.  One of the few downfalls this cube comes with is the amount of lube it comes with out of the box.  This thing is soaked in lube when you first receive it, but once you do a couple solves to work the lube out and wipe it off, this cube is incredible.  I would highly recommend this to anyone who needs a new 5x5, especially one on a good price-point.  The magnets aren't incredible strong, which helps the flow during the 3x3 stage for me, but some people may prefer them to be a bit stronger.  Although lockups are rare, you can occasionally get pretty bad ones where the cube deforms.
 Overall, not a perfect 10/10 rating but it's pretty dang close. 

 PROS:
 speed,
 good flow during algs,
 corner cutting,
 price,
 stability,
 buttery smooth feel,
 pieces don't wobble around,
 incredible 3x3 stage. 

 Cons:
 comes covered in lube,
 magnets could be a little stronger on inner layers, but they aren't that bad.

review_title: FINALLY I CAN PROVE TO MY BLIND BUDDY THAT I’M FASTER THAN HIM!
review_text:
Ohhh the days of my visually impaired cubing friend setting WR solves over and over again… no matter what I do, they always win at solving the Rubik’s Cube. 

 NOW!! Finally, I have a Rubik’s cube that I can beat them with! No more “I’m finished” a microsecond after starting the timer; no more “your colored vision impairs you, you slow poor cuber”. Since I’ve received the puzzle my friend still beats me, but at least it’s fair now! 

 The puzzle has mediocre turning, an okay speed turning feel, and quite good turning if your accuracy is acute. Beside that, I’m comfortable with saying this is a blast to solve, and I’ve had ZERO issues. In annexation, it has no stickers to peel off, and instead, marvelous textured-tiles to enhance the view when you’re not solving it; at least for me, and not my blind friend.  

 Until GAN or YJ’s pet, MoYu, makes one, this is the five-star puzzle to bargain for!

review_title: Interesting Concept, Can Be Improved on V2
review_text:
Very tight and dry out of the box.  When I go and set it up, the screw was screwed in very tight.  I had to use some force to get them loose.  Spring noise was very loud but goes away after you lube it with Weight 5.  Once set up, it feels great.  I used Silk on the piece and tracks.   

 They can improve the accent on the heart and star shape.  They both feel almost the same to the touch.  I do believe they should only use shapes that feels the same in whatever orientation they're in and more different to each other.  Heart and 5-sided star will not fit this bill.  I do believe cyoubx already suggested the better shapes for them.  I haven't been able to solve them yet for this reason.  Too much ambiguity in the feel of which piece is which.  I will keep trying and train my finger tips to better identify the pieces.  Also, I'm not blind so, I'm just in it for the challenge. 

 One more thing that can be improved for v2.  Magnets.  It will help a lot in the alignment when you're blind solving.  Maybe I'll magnet mod it once I figure out if the pieces can be separated safely.

review_title: To buy or not buy? You choose!
review_text: So yes, I did eventually fall for the hype and got myself a QiYi ball-core 2x2! Now, I love my ball-cores, however I barely felt anything there, Honestly, if you can resist the hype around this cube, just get the base magnetic version. $2 (in my case, around £1.50) isn't much, but there's really nothing to add with the ball-core. As for the cube, it's decent. However, in every 2x2, there's a set of hidden edge pieces that stabilise the cube, 3 of them attached to a corner so the inner edge pieces don't catch. Now with some 2x2s, when you twist this corner, your 2x2 is cooked. However, I do feel quite confident twisting that things and the 2x2 should stay intact. The dual-adjustment on this cube is weird. Bare weird. Tightness is just adjusted with a screw, but compression is adjusted with a quite confusing tool. Also, settings 4 and 5 make the cube too tight and 1 and 2 make the cube too loose, so I'm stuck on setting 3 and a decently loose cube. This is the only tension on this cube that feels about right for me. Also, the turning feels ever so slightly sandy and those fixed hidden edges keep on catching. How ironic, that the solution to catching in a cube makes the cube catchy. For a beginner cuber? Great! For a pro? Or even a super fast Ortega solver? Or even a cuber who just likes experimentation? Not the best.

review_text:
Superb 6x6. Main pros: SUPER good price, good corner cutting, it's very swishy and airy. Its a solid cube. it feels great to solve on and I could see myself putting a lot of time into 6x6 as an event now.  

 Here are some notes I have about this cube.  

 I have gotten a few internal lockups where the cube doesnt look like its catching on anything from the outside but it's locked on the inside. I wouldn't call it major but I also wouldn't call it minor. I think it was a tensioning error since I haven't had it happen again once I tightened the cube slightly.  

 Main downsides: Too much lube from the factory. Its gross and unnecessary. The cube actually turns better without it and I really wish QiYi took the latest YJ and Moyu approach of just shipping cubes bone dry.  

 Also this cube is a lot more flexible than the warrior M 7x7. I find myself having to be a bit more careful with how I turn this cube, while I can turn the warrior 7x7 with a lot more confidence. I totally understand this is just how 6x6 is going to be due to the mechanism.  

 The magnets could be stronger too. And its a big deal for me to complain about strong magnets. I've been cubing since before magnetic cubes existed and usually my complaints about modern cubes are that the magnets are too strong. Not on this cube. They're a bit weak, which definitely harms stability.  

 Overall this cube is a solid 8.7/10. It would be a 9/10 if the magnets were stronger.

What I mean by this is that even if there are a lot of magnets you can't really feel them and the plastic feels like cheap plastic. I got this cube as a free bonus $3 mystery puzzle with an order, and for such a low price, it is a great cube.  Even though it is a budget cube, it's still a big step up in quality from a rubik's brand cube.  It is light, adjustable, turns easily, and can corner cut about 30 degrees.  It would make a good beginner cube for someone on a tight budget who wants to try out speed cubing and see if it's for them, or it can be a nice addition to a growing cube collection if you get it as a mystery puzzle.

For a $4 puzzle, the QiYi Sail W does all that you should expect and more. It has a fun "clicky" feel that I've missed since my MoYu Weilong from 2015 and has a performance that rivals the RS3M. In fact, I actually prefer the Sail W.  I've spent some time breaking in the puzzle and I've gathered a few pros and cons: 

 Pros:
 -This puzzle is fast out of the box. I haven't messed with tensions as I was very satisfied with the feel of the cube almost immediately.  I used a small amount of Cubicle Silk in mine and it has still retained its speed. 

 -The stickers are vibrant and easily discernable. The darker blue threw me off for a little bit, but I got used to it quick enough. I've done a couple hundred solves on this puzzle and haven't had any issues with the stickers peeling. 

 -The overall quality of the puzzle is great. The feel isn't luxurious, but it certainly does not come off as poor or flimsy. 

 Cons:
 -The puzzle is not magnetic. This is not to say that magnets are expected in a puzzle this cheap. However, it's hard to ignore when other cubes have the feature at a slightly higher price point.  

 -The puzzle is loud. I wouldn't entirely consider this a con as I do enjoy the feeling of louder cubes. The springs were a bit noisy early on, but some Silk fixed that.  

 Final Impressions: Should this be your first speed cube? It could, but I think there are better options. Realistically thinking, this puzzle is not going to have the same longevity of quality and performance of a cube such as the RS3M. Additionally the Sail W's lack of magnets immediately puts it a few steps behind all of it's competitors, which is why I wouldn't recommend this from a competitive standpoint. All this being said, I do strongly believe that there are a few examples where the Sail may be perfect for you: 

 1. This cube is really cheap, making it a great cube for when you are out and about for hikes, trips, etc. 

 2. It is easy to justify spending a few extra dollars on your main puzzle, but sometimes putting much money into a competition warmup cube is a bit much. The Sail W is a great option because it's speed is comparable to many flagships. It's also far less painful to spend $4 dollars on a warmup puzzle than another $20+. 

 3. Everyone get's bored of solving the same 3x3 over and over eventually. If you are looking to diversify your collection on a budget, the Sail offers a unique feeling that makes casual solves more enjoyable. 

 4. Over time, many cubers will have friends/ family that will gain interest in puzzles and want to take a step towards speed solving. This puzzle makes for an easy gift. 

 Great puzzle, great price, definitely worth the buy.

I'm an old cuber (an old geezer at 27) and I missed out on the Rubik's Clock when I first got into speed cubing and twisty puzzles almost half of my life ago. I feel like it was a more widespread puzzle back then but I never got the chance to purchase one. So when I saw this newly released Clock, made with an elegant design including magnets, I knew I had to finally experience this puzzle. 

 This Clock is beautifully manufactured with a sleek color scheme: black and white and hints of red. My biggest concern when purchasing was not being sure if the plastic bottom was an attached piece, or a separate stand. I really wanted it to be a separate stand, and indeed it is a completely separate piece only used for displaying, such as on a shelf. The movement of the gears is very smooth, with the magnets adding a nice feel and (I'm guessing) improved gear alignment for the push pins in the middle. I noticed a piece of dust under the clear plastic front so I took it apart to see if I could clean it out. All you need is a small Phillips screwdriver. While it did kind of explode all over the place when I separated the inner two frame pieces of black and white, I had a blast putting it all back together, sans piece of dust. The magnets are not loose, they seem to be snug in their places without being able to loosen and fall out. 

 When I was a kid, anytime I got a new puzzle I would rush to watch the tutorials on youtube. Not that there is anything wrong with that, but I wanted to savor the feeling of exploring new puzzle territory completely blind with this new Clock. The designs of the dials are very detailed and make the lingao feel tacky. This revolutionizes clock just like the Square-1 did a few years ago.

This puzzle is amazing! I used the Qiyi clock to get a sub 4 average officially, I’m amazed with the amount of magnets in this puzzle! If you’re going to start clocking definitely get this puzzle, it’s definitely worth the money

Here are the good things about the puzzle. There are actually magnets in the dials, so there is feedback on every turn you do. This means that you never get any lockups due to the pins not being exactly aligned with the hour markings, because the magnets prevent that from happening. The turning resistance is still there when there are 3 or more pins up (and you're turning the corresponding dials), but compared to other clocks on the market, it is much much less especially doing the turn. Only the force required to get the dial spinning is comparably resistive. When doing long sessions with this clock, you don't get nearly as tired out or exhausted compared to other clocks. This is mostly due to how relatively light the actual turning is over. And finally, out of the box this clock is perfect and ready to go. This is literally unheard of for any other clock.  

 Some bad things. The sides of the plastic casing isn't flattened out, like the shengshou, so you can get some rolling when setting it down. The turning is a bit too light, so you can overshoot. However, the biggest drawback is that the pins are too light. You can get them to swap sides by just shaking the clock a bit forcefully, and you can accidently push them down during inspection.  

 In summary,  this clock is amazing and you will not regret buying it. Out of the box it is literally lightyears ahead of any other clock, and you don't even need to set it up. The first solve I did out of the box was a 6.96, and I averaged mid 8 with the shengshou. My ranking of all the clocks on the market would go like this: Qiyi > magnetic lingao > shengshou > lingao

 I held my first Megaminx back in the 80's. The early Megaminxes were fun to solve, but popping was a regular issue. When i let my interest in cubing fade in the late 90`s the Megaminx had yet to see any major changes in design to deal with the problem. In fact it seemed the entire range of twisty puzzles had been frozen in time and little or nothing seemed to have been done to help improve the Megaminx or any of its more famous cousins.  

 in the 90's the era of graphic user interface in personal computers had arrived ,and many puzzlers ,like myself, gravitated tward this new phase of technology. And it seemed that puzzles like the Megaminx, Rubik`s Cube and Pyraminx et al, would be fond memories that would only be reacquainted with through key chain versions and the rare puzzle or two that would pop up on store shelves every so often . That is until the age of 3D printing came to light. People searched for things to make with this new technology. Eventually, someone decided to print a Rubik`s Cube, and then the second age of twisty puzzles was begun. 

 This Megaminx is not your father's Megaminx. It does not pop, there are no stickers to replace or glue back on. The turning is smooth as ice. The sculpted pieces make for a non-slip

review_title: Everything From QiYi is Literally Speedsolvable
review_text: I know, I tend to review WCA puzzles and I just bought a 2x2x3 for the sake of the non-WCA collection. Here's the thing, this is not your typical non-WCA puzzle that you're playing around with that does not turn well. This puzzle is from QiYi, which means their build quality for their puzzles is very unheard of. In terms of speedcubes, they perform well and everything you expect in a popular brand. Non-WCA? Well, yes because since they are so used to making good puzzles from cheapest to the most expensive that they can build a 2x2x3 and other puzzles that can turn nicely without any effort. That is the case with this puzzle. The shades are very nice and what's crazy about this 2x2x3 compared to others is the ability to speed cube with. One reason why the cube is speedsolvable is they kind of borrowed the mechanism from their 2x2s that had anti-pop technology and they modified it. Another reason why they are speedsolvable is the use of screws and springs, so they can cornercut very nicely. Finally, they have track designs that made the cube very easy to turn. With all of that reasons that made the 2x2x3 a good cube for speedsolving, I had a personal best of 2.35 seconds and averaging sub-9 seconds. If you are looking for a non-WCA puzzle, this is the one to purchase.

review_title: Lighter Meilong v2m for cheap but Qiyi
review_text:
After ordering it from different platforms I finally received it yesterday.
 When the postman handed the package to me I was surprised how light it was.
 After unboxing it looks as light as a feather. The budget cubes from Qiyi are prelubed and ready to go, but this one felt bone dry and scratchy, out of the box.
 It's very light, less than 60 grams and due to it, it's turning is completely effortless. I added 2 drops of Qiyi m lube to its internals and 1 to the piece and after breaking in the lube it was amazing. As I had also recently found a warrior w and have a warrior m pro and several warrior s, it was time to actually compare it's piece design with it's predecessors and the rival meilong v2.
 In the pic from left to right are: Warrior w, warrior s, warrior m pro, warrior m uv and meilong 3mv2 uv.
 Meilongs and Warriors have always been the same cube from different companies and you can swap pieces between them. Looking designwise, the piece design of warrior m goes back towards the warrior w rather than it's direct predecessor warrior s, but they're grooves on the pieces as in modern cubes for withholding lube. The pieces are also identical to the meilong v2m piece design except for the different pattern and being lower weight. However the center caps are different and and aren't compatible with either the meilong or warrior m pro. Also warrior m pro is a completely different cube and it's only similarity is the name and company. 

 It's magnets are fairly weak but due to the paper thin plastic it works. Frankly speaking its very similar to the meilong v2m in turning but lighter. The UV coating also feels premium and hopefully it's scratch resistant.  By its surface, turning and UV coating it doesn't feel cheap, but to me it's very light weight throws me off as if it's a cheap cube. It is cheap but in a good way.
 Overall, I would suggest it as a first cube if you're an adult but as a second or third cube if you're a child as I don't think it would survive a child's tantrum if it's knocked around a bit.
