I'll start with the tldr: this is a fantastic cube. It is smooth, has great corner cutting and is incredibly stable and it will make any cuber at any level happy. 
 In more detail, this cube has both positives and negatives as all cubes do. Starting with the positives, it feels amazing. Just turning it is so crunchy, satisfying and smooth and it truly as highly addictive as advertised. Coming from the rs3m V5, it feels so much more premium and elegant and it makes the rs3m V5 feel so cheap that I can't use it consistently anymore. Basically every positive thing that CubeHead and the Cubicle had to say about this cube is true. The cornercutting is one of the best I've seen although it may be a bit snappy and the UV coating on the cube is fantastic (although this is a given considering moyu has great UV coating). The autoalignment is so natural and instead of being so noticeable it can get in the way like it was on the GAN 12, it just makes sure that everything you aren't controlling when turning is where it should be and that you never over shoot your turn.
 Now going onto the negatives of this cube it definitely has some flaws that may be a dealbreaker for some people. Firstly, it has that half blocky feel of the stock moyu v11. I've tried a few v11s with different setups and settings and the feryoocore v2 is definitely not as blocky as them but it still does have that snappy feel that the stock v11s have. Some people really like it including me, some people don't but this cube is in that middle ground where it may either end up pleasing everyone or no-one. Secondly, I'm not the biggest fan of the setup this version of the cube comes with. It is such a naturally fast cube that adding such fast lubes in mystic, stealth and dignitas almost feels wrong. With that being said, the feel that the cube has is exactly how CubeHead described it where it is fast and controllable, it is just that I personally don't think it fits this cube well. For me, I added some pilube blue 10k and lubest xmt just for that gumminess and it felt so much better and I started to average faster than I did on my previous main. Finally, the magnet strength is incredibly strong. Not just "ah there is a bump" strong, but "OH THERE IS A BUMP" strong, especially when the cube is completely dry. Once lubed, as Phil said in the overview video, the magnet strength becomes manageable but I will say it is still pretty strong. Because of the magnets, it took me some time to get use to the cube and truly become my main but once I did get use to it the magnet strength did add some well needed controllability to the cube so I guess it is a positive and a negative.
 With that being said, this is still a fantastic cube and should be a contender if you are looking for a new main and it is within your budget. CubeHead's spring and screw settings are fantastic so copy those if you are not sure, but his lube setup may be too fast, although it is also a good place to start if you are stuck on which setup to try on this cube. As critical as I was in this review I just want to say that this cube is definitely my new main, it beats any GAN 16, GAN V100 or V11 and I can guarantee that if you get this cube and you set it up well, you will enjoy it a lot even if it does not become your main right away.

review_title: Feryoocore V2 UV — CubeHead’s Setup vs. the Standard Ferrocore V2
review_text:
To start, I own the Feryoocore V1, four Ferrocore V2 UVs, and the Steven’s Signature Ferrocore V2. Now, with the Feryoocore V2 UV, that brings my total to seven Ferrocores overall—six V2s and one V1. So, it goes without saying that I absolutely love this cube. It is definitely my main. 

 To give some perspective, I’m not really a speedcuber. I mainly attend speedcubing events to have fun. I use this cube because of how smooth it is. It rarely snags, even with my bad turning. 

 I decided to make the Ferrocore my main partly because it finally let me stop buying other cubes. Some cubes are great, while others are just… not so great. Personally, I prefer the regular Ferrocore V2 exactly how it comes right out of the box. I didn’t need to adjust anything. 

 The Feryoocore is set up to CubeHead’s specific preferences, and I like it as well, but I still prefer the standard Ferrocore V2 a little more. 

 Overall, I would definitely recommend this cube. Great quality, great design, and perfect turning.

The MoYu Ferrocore V2 UV is honestly one of the most satisfying cubes I have used. The turning feels incredibly smooth, but it still has a small amount of feedback that makes every turn feel controlled and responsive instead of overly soft or taut. The corner cutting is also very impressive, consistently cutting around 40–45 degree angles with very few lockups, even at higher TPS. Because of this, the cube feels extremely forgiving during solves and handles imperfect turning very well. 

 One of the best parts of this cube is the balance between speed and stability. Compared to some premium GAN cubes that can sometimes feel too fast or flexible, the Ferrocore V2 feels much more stable while still being quick and effortless to turn. The slight "tug" during corner cuts also adds a really satisfying feel that makes it hard to stop solving on, which is probably why people describe it as "highly addictive." 

 The Yoo setup from The Cubicle is a great middle ground. The tensions, compression, and lube combination make the cube feel balanced and stable without relying too heavily on strong magnets or an overly tight setup. It also has a wide range of customization, so you can make it tighter for more control or looser for a faster feel depending on your preference. 

 For around $70 USD with the Yoo setup ($60 USD for no set up), the Ferrocore V2 honestly feels like one of the best value flagship cubes currently available. Compared to some more expensive premium cubes, especially certain GAN models, it delivers a smoother and more forgiving experience while still feeling extremely high end. 

 Overall, I would easily give this cube a 5/5. It combines smooth turning, strong corner cutting, stability, and customization into a cube that feels both premium and very enjoyable to solve on.

review_title: Very good, but definitely not for everyone
review_text:
I like this cube, but I do not love it, and that's a sort of painful error to make given the price.  

 I want to clarify where I'm coming from so you can understand the rest of this review. I turn very lightly and prefer cubes as fast as possible. My previous main is the wrm v10 ball core maglev on 2/2 settings with only xmt10 in it. That will be my primary point of comparison.  

 I played with the settings with this cube a bunch and ended up on 1 tension, 2 elasticity, again with just xmt10. The tighter settings just make the cube feel blocky and unpleasant to me. Performance wise I have no complaints. No pops, no catches, no issues with over or under turning, no corner twists and smooth turning. Basically what you would expect from a modern flagship. I also really appreciate having a solid core that I know won't break on me, the grey internals look sick, and the UV coat is nice as it usually is with Moyu.  

 So features and performance out of the way, I'm going to talk about the feel of the cube, which is where my complaints lie.  

 Compared to the wrm v10, the force required to turn a face is noticably lower. In fact, it almost feels like the cube is pulling you along rather than simply assisting you, which is a very unique feeling that I'm not really sure I like. It's kind of like as soon as you commit to a turn it's already finishing it for you. In other words the cube feels "opinionated." 
 On the other hand, what I'm almost certain I do not like are the magnets. They are not kidding when they say this has "stronger magnets"; these are the strongest I have ever felt in a 3x3, and combined with the otherwise smooth and light turning it makes each turn end with a distinct "thud" as the magnets yank the layers into alignment.  

 This is a thing you experience with any ball core that's actually doing its job, but it is VERY noticable here, to an extent I don't personally enjoy. I cannot stress enough how much you feel the magnets in this cube. It's kind of like the inner layers of the aosu v7 triple track.  

 Alongside that there's also a clackiness to the cube that doesn't suit my taste. You can constantly hear and feel the pieces bumping into each other as you turn. Combined with the significant spring noise this thing comes with out of the box, it is the loudest cube I've owned in years. You can probably make it way quieter by tightening it and putting heavier/slower lubes in it, but I personally can't stand setups like that, so it's loud or nothing for me.  

 Basically, if you like your cubes to feel smooth, quiet and gently assistive, this is not the cube for you. This is for people who want something clacky, tactile, and strongly assistive.
As a big Gan 12 maglev fan this cube is hands down even better to another level.  Wow. Buttery and no lockups! I like it so much I ordered a second one.   Amazing design by the whole Cubicle team.

review_title: MoYu AoSu V7 Double-Track Matte Special Edition Review
review_text:
Before I dive into this review, I want to mention that I already own three regular AoSu V7 Double-Track cubes (excluding this Matte version) and a Single-Track version. I’ll be directly comparing this special edition to those. 

 Out of the box, the AoSu V7 Double-Track Matte was very fast, dry, scratchy, and extremely uncontrollable. This changed drastically after tensioning, and even before any lubrication. The turning immediately stood out: it was insanely light, much easier to perform slice moves than any of my other AoSu V7s. The magnet strength (both outer and inner layers) felt more subtle compared to the regular Double-Track and Single-Track versions, but still pronounced enough to keep turning clean. 

 This is very close to what my dream 4x4 would turn like. On the standard Double-Track and Single-Track versions, slice moves required a lot more force, and I experienced more catches. On the Matte Special Edition, these problems were gone — slice moves are much lighter, and I catch far less. After only a few dozen solves, I even managed to break my personal best with a sub-35 second single, which says a lot about the cube’s potential. 

 Physically, the cube is slightly lighter, weighing 98g compared to the regular Double-Track’s 99g — likely because of the lack of UV coating. But the "lighter" feeling isn't just about weight: the turning itself is physically easier. Movements feel effortless compared to the standard editions. 

 In terms of stability, I initially experienced a few catches simply because of how fast the cube was, but no major lockups or pops occurred during solves. It feels reliable. 

 Now for the finish: I’m a huge fan of matte and satin finishes. The cube looks much more premium, especially when you consider that many puzzles today come with high price tags. I didn’t notice any meaningful difference in grip during solves compared to UV-coated versions. However, the Matte version looks much cleaner and sophisticated in my eyes. MoYu nailed the aesthetic here, and I hope they start offering more non-UV versions in the future, also using this cleaner logo. 

 Pros:
 Incredibly fast and light turning 

 Easier slice moves than regular Double-Track and Single-Track versions 

 Premium matte finish with clean logo 

 Subtle but effective magnet strength 

 No major lockups or pops 

 Cons:
 Might be too fast out of the box for some people (needs setup) 

 Final Verdict:
 The AoSu V7 Double-Track Matte Special Edition is easily my new main — it's the perfect choice for anyone who wants a fast, light-turning 4x4 that looks and feels premium right out of the box.

review_title: From old DaYan Zhanchi to modern magnetic cubes — what a difference
review_text:
This is my first magnetic cube, and I honestly wasn’t sure what to expect. I was initially planning to get the Weilong V11 for a comeback to cubing, but the Ferrocore V2 came out at the perfect time. After reading many reviews describing it as an improved version, I decided to give it a try, and I’m really glad I did. 

 Coming from an old DaYan Zhanchi 5 (stickered and white internals version, the one with the purple box back in the day), with no ball core, no magnets, and when torpedoes were considered advanced technology at the time, the magnetic feel of the Ferrocore V2 was a bit strange at first. However, after just a few solves, it quickly felt natural and very satisfying, and it really helps with control and overall stability. 

 This cube exceeded my expectations. It feels like a huge upgrade in every way — faster, smoother, and more controllable (obviously). At first, I thought it was expensive for what it offered, assuming the price was mostly due to its features. But when I held it, I immediately felt a very “premium” kind of feel (I have the matte version). As soon as you pick it up, you can tell it’s not a cheap cube. 

 Performance-wise, even at its most extreme settings, it never feels too loose (I haven’t had a single corner twist in a week of daily use) nor too tight and rigid — it still feels incredibly fast. It really feels like a perfect balance between speed and control. 

 Overall, this cube has made coming back to cubing incredibly enjoyable. I highly recommend it to anyone. If you’re coming from older non-magnetic cubes, be aware that the magnets are quite strong and may feel surprising at first — but you’ll get used to them very quickly.

review_title: Great skewb! Hard to set up
review_text: I got this skewb a while ago. It was sandy out of the box (just like all Moyu cubes), but that went away after a while. This is a great skewb. There are no problems with it. It performs great, is customizable, and doesn’t pop. However, I started having trouble when I started to lube it after a few months. What would happen is the Lubicle Speedy and Dnm I put in there would get trapped in the corners that don’t have the little holes, and somehow that just made the skewb super slow. After trying multiple times, I found that it’s best to just put DNM in there. No speedy. Of course, that’s the only 2 lubes I have, so if you have others, try those out. I also attempted to core lube it with weight 5, and that was actually a success. It stopped all spring noise and made the cube feel smoother. I opened the center caps, took the weight 5, got the tip of the lube  below the dual adjustment thing, and then injected some lube in there. However, make sure to get all your tensions settled. Once you put the lube in there it doesn’t make a sound when you adjust it.

review_title: MoYu RS3 V5: Simple, Fast, and Worth It
review_text:
When I opened the MoYu RS3 V5, the unboxing was simple with just basic accessories—and that’s enough. The small robot stand looks reallycool and unique. 

 Out of the box, the cube felt rough and sandy, but after adding some weight 3 lube, it turned smooth and fast. The medium magnets and the ball core make it very stable. 

 I used to main the Tornado V3, but the RS3 V5 is better. My average solve time dropped by about 1 second. You don’t have to change much— I left the screws as they were and only adjusted the blue elasticity dial once, and that was optional. 

 Though not highly customizable, this cube performs great right away. It feels just as good as many expensive GAN cubes, but costs less. Some say it breaks easily, but mine is holding up well. 

 I’d recommend the RS3 V5 to anyone who likes MoYu or GAN cubes and wants a reliable, fast/stable cube for a good price.

product_name: MoYu RS3 M V5 3x3 (Ball Core UV + Robot Cube Stand)
review_text:
This cube is really good but there are a few things you should look out for. 

 Pros: It is very fast and controllable at the same time. The UV coating is super grippy, so you will never lose your grip. The Dual Adjustment system is very easy and simple to understand. The Maglev makes the cube fast but doesn't make it overshoot and uncontrollable like some Gan cubes. The corner cutting is great. Some might say cutting 45 degrees on this cube is a bit hard, but for me, the corner cutting is flawless. It can basically forward cut any reasonable angle you can experience in normal solves, and the reverse cutting is also really good. You're essentially getting a cube with all the features a flagship (like the Gan 16, or Super Weilong V2) has for a really, really good price at only $25. Also, the Robot Cube Stand is also a nice addition. 

 Cons: OOTB, it feels dry and sandy, but after setup with any smooth lubes like Mystic or FZ calm, it is no longer a problem. You have to be very careful with this cube. The pieces, especially the corners, are prone to splitting if you drop it, but if you have protection like a bag, then it is not a problem. This Con is really only for me because I don't think anyone has experienced this problem. My cube's auto-alignment isn't great. I know it has a ball core which helps with auto-alignment, but for some reason, it just doesn't seem to work. I think this problem is only for my cube, so yours probably won't have this problem. 

 All in all, this cube is absolutely fantastic. I would definitely recommend this cube to any cuber, whether you are a beginner or professional. Also, if you're not great at setting up cubes, I highly recommend using some FZ Calm on the tracks, some Angstrom Dignitas and any fast lube on the pieces for a great, all-round feel and performance

review_text:
This cube features a very tactile smooth yet kinda crunchy feel the cube is priced very fairly and is a great release. The cube lacked a lot of corner cutting and fluidity ootb but that is fixable with setup. My set up is as follows 
 Loosed the spring by 180 degrees on all sides 
 Use the tool to turn the system for 2 clicks on all sides 
 Apply dignitas to the tracks of 2 pieces 
 Break in for abt 5 solves 
 Apply 3 drops of fz rush on the pieces 
 Break in for around 10 solves and it’s done :)
 I average around 11 and this cube has helped me maintain and get more confident during solves. The uv coating workes very well and it helps in comps. In total nothing wiring with this cube and it’s prob my net main for oh and 2 handed:)

product_name: MoYu RS3 M V5 3x3 (Ball Core UV + Robot Cube Stand)
review_text:
I've had this cube for just a few weeks now, and it can already hit sub-16.5 OH, only a second out from my main, the Guhong Pro M. The distinctly different feel from the Guhong also makes it a viable option for a competition if I ever feel that the Guhong is not performing well on the day. 

 Strengths:
 - Cheap, but with practically all the flagship features (see below)
 - UV coating helps with grip (plus shiny)
 - Simple, iconic adjustment system with reasonable OH range
 - Surprisingly light and papery feel 
 - Ball-core helps with stability
 - No adjustable magnets makes turn-feel consistent throughout 

 Weaknesses:
 - Though better than 56 mm, I think it is too close and causes me more fingertrick complications than the 54 mm Guhong
 - Weight distribution seems highly concentrated in the center ball-core (as expected), but this resulting papery feel is also something I am not used to and don't particularly enjoy
 - Need to glue to corner and edge split pieces together, or else they snap easily
 - Eats lube like crazy (good for a consistent feel during a competition though)
 - Rather loud (less enjoyable experience too) 

 Overall, the strengths definitely outweigh the weaknesses and this is an excellent OH cube with similar results to my main, the Guhong Pro M. It has slightly less enjoyable turning, but definitely a valuable purchase for anyone looking to get a budget OH cube that many also consider the best.

review_text:

product_name: MoYu RS3 M V5 3x3 (Ball Core UV + Robot Cube Stand)
review_text: For $25, this cube is amazing and I'd 100% recommend getting it. It feels like the WRM v9, but with lighter magnets and no edge alignment. This cube is perfect for me because the only problem I had with the YS3M and WRM v9 was their strong, unchangeable magnets. Out of the box, this was tight and corner cutting wasn't good, but once you loosen the screws a bit it'll be fine. This is also great for OH since it's easy to turn, has light magnets, and stays stable while turning. After just two sessions of OH, I broke all of my PB's. Even for regular 2-handed 3x3, this cube is great. I wish Moyu didn't have to sell it with the cube robot, but don't let that stop you from getting this.

product_name: MoYu RS3 M V5 3x3 (Ball Core UV + Robot Cube Stand)
review_text:
Disclaimer: I got this cube as a gift, so it won't be a verified purchase :(
 I got this cube as a gift and wasn't expecting that much from it, the most interesting thing about it I thought was going to be the weight-saving design incorporated into the pieces, but after about a week of use, I think it's an extremely viable cube for a main and I'm absolutely enamoured. Was also sceptical about the cube case, as I thought it was a tad of a gimmick, but it's honestly quite cute and I don't mind it, only a few quid and the whole cube is very reasonably priced so barely matters.
 It's really smooth, and the cube comes very tight out of the box, but once you loosen it by a turn or two each side and tighten the compression by 3 or 4 clicks, it starts to feel like a more stable WRM V9. In fact, I think it is very close in feeling to a similarly set-up V9. It's very fast, easy to get speed out of like all the other RS3Ms, and the smoothness is really great. Also very stable, but what makes me like this cube so very much is how effortless it is to turn. The weight is lovely; one of the problems I had with the YS3 was that it was rather a bit too heavy, and even thought there's a sufficiency of speed to be got from it, it hurts after a long enough solving session. This one, though, is so much lighter that it feels much more effortless and healthy. Only a few things I'd recommend one knows: a) the pieces are just a tad fragile, so don't drop it, but I mean that's the same for most cubes; b) if you have really inaccurate turning, the cube might catch a bit much, so the V9 might be better; and c) for whatever reason, the cube seems to have factory lube all over the internals, not just the feet, which makes for an unfortunate surprise. I'd strongly encourage cleaning out and then re-lubing the cube immediately, or at least cleaning the lube off the scaled surfaces (I'm not sure what causes this, I think not having skirts like the V9 allows lube to easily leak from the core but it's more pronounced than others with this design so I couldn't say). All in all though, I think this cube is hugely viable for a main, and as long as you're not extremely inaccurate in turning, for the price it's a good consideration for any cuber.

review_text:
I didn't use it out of the box, but that's because I got recommendations to set it up before using it. I lubed the core with Lubicle Black, but other core lubes will probably work just as fine. I leave the spring tension on the lowest or second lowest setting because their cubes don't have corner twisting issues and don't adjust the screws more than one 1/2 turn tighter than the factory settings. 

 This cube is the best cube I've bought this year. It's lighter than the YS3M, the magnets are weaker than the WRM V9, it doesn't have (non-core related) durability issues like the Tornado V3, doesn't catch like the GAN 13, and the Super Weilong is probably not 2.5x better than this to justify its price. 

 I did an Angstrom Setup+Fz lubes on this cube plus some thicker lube on the pieces, and this cube feels amazing. Budget cube or not, I'd recommend this cube over any other.

review_title: This is the true king of the budget cube market.
review_text: What can I say... you need to buy this cube!  I have been wanting to try a MoYu ball-core cube for a long time now, and when this one came our and all of the Cubicle staff loved it (also it was hecka cheap), I HAD to try it.  This is only the second day that I have had this cube, and I've already broken my PB single!  I went from 8.766 to and 8.280!  I am a 14-15 second average cuber, but these past two days I have been dropping down to low 13-12 seconds!  i love the UV coating on a budget cube, it is just so helpful with the grip.  The magnet strength is perfect, it's not too fast, the adjustment is straightforward and simple, and it feels AMAZING with the MAX setup!  I would say that if you get this cube, (for the new cubers out there) you should ABSOLUTELY buy some lubricant for your puzzle.  It is just a good idea overall, and helps extend the lifetime of your cube.  This is an AWESOME cube by an amazing company and I recommend it 100 out of 10 :) (and you CAN trust me, because I have tried about three quarters of the 3x3s on the market, LOL)

This cube has extremely good performance, but may need some setup depending on your turning style. OOTB it was extremely fast and the magnets were so weak that they were barely doing their job. I had to double up the magnets in the edges (I used some spare N35 4x2 magnets, but you could buy the RS3M+ kit), lube it with a more controllable Angstrom setup, then tighten the tensions and put the spring compression system on 8. The Lubicle Black on the core mostly fixed the spring noise problems that were present OOTB. The feel compared to the original RS3m is how the Aosu WRm is to the Aosu GTS2m. It feels denser, less flexible but still has great speed and plush, glidey turning. Compared to the 356M, the magnets (with my setup) feel slightly weaker, and the turning is less crisp, but the overall feel is very similar. The matte finish is not as slippery as even a broken in 356M, so I didn't have any dropping issues like I did with the 356M. Some minor downsides are that the cube is quite heavy (although this does make it feel solid and premium) and that the Moyu dual adjustment system doesn't have numbers on it like the MGC3 Elite's system. However, putting those issues aside, this is a very solid cube that will please anyone. And it's only $9!

It's pretty insane that this is a $9 cube.  If it had been packaged differently, I would not have been surprised if it were sold as a Moyu for double the cost. Both have the same spring compression system and corner cut really well.  I slowed down both of them with some heavier lubes and they feel amazing now.  The WRM is a slightly nicer cube, but not so much to justify its much higher cost.  I did buy the extra magnets for the RS3M 2020.  I highly recommend them.  They are very cheap and give you an easy way to give your cube a different feel.  After adding the magnets, not only is the magnetic effect stronger (still not very strong), but the cube is noticeably heavier with the weight distribution farther from the center.  It gives each turn a feeling of more momentum.  So for $10, this cube with magnets are an obvious choice. Just make sure you have some heavier weight lube to slow the cube down.

review_title: Amazing cube that beats out flagships
review_text:
I pre-ordered this cube and after days of testing, solving, and just messing around with the tensions, this has been my favorite cube since the Aolong V2. I really enjoy solving 3x3 thanks to this cube.  

 My only complaint is that the orange side on my RS3M loosens the screw every now and then. I'm not entirely sure why, I don't see anything wrong with the core, but I have had it suddenly feel extremely loose on that side and has even exploded due to this. This might be just my cube, like a factory defect, or maybe I just tightened it too much in that side while messing with it. However, I don't think it's a big deal, as I'm able to catch it and I don't find it too annoying to retension the orange side.  

 I'm willing to look past this issue because this cube has worked so well for me, and has helped me reach a sub 10 average of 5. I get pretty consistent solves with this cube, and I am really glad I pre-ordered it. I would definitely recommend this to any cuber, beginner or advanced.

Great cube, and after putting Max Command on the core, 30k on the tracks, and silk and DNM to finish it off, it is the most plush feeling cube I have. Great mix of speed, comfort, and with the addition of a few magnets, stability. 

 I keep seeing reviews and vids asking "how could this cost 10 dollars?" It seems simple to me. Nothing is over-engineered: no fancy honeycomb patterns or track designs, no fancy snapping mechanisms to keep caps in place. And as for the dual-tensioning system, all the R&D likely already happened during the heyday of the GTS3M and WRM. It's a little sloppy when it comes to fit and finish. But everything just works together beautifully. A definite main contender.

All I did was put in 50k on the pieces and in the core to get rid of the spring noise. The cube turns perfectly with a moderate magnetic feel compared to my 356M. I got the cube today and I actually set a new PB after an hour. I think my times will be better than on my Valk 3 Elite once I get used to it. I still prefer the magnetic feel of the Valk 3 elite but I felt the 356M magnets were far too strong. However I still prefer to have the $1 add in magnets because the stock magnets are really small. I use the spring compression on the max which is what I had it on for the gts3m. The matte finish is great and the cube is extremely solid feeling like the GANs. It's by far the loudest cube I've heard in the past couple years and I would pay $60 for the same exact cube with center cap magents and a quieter design. I'm colorblind and I haven't run into problems with the orange shade. The yellow is very very bright and the matte finish makes it even better. The cube doesn't feel cheap whatsoever, however I would pay to have the faces of the pieces not show the inner structures of the inner castings. For example the center caps have circles in the reflection. Other than that the cube is perfect and I much prefer it to the other cubes mentioned.

Then I changed the spring setting to 6 clicks.  Somehow, I kind of like the feel.  It's a bit stiff but feels nice.  Then I opened the other cube that I bought with this: MeiLong 3x3 M.  After setting up that cube, it was so light and airy and I immediately changed the spring setting of this cube to 2 clicks to match the feeling of that cube.  While the turning is now lighter, the cube is still heavy.  This cube is even heavier than my old main QiYi MS 3x3.  And that cube is quite blocky and heavy.

This cube is by no mean bad, I still keep it on the side and play with it as my second main.  If you don't mind or prefer heftier cube and want the option to customize the spring setting to match your style, get this one.

review_title: RS3M 2020: A Bargain Outsold the Weilong GTS3M
review_text: More than a year ago, I said that I truly cherish my WR M and was my main for more than a year now. When my WR M started to lose its stability just a bit, I decided I kind of need something new and bought the RS3 M 2020.  This cube is 56mm across, weighs 85 grams, and costs 9 dollars. While this spec may not surprise you, but there are 2 things that this thing has: A flagship feeling plastic (Almost) and a spring compression system. Typically,  budget 3x3s have a hollow, cheap feeling plastic that is harsh and no adjustable spring system. Instead, Moyu grab those 2 characteristics from higher end flagships and just shoved them into a budget cube. Moyu intentionally did this to target advanced cubers who like flagships, but don't like spending too much money. Anyway, the turning on this cube out of the box is very fast and light, but it is feeling a little lose because of the lighter magnets that came pre-installed. The feeling feels like a flagship (like I mentioned earlier) because of its plastic, but a little more on the cheaper side due to its lighter weight. I then set this cube up by putting extra magnets from the magnet kit, lubing the core with 50k, setting the adjustment system to 2, and lubing the pieces with lighter lube. That resulted in a very stable, controllable cube with a very good speed. The feeling is also smoother overall. I broke my PB single of 7.52 seconds and an average of 10.61 seconds. I'd say buy the magnet kit if you perfer your cubes to be controllable and lube it to prevent wear. Overall, I really like this cube and I highly recommend it since you get the DNA from flagship 3x3s, but for a much lower MSRP.

review_title: YJ YuLong V2 M vs. MoYu RS3 M 2020 vs. DaYan GuHong V4 M
review_text:
A review of a nice sample of budget cubes, current prices $7.99, $9.99 (w/magnet kit), and $14.99 respectively. 

 After adjusting and lubing to my preferred state, here are my observations: 

 Corner cutting:  Almost identical, the DaYan may have a TINY bit more reverse corner cutting. 

 Speed:  YJ slowest, DaYan fastest, but your lube can bring them fairly close together. 

 Weight:  YJ 88 grams, MoYu 87 grams, DaYan 65 grams. 

 Color:  DaYan colors are slightly more saturated, except the yellow looks more orange compared to the other two, and the white is a cool white and the other two use a warm white. 

 Sound:  MoYu may be the loudest, but not by much.  It has more spring noise.  DaYan is the quietest. 

 Feel:  YJ has the best quality "feel" (subjective, of course).  MoYu finish is frosted, but it becomes smooth before long. 

 Magnets:  DaYan seems to be the strongest, the other two less so. 

 Miscellaneous:  MoYu pieces will separate a bit along the edges occasionally, but it's very little and not a detriment.
 		MoYu has an adjustment system, but it's used so infrequently it's of no consideration, unless it's important to you to have it.
 		DaYan cube faces show the most sink from the reinforcing ribs (molding issue).  If the face thickness was increased or the pack and hold times in the injection molding process were optimized, it would improve the appearance.  But it makes no difference in performance.
 		YJ corner twists the easiest, though if you tighten it a bit it isn't a big problem.  The other two are quite good at not twisting. 

 Conclusion:  First of all, the best speedcubers could sub 10 on any of these all day every day, that's how good these cubes are.
 	     However, they're freaks, so most people won't be able to do that.
 	     The typical person will be held back more by his technique than by his choice of cube, and if you are sub 15, any of these cubes should be fine.
 	     However, once you improve your technique as much as you can within genetic and practice time limitations, your cube can help you eke out that last little bit of time you're looking for.
 	     And perhaps around the 10 second mark or so you may be ready to try something a bit more expensive to see if it'll help.
 	     Of course you may always be able to improve you time by getting a more expensive cube earlier, but if you're reading this you're looking for a budget cube anyway, and any of these will suffice for a long time.  Trust me, for the most part your cube isn't holding you back -- if you have one as good as one of these. 

 Preferences:  YJ feels the best in your hand, but the MoYu is only 25% more expensive and you get fewer corner twists.
 	      If you like fast and crisp turning and snappy magnets, the DaYan is quite nice at 90% more expensive than the YJ. 

 Recommendation:  Really none of these are bad, and we're splitting hairs to rank them, but here goes:
 		 YJ is the budget pick,
 		 MoYu is the best buy,
 		 DaYan is the best overall.

When getting this cube make sure you have some lube it generally comes out of the box a bit dry but overall its great out of the box. If you prefer stronger magnets there is a kit for 0.99 cents (use discount code Cubehead for 5% off ;) if you prefer stronger magnets. 
 The stock magnets are medium-ish strong enough to be noticed if your turning slowly with a medium bump but when solving the magnetic bump is much less noticeable.
 I'd recommend not to mess around with the screw because the tension on the screw is good by default although for the compression i would recommend something between the 5th and 7th click.
  Also you might hear some spring noise to remove the noise add a bit of weight 5. The feeling of the cube is crispy and fast, corner cutting is great. Tighter tensions can reduce the corner cutting by a tiny bit but since its more stable it balances out.  

 Tips
  #1 Lube the cube as necessary, don't let it get dry it can damage the cube in the long run 

 #2 Clean the cube, once a month depending on how frequently you use it. If it is visible dirty clean it right away it will extend the cube's lifetime  

 #3 When you are done using your cube place it in a spot where it wont get dusty at all. Drawstring bag, cube case, etc  

 How to clean cube for beginners
 Start by getting supplies ready a small brush, paper towels or towel-.(optional) wipes although i prefer using wipes.  

 Turn a layer half way so that the corners at sticking out and grab the edge piece and try twisting it out if it doesn't come out try loosening the cube a
  
 bit, once it is out remove the rest of the pieces and start wiping the dirt of the pieces with the towels/ paper towels until its clean use the brush to  

 clean the tracks (the part that has a yellow white-ish color. repeat for all pieces once all your pieces are clean assemble the cube in a solved way  

 and leave out a edge and a corner and lube either the piece itself of where the piece will go after lubing both pieces or the spot they will go in put it
  
 both pieces and break it in and you're done. Hope this was helpful if you want more help search a tutorial on YT.

review_title: The best cube I've ever used
review_text: Up until about a month ago, I had never used a magnetic speed cube. I hadn't been taking speedcubing seriously for several years, and was still maining my Cong's Design Meiying from around 2015. I got this cube and the YJ MG C Evo for free in a promotion, and shortly after bought the X-Man Tornado V2 and Dayan Guhong V3. I've tried many setups on all of these cubes, and despite this cube having non-adjustable magnets like the MG C Evo and Tornado V2, it is by far my preferred cube. I personally need something that is very stable and controllable, and I find this cube has that quality over all, despite lubricating them all with the same products. I'm not an extremely fast solver, but with this cube I am very consistent. I have it setup with weight 5 on the screws/springs, Angstrom Gravitas on the stalks/torpedoes, with a bit of silk and DNM-37 on the pieces. I've tightened the axis distance (screw depth) slightly from factory, and lessened the spring compression from factory setting (2 or 3, I forget) down to a 0. I'm more consistent than I've been in years, and on my way back to my peak (13.xx). Currently averaging around 16.xx. I've been getting 11 second singles almost daily, which I haven't gotten so often in years. The fact this is a $9 cube blows my mind. At this price, I think everyone should give it a try. There's even upgrade options for corner to core magnets, and a maglev conversion that would still put the price well below most flagship cubes.

review_title: As someone who is very picky with his 3x3s, I'm really impressed.
review_text:
For the record I must mention that I did receive both of my RS3Ms for free due to a couple of sales that TheCubicle was holding. However, this will in no way affect my review of this puzzle. 
 First off. This cube is $10. When I got this puzzle, I knew people liked it, but I had no idea that it would be this good. The cube comes with accessories, which are quite useful if you don't have them already. I have like 20 of these moyu accessories lying around, so even if I didn't need them personally, I still love the inclusion, as the RS3M is more aimed at those on a budget. Over the past couple months, I have been maining the WRM 2021. But for some reason, with the RS3M, I was doing slightly better. So I decided to do a session with the RS3M. 
 I ended up getting a 15.92 PB AO5. 
 I noticed myself catching less than I normally would on my other cubes, probably due to the fact that it is extremely stable and the corner-cutting is the best I've seen. 
 With this in mind, I officially decided to switch to the RS3M as my main. 
 The feeling of the puzzle itself really reminds me of a mix between the Valk 3 and the GTS2M both cubes were cubes I quite enjoyed and even mained back in 2017.
 The only issue I have is the magnet strength. 
 Unfortunately it is way to weak for my preference and I find myself often getting +2s.
 Luckily there is a way to fix this. 
 I recently purchased core magnets for the cube, which will hopefully help with that issue. 
 Along with this I have since added a small amount of Dignitas, DNM, and Mystic on the pieces., as well as put Traxxas on the core and the tracks. I have mine at medium tensions, and the spring compression is at the fourth click. 
 I'm honestly shocked and delighted that Mofang Jiaoshi has essentially made a near-perfect cube, despite them being a budget company.
 The MF3 series has come a long way in the last six years.

 The massive flaw is most likely due to terrible quality control at this price point. The screws on this cube are be extremely prone to stripping and unscrewing themselves, leading to the whole centre face coming off during solves. If MoYu were to somehow fix this issue, this would be must-buy for every cuber, but otherwise, I can't in good conscience give this any more than 2 stars.

Ok, I know there are a TON of review and hype around this cube, and I just wanted to voice my personal opinions on this. 

 OOTB, this cube is dry, crips, and fast. There was also a significant amount of spring noise on various sides. I applied some core lube (weight 5) and piece lube (DNM-37), and put the dual adjustment to the fourth click. On top of this, I also put in the extra magnets that I purchased into the edges. This cube is now my main. 

 For reference, I have a self magnetized Yuxin Little Magic, a Little Magic M, a YJ Yulong V2M, and a GAN 356M as 3x3's in my collection. This cube is the only cube that allows me to get sub 16. This cube not only performs excellent with flagship features, but also has premium plastic. Most budget cubes have the problem of having good performance with cheap materials. MoYu has gone above and beyond with their budget cubes (this one in particular), and uses high quality plastic with great color shades.  This cube has a very enjoyable/addictive crispy soft feel, and has the best forwards corner cutting I have ever seen (reverse is also pretty good).  

 With many cubers replacing the expensive flagship cubes with the RS3M 2020 as their main, I believe this raises a bigger question in the cubing market design. Oftentimes, simpler is just better. I don't need a bunch of magnet adjustment (cough cough GAN 11), complex spring adjustment (cough cough Tengyun V2) to get good times. It gives me a peace of mind to set it up and start cubing.  

 Sorry for the long rant, but in conclusion this cube shines in EVERY SINGLE ASPECT. Except 1. The only fault this cube has (and its a decent one) is its weight. Weighing in at 86 grams stock, and 89 grams with the extra magnet, its a pretty thick boi. Especially when doing long sessions/averages, you can start to feel the weight wear down on your hands, and starts to affect your TPS. It's not a bid deal (especially for beginners), but I can't help but think how good the WRM 2020 performs. Lightweight, same adjustment, and a more compact size, it's the dream cube right? Well yes, but no. Although I'm sure the corner cutting is jsut as good or better than the RS3M 2020,  It may feel more "snappy" or "forceful" due to its lightweight (props to cyoubx for this explanation). Maybe cubers have to give and take with heavy cubes and good corner cutting, or light cubes and more forceful corner cutting (GAN cubes have this problem).  

 If you're a seasoned cuber with many lubes, definitely make sure to check out this cube (also get the magnet kit)
 If you're a beginner or someone on a budget, this is hands down the best cube on the market for under $10 (get the magnet kit!) The only reason I would advise you stay away from this, is if 1. You absolutely HATE heavy cubes . 2. You don't want to pay for lubes (this cube NEEDS to be setup). 
 If you're a beginner, there are essentially 2 types of lubricants. 1 for the core (where the spring and screw make contact), and the other for the pieces. For those on the tightest budget for lubes, I reccoment the "QiYi M-lube" for piece lube, and the "Adheron Heavy" lubricant for the core lube. 

 Well, if you still stuck around, thanks! 
 Happy cubing yall

review_title: Amazing, but takes an INSANE amount of setup
review_text:
When I first bought this cube, it was crazy fast, to the point where it was uncontrollable (as is the case with most MoYu flagships OOTB). I tightened the settings and added some FZ Seattle, Calm, and Rush. The cube felt insanely tight yet fast. The corner cutting was really harsh, and I got lockups that I never would have gotten on my Weilong V10. I did a few hundred solves, and the lockups still wouldn't go away. I had to really experiment with each and every possible customization setting until I could find one which suited my turning style (outer setting 6, inner setting 4). Additionally, I added some DNM to really speed the cube up.
 The cube was still fast, although not uncontrollable anymore, and the corner cutting was the best I've ever experienced on a flagship. The cube still took some getting used to, but after a few hundred solves I think this cube will be my main.
 One thing that really stood out about this cube was the weight: it is so much lighter than the Weilong V10, which I'm not a big fan of to be honest, because I feel the added weight of the V10 makes me more confident when I'm turning. However, it is faster than the V10 in my experience, which I like. Normally I wouldn't have to take this much time to setup a cube (I only took around 30 minutes to setup my V10 vs around 2-3 hours with this cube), but I think the time is worth it as this cube offers speed and stability unlike any other speedcube on the market. A must buy if you're serious about 3x3.

product_name: MoYu WeiLong V11 3x3 (20-Magnet Ball-Core + MagLev + UV)
review_text:
Let me preface this by saying I've been using the RS3M2020+ as my main for 4 years. It started becoming clacky, slow, and hard to turn, so a month ago I decided to get the Weilong v11. The Weilong v11 solved all the problems I had with the RS3M2020+.  

 Out of the box, it was very buttery smooth and very dry. I don't think it even comes factory-lubed. It's fast, but not as fast as people make it out to be. At most, I can do a U4 on the loosest settings with a lot of effort. Doing a U2 requires medium-effort, and a U requires minimal effort. If I had to describe this cube in 3 words, it would be light, airy, and smooth.  

 The cube features a nice sculpted design. The center-caps have a snap design, so they are easy to take on and off. You don't have to worry about them sliding off mid-solve since they are snapped in place.  

 The v11 feels very light to hold. Coming off from the RS3M2020+, holding the v11 feels like I am holding a cube from the future. The pieces feel airy and hollow, yet premium. The pieces don't feel like they will break. Holding this cube feels like I am holding nothing because of how light it is.  

 The performance of the v11 is the best of any cube I've tried. I can turn as fast as I want to without locking up. I don't even have to turn it accurately. Because of the light and airy piece design, the layers require very little effort to turn and spamming algs feels like a breeze. M, E, and S slices feel very easy to perform. I can perform algs on the v11 that I previously couldn't do before on the RS3M2020+ and Valk 3 M. Corner-cutting is definitely not an issue. It feels stable. I can do long practice sessions on the v11 without my hands getting tired, which was a problem I had with the RS3M2020+. 

 The piece-to-piece contact feeling of the v11 is buttery smooth. The cube has a light airy crunch to it when spamming algs. The feeling is even crunchier than my Valk 3 M. It does feel a bit dry even after putting XMT 10 and FZ Calm in it, but I guess airy feeling cubes are just like that. Because it is a combination of airy and crunchy, the v11 is not the quietest cube I have used, as it lacks the dampened sound that comes from denser cubes like the RS3M2020 or the Valk 3 M. Despite being the smoothest cube I have ever felt, it is not the most satisfying cube I have ever felt. This really comes down to the weak magnets. The magnets do their job and keeps the layers aligned, however unlike my RS3M2020+ (that was modified using TheCubicle's magnetic kit) it lacks the soft magnetic cushioning at the end of each turn that makes each turn feel satisfying. For a cube that is so light and easy to turn, you would think that Moyu would put stronger magnets in it. And because of the piece design, you cannot easily mod it with stronger magnets.  

 Overall, the v11 is an excellent upgrade from my previous main. If you're like me and you've used the RS3M2020 for a long time and you're looking for a new main, but you are unsure whether or not to get the v11 because you think it will feel like "another moyu cube", I can assure you that the v11 feels nothing like the RS3M2020.

review_title: Good for a budget cube or if you prefer a much tighter, more controlled cube
review_text:
PROS:
 - Buttery smooth turn feel out of the box
 - Faces snap into alignment well if you use enough force with your turns
 - Feels very solid
 - Corner cutting can be very easy with looser tension at the cost of make the cube easier to deform during turns 

 CONS:
 - Kinda slow
 - Doesn't tolerate much lube or heavier/more cushiony lubes very well 

 I got this as my first speed cube. Compared to the basic Rubik's brand cube, that requires entire wrist and arm movements to turn, that I had been using for a few weeks, the Super RSM 3 2022 Standard felt amazing. I even ended up tightening the tension and compression some from their factory settings because I thought the cube was too uncontrollable. It felt buttery smooth, the faces seemed to just snap into place at the end of a turn thanks to the piece-to-piece magnets, and it felt very solid. 

 My second cube, and current main, was the DaYan GuHong Pro+ MagLev, which I initially thought was too hard to control, and so I kept using primarily the RS3 M for a while. Eventually, I got used to the GuHong Pro+ and ended up preferring it's effortless and less controlled feeling to the RS3 M.  

 After using the GuHong Pro+, I no longer feel like the RS3 M feels as good to me as it used to. I still appreciate it's blockiness and buttery smooth turns, and how well the faces snap into place if you put enough force or effort into your turns, but compared to what I've come to appreciate about the GuHong, it now just feels slow and limiting. 
 It doesn't tolerate lube as well as the GuHong, being very easy to over lube, making it gummy and slow, and thicker lubes that you would typically think of as adding more control, cushion, or a pillowy texture to the feel, make the RS3 M feel like a chore to turn. The only "success" I've had with lubing this cube is with using just the tiniest amount of weight 5 on the springs and washers, and then using a very slight amount on the piece tracks and contact surfaces. I then have to break the lube in for a good while, and then disassemble the cube and give everything a good once over with a cloth to remove some lube before it gets its buttery smooth feeling back. 

 That's not to say that I think it's bad. I just found something else that I like more. I still think the cube feels very solid and is satisfying to turn. I just prefer a faster, less controlled cube, and it just so happens that the Super RS3 M 2022 Standard is more of a comfortable, controlled cube. At $10 USD, it's a pretty good deal for what it is, and is probably a cube that you could main for a pretty long while if you like it's feel and performance.

review_title: Great for the price, but you get what you pay for
review_text: I bought the single track UV coated version of this cube, as someone who barely touches nxn cubes at all. My last 4x4 was some no name speedcube I has gotten years ago, so of course this was a huge improvement. Out of the box, it had that standard moyu turning feel, similar to the rs3m v5 that I main. Corner cutting is about as good as it can get with the way 4x4s turn. My main issue with the cube is that it is really slow for my taste. Even dry out of the box, when other cubes are usually uncontrollable, this one felt like it was almost sanding away at itself. Even after setting it up with no heavy lube, dignitas on the tracks and about 6 drops around the cube, it STILL turns pretty slow. And im not even someone who needs a cube to be so fast you can do a u4 with a single flick, but just to do a single u move for example you have to use a decent amount of force to do a full turn. Its really annoying and it makes it so you have to rely on the corner cutting to do its thing when turning fast. Also, this cube does pop a bit. Even when its pretty tight, the inner hidden layers will often pop out of place mid solve and its a nightmare to fix. The magnets arent as bad as people say they are though, I do agree that the inner wing magnets are very strong and clicky, but you can get used to them. The outer layers are exceptionally good, 3x3 stage is really great on this cube besides the popping issues, I dont like how the middle layers are so small but it doesnt affect my solves too much. Overall though, for as little as 20$ this destroys the MGC and doesnt really limit my times at all. The main problem is just that if you use your normal turning style with this cube you will often end up not doing full turns and popping or locking up.

product_name: MoYu WeiLong Ferrocore 3x3 (Special Edition WRM V10)
review_text:
The cube is light and fast, with impressive magnetic strength—strong enough to keep the cube aligned without being overpowering. With its modified distance travel, this cube strikes the perfect balance between the v9 and v10. 

 I was surprised by the absence of UV coating. Having relied solely on UV-coated cubes for the past three years, I didn’t think I could perform well without it. But this cube has completely converted me! I always thought UV coating was essential for grip and high TPS, but the matte plastic feels fantastic and performs just as well. 

 The Cubicle and Cubehead clearly knew what they were doing with this design. I've tried several other cubes, including the v5, v9 (8 and 20 mag versions), the Super Weilong, and the Tornadoes, but this one surpasses them all. I'm absolutely loving it!

product_name: MoYu WeiLong Ferrocore 3x3 (Special Edition WRM V10)
review_title: Like weilong V8 with core magnets but better
review_text:
I got the FerroCore as a gift this June 2025. I haven't got a V10 so I can't compare it directly, but I have a v9 ballcore and a V8 maglev. Out of the box it was super soft and silky with a hint of scratchy. I had been wanting to get a V10 but was wary of it's new plastic core fearing breakage during disassembly. However the FerroCore fixes that issue by having a traditional core from the v9 20M core. Out of the box, it's turning reminded me of a super rs3m, because that's also in frosted plastic rather than the more common UV.
 I later disassembled it and set it up using dayan standard lube on the tracks and pieces. It was already good before but it became better much better, with buttery and silky turning. I would think it's more similar to the weilong V8 maglev (2021 maglev) than the v9.
 It's magnetic strength is somewhat lower than the v9 for both the piece magnets and core magnets but somehow it suits it better.
 The standard V10 has white internals and it's grey internals look super good to. Not to mention it has the new moyu dual adjustment system. It's good but I need to familiarize myself with it.

product_name: MoYu WeiLong Ferrocore 3x3 (Special Edition WRM V10)
review_text:
I bought this because, I mean, I obviously LOVE Cubehead, and all, so I thought I might try out the cube that he helped design.
 It arrived at my doorstep, and when I opened the package, I was amazed by the packaging. The box was a nice black, with metallic designs on it. The main thing I was amazed about was the fact that it had semicircles cut on the bottom of the box. No more shake-shake to get it out.
 The cube was awesome. I cant say much about first time experiences because of the fact I've used it so much (hint, hint).
 Since the cube was obviously dry, I added some lube to it. I have been perfecting my lube combo, now it consists of Fz-Glide on the tracks, weight 5 on the pieces, Cubicle Labs Silk, and some DNM-37. (added in that order).
 I had also bought the Weilong V10 Maglev kit, just to see what it would be like. After adding the maglev, the cube was effortless to turn. It became my main quickly and has been ever since.
 After all of this, the cube was fast and light, while also being controllable. The only way to describe this feeling is: "it's almost like the cube knows how much to turn and will turn no further."
 As for the popping, depending on the settings, the edges are difficult to pop out by hand, which is a good thing because it means the cube will most likely not pop. 

 Make no mistake, THIS CUBE IS AMAAAAZING! 

 ---CubeTheory

product_name: MoYu WeiLong Ferrocore 3x3 (Special Edition WRM V10)
review_text:
The idea of a cube "outfitted with metal parts" in the core, steel grey internals, the collaboration with CubeHead, and even just the name "Ferrocore" all caught my attention when I first heard about the cube.
 Then I saw a reddit post where they described the cube as just being core swap with a V9 and the "Ferro-" part of the cube was just screws. At the time I also imagined the Ferrocore having the old MOYU screw system from the V9. After seeing that post I decided to hold off on buying it.
 Soon after Cubicle released a video going over the Ferrocore. There I found out about the extra modifications made to the Ferrocore, like the custom springs and the fact that they kept the V10 adjustment system. That was enough to get me to buy one for myself.
 A couple days later the cube finally arrives. Packaging is compact and sleek. I take the cube out of the box, do my first turns and... it honestly felt awful. Out of the box the Ferrocore felt slippery and very blocky despite the modifications on the cube being an effort to make the cube more flexible. My first impressions with it had me pretty disheartened, but I still had hope.
 Fortunately, I also grabbed a Yoo Lube Bundle along with the Ferrocore. One lube video tutorial (also copying Phil's 3-7 tension settings in the Ferrocore video) and a session of breaking the cube in later the Ferrocore starts to shine. On the Yoo setup the Ferrocore is so soft and smooth. The modifications made in this cube really put in work to create a nice balance between flexibility and blockiness/control. My main gripe at this point is that the "Ferro-" name and calling plain old screws "metal parts" is a bit misleading; I was expecting a full metal spider core or a metal ball or something. At least it makes the cube more robust and flexible compared to the original V10. Also props to Cubicle for making it clear that their video would be biased, so their honesty and clarity in the video kind of cancels out the misleading name for me. Another small nitpick is the steel grey internals are hard to see since the edge and corner pieces are not capped like in GAN or Tornado cubes, but that is due to the design of the V10 and the steel grey colored internals aren't really the main highlight on this cube anyways. Overall a really comfortable cube with a somewhat misleading name but makes up for it with good modifications that help it stand out from the other versions of the V10. 

 TLDR:
 Sees Ferrocore on the website for the first time: "Yoooo!"
 Hears that the Ferrocore is just a core swap: "Noooo!"
 Sees Cubicle video about the other mods done to the cube: "Yoooooo!!"
 Gets the cube and does first turns in stock setup: "NNOOOOO!!!!"
 Gives the Ferrocore the Yoo lube setup: "YYYYYOOOOOOOOO!!!"

review_title: By far the best iteration of the V10 - as well as my new main
review_text:
I'll start off with this - I liked the original V10. But there were a few issues with the cube that made it incompatible as a main for me. For one, it was too rigid - I felt the cube was not flexible enough and often felt too blocky. Some people may prefer this, however I am not one of them. The cube was also quite fragile, with numerous reports of the ballcore snapping and not being as durable as the V9's ballcore. 

 This cube fixed ALL of those issues - replacing the V10 BC with the V9 20 magnet BC made the cube less fragile, and the components connecting the center pieces to the core being made out of metal made it more durable - as well as more flexible.
 The cube being more flexible means it has more room to breathe, it is not nearly as blocky as the original V10 and that is an improvement for me. 

 The steel gray internals are also very neat, and give this cube its own distinctive look compared to many other cubes on the market.  

 I set it up with Cubicle Mystic + some DNM 37 and the cube was quiet (compared to most other cubes I have mained), fast, and buttery smooth. It is now my main. 

 My only gripe with it, albeit a very small gripe, is matte plastic instead of UV Coating. However, the matte plastic feels quite nice, and it wears out eventually, so that doesn't dock any points.

review_text:
This Pyraminx is GOATed. I have been gaining it for about 4-5 months, and it has served me so well! Out of the box, it was extremely over-lubed, fast, extremely strong magnets(even for me), and super greasy. However, after cleaning it out, installing the upgrade kit (10 magnet ball core with tip mods), and lubing it with diginitas in the tips, weight 5 on the springs, fz calm and diginitas on the tracks, and diginitas, dnm-37, mystic, and fz calm on the pieces, it feels so nice. I also put it on magnet setting 2, which is almost perfect (wish it was like a setting 2.5 or something, but still good). I am a semi-all-rounder (I don't do big blind, 7x7, or multiblind), but I main pyraminx and I average sub 4.7 with this using l4e and some ml4e. After about 600 solves on CS Timer, I was even able to achieve a PB of 1.89 in the single and a PB average of 3.29, along with a sub-4 AO12. I have yet to try the YLM, but so far, after trying the gan enhanced (just overpriced and slow with horrible tips), rs standard, and maglev, the only real complaint I have with this cube is the weight, which is a little too heavy and how much factory lube there is. I've tested this out in comp, and I got a 4.01 pr single, and a horrible 6.12 average because of my nerves leading to 3+2s (including a 5 that I one-looked lol), but this cube honestly dealt with my nerves very well! This cube is the reason I started raining pyraminx, and will likely be my main for years to come! 

 TLDR: Best pyra on the market once you clean it out and set it up, even better with the LBL Designs Magnetic Core DIY Kit for WeiLong Pyraminx!

 Secondly, disassembly. There are no instructions whatsoever on how to disassemble this thing. I've watched Cubicle's product review video on how to disassemble it, and let me tell you, DO NOT PULL THE TIPS OFF WITH YOUR HANDS. It will bend/break the cheap rotating plastic platforms on which the tips click in place. Horrible design flaw. To avoid breaking the piece mounts you have to half turn the tips and pry them off one side at a time with the plastic magnet adjusters they provide you in the accessories box.  

 This puzzle is 5 stars on performance and price however:
 Broken core:  -1 star
 Design: -1 star

It is an excellent pyraminx, much better than the maglev without a doubt. To a certain extent it reminds me a bit of the sensations that the Bell v2 gives me but it is much faster, stable and much more pleasant to turn. Some drawback that I would find but that do not ruin this cube at all are the tips, sometimes they are a bit slow but they are not bad at all, and the falling of the tiles of the edges, it is a bit annoying at first but it can be stick with glue and no more problems. 

 About the magnets, they are either quite strong or somewhat weak, between level 2 and 3 there is a too radical change between them, I would like it to have another level in between but I'm not complaining. Actually level 2 makes the cube very stable although sometimes hard to turn, it takes getting used to. Level 3 is not bad but it can cause some lockups. 

 As I said at the beginning, an excellent pyraminx, I am really very happy with the work that moyu has done with it
I bought this cube at Nationals and it was great! It ended up helping me get a PR average. The only problem is that you can hear the springs, otherwise it's great.
When I got this pyraminx out of the box, it completely fell apart. I wondered why and I looked at the core and it was broken.  I am not sure what happened, but I think it had to do with shipping.

While this is my current main, I don't feel like this is the best pyraminx experience on the market. Simply put, while I have zero issues about people of any skill level buying any level speed cube they want, this just isn't a good pyraminx for beginners. There's the obvious core stability issue, for which I recommend (if possible), just requesting the free, stronger core right from the get go and installing it immediately. My core broke on me after only a couple hundred solves. Additionally, despite being careful, I had 2 of my internal tip pieces (the ones that hold the magnets in place) bend upwards when I tried to remove the tips to unscrew my broken core.  And on top of that, I'm now getting cap pops for the edges, which has never happened for me with any other pyraminx. In short, if you're looking for a really fast pyraminx with some customization features and are relatively experienced with pyraminx hardware, then sure, I recommend this cube. But if you're looking for something much more immediately plug and play, I think you'd be better off going with either of the Bells or the Gan pyras.

product_name: MoYu WeiLong Ferrocore UV 3x3 (Special Edition WRM V10)
review_text:
Meets all my expectations. As a casual, I have never held a cube this well engineered! I have used many cheap magnet-less cubes though. One thing I find fascinating is that, on the outside, this cube is exactly the same as my cheap NexCube. The UV coating is noticeably nicer to hold, though, and because of the spherical core and magnets, turning the cube feels indescribably fast and smooth. 

 My NexCube, which felt very smooth to me right up until I pulled this cube out of the box, has a noticeable friction between the pieces, and if you turn the cube too fast it's impossible to avoid the cube catching because it can't spin as fast as you are trying to turn it. So you are constantly slowing yourself down. With this cube, turning it feels like there is practically no friction at all, and as the layer's corners line up, the magnets cause it to snap into place. This snap feels very satisfying, but the act of turning the cube itself feels a little less satisfying, because it's that effortless, and quiet. 

 If you want a good cube to have fun improving your solving skills, or to show off to people who have only every held a Rubik's brand cube, this will not only not disappoint, but you won't even believe a cube this amazing is possible.

I bought this cube with pretty reasonable expectations, but I am still blown away. Out of the box, the feeling is kinda sandy and crunchy, and it is a bit tight. For setup I loosened the cube a bit, put the compression on 3 clicks, and added some Traxxas 10k and Mystic. It still has a bit of crunch, but it is also smooth and stable. You are able to corner cut from pretty much anywhere, although if you are at an extreme angle, it will jam up some of the time. This obviously depends on tensions. Tip: To tell which corner is anchored in the core, just peel apart the layers and turn a side. If you see the entire core moving with the layer, then that side contains the anchored corner. Repeat that on all 3 axes, and you can deduce which corner is anchored.

product_name: MoYu Super RS3 M 2022 3x3 Ball-Core (Magnetic Core + MagLev)
review_text:
Having tried the Super RS3M Ball Core , G13M, and YD2 (Tv3) in the same day, with at least 50 solves on each, I'd say I personally preferred  the overall hand feel and tactile texture of the ball core. As much as I aesthetically enjoy the UV of the G13M, the ball core's matte texture felt very natural and comfortable. It glides well without being overly uncontrollable for me. In terms of sound, I'm not overly bothered by "loud" cubes, but for me the ball core sat between the G13ML (loudest) and the YD2 (quietest). In terms of speed, again I'd place it between the G13M, which verged on being unwieldy at times, and the YD2, which definitely felt "grounded" due to the custom lube combination. Maybe it's because of my natural grip style or possibly current skill level, but I tended to lock up more with the ball core than either the G13M or the YD2, regardless of if I sped up or slowed down, though making M/S/E slices was more stable on the ball core than it was on G13M due to the ball core's more overall sturdy feel.  

 If I was blindfolded and had to pick purely on tactile experience I'd lean more towards the ball core. I'd personally use this more as a training cube to practice techniques and speed/pacing, to train myself to avoid locking behaviors/grips and transition to the G13M or the YD2 to actually break PBs. If I'm trying to level up my comfort with speed then I'd practice with the G13M, but for consistency and avoidance of locking when it matters I'd default to the YD2. 

 Though I don't particularly enjoy the springy sound of the YD2, or it's grounded feel, it is without a doubt the most stable of the three with the fewest lockups. The G13M gave the strongest sense of speed (naturally) but at times would verge on outpacing what I was expecting my hands to do. It definitely had the most flexible/warp-able feel of the three, and was more difficult (or at least uncertain) to execute M/S/E slices without lockups. Most of these issues are likely due to my own grip style (I'm a lefty, so I've trained myself to be able to do most algorithms mirrored for both hands, though I'll still naturally tends toward my left handed grip on default)

review_title: The best Skewb on the market
review_text:
The maglev works perfectly with how the Skewb's mechanism functions. The puzzle is incredibly stable and secure with how the pieces connect with each other, and the magnets create a very smooth and pleasant turning experience allowing for precise and speedy turning. This puzzle is very receptive of lube and can be sped up or slowed down, potentially to your liking. I did not do much testing with slowing it down as I prefer speedy puzzles but a few drops of silk gave it a very pleasant and slightly more controllable feel.  

 The one downside to the puzzle is the potential for dropping it. I have been unable to pin down exactly why it happens but during the first 50 or so solves I dropped the cube 8-9 times, if not more. In the last 100 solves that has been dropped to 2-3, but it still feels significantly more slippery in that sense than any other puzzle I have used. I am not sure if it is more of a personal issue or if it is a problem with the puzzle, but it was never a problem with other skewbs. I recommend your first solves either be entirely over a table or a softer ground just in case, but it does get more manageable over time.

I decided to go all in and get the triple track version and it feels quite different than other 4x4x4s I have tried. After using it for a week, I cannot go back! 

 The primary difference that stands out to me is single slices are a bit harder to do because the center edges REALLY want to stay together because of the additional magnets holding them together. This makes single slices a bit less fluid. 
 This might feel like a negative at first, but at least for the algorithms I use and solves I do, those only come up during oll parity and only takes a bit of use to acclimate to the change. 
 The great news is the additional magnets actually make the normal 3x3x3 solve portion a LOT easier, because the center pieces REALLY do not want to be misaligned. This has reduced lockups for me QUITE a bit.
 Wide moves have a bit more magnetism on the corner alignment, but you likely won't notice or care much if you do during solves, because those are a lot easier to control than single slices.
 For me, this cube is exactly what I never knew I wanted. It makes the 3x3x3 solve portion so much easier, doesn't really affect edge pairing (because I use wide moves), and just feels great in all other arenas. 
 For settings, I did loosen tension by a half turn on all sides, and that made the cube a whole lot more flexible as well.  
 So unless you use a TON of single slice moves in your 4x4x4 solves, consider the triple track as quality option.

This cube is a great, magnetic 2x2. It lost one star though, for these reasons: 

 1. For a newbie, it is quite fiddly adjusting and changing the GES nuts. It has very small tensioning numbers (0.6 and 0.8) that you have to squint to see.  

 2. It is really expensive. I don't regret buying this, but I do regret how my wallet feels lighter :) 

 3. If you, on 3x3, upgraded from a cheap cube to a great, expensive cube (in my case, the Gan 356 RS to the Gan 12), and really felt the difference between the 2 cubes (for me I felt like it was amazing just to scramble the Gan 12), then don't expect the same life-changing experience. This cube didn't have that same feel as the 3x3s, and is not UV Coated, so it didn't feel as amazing. 

 But those were the bad points. The good things about the cube are: 

 1. Even as hard as it is to adjust (for a newbie), it is not that hard to put back together. Just be wary of different settings/GES Nuts for different faces. 

 2. As my wallet feels lighter, my new main 2x2, this cube, also feels lighter. It's lightness probably helped me get multiple times that were good for me (multiple 5's and 4's), because since I'm a beginner, I usually get 7's or 8's or even 10's!!! 

 3. It may not be the same life-changing experience, but it is worth it if you love cubing, which you probably do otherwise you wouldn't be reading this review!

review_title: Highly decent cube, but controversial opinion ahead (no politics, don’t worry)
review_text:
I got this cube awhile ago, and it used to be my main. Just the only problem, is that sometimes the internal edges sometimes can’t pick a side of the core to be on when you turn quickly, (I use Ortega so I rely on fast turning and lookahead) I don’t blame Gan, it’s my turning style that’s sloppy. I could see that the company probably had a hard time implementing their GES nuts into a 2x2 and still keep it fairly decent. Coming from me, I am a huge Gan fanboy (with just a sprinkle of bias against their 4x4) but sometimes they just don’t work with me. To be fair, my turning style is that of that one “fist bump” that Jesse did with Max Park; the expected is completed, but it’s just super awkward and probably damp. If you want another cube for as good in the price range, try out; 

 MoYu WeiPo WR M : A tactile, somewhat customizable cube.
 CONS : It has really weak magnets, and I +2 half of my solves on it. 
 PROS : Fast turning and decent corner cutting. 

 MoYu RS2M “Evolution” : Another 50mm cube, also customizable, the RS3M of 2x2.
 CONS : It does take quite a bit of force to turn, but that’s coming from a weak tweenager. Also, the corner cutting is slightly less than the WeiPo WR M. It’s also quite fragile, based on its reviews.
 PROS : Amazing, smooth turning, that doesn’t really discriminate against the rougher turners, unless you go full jackhammer turning. 

 In conclusion, this cube is really good for those who turn lightly, and accurately.
 But I turned it into a Speffz practice cube. Oops.

This cube is incredibly light and airy, a bit floppy, and it was a little bit to fast out of the box, but after a few minutes of break-in and setup, it easily became the best 2x2. The only flaws that I can think of, is that the ges nuts were very hard to replace (at least for someone who’s never dealt with them before), and the plus and minus sign for the magnets were extremely hard to see.
 All right, now onto setup: For the ges nuts, I replaced the default green with the transparent 0.6 so that the cube would be more stable and easier to control. The medium magnet setting seemed quite weak, so I put the magnets on the strong setting. For lube setup, I started with mystic (which is my favorite, btw), and silk, which gave it a nice fast and soft or plush feel. I then added some Weight 5 for controllability, after that this became what I believe to be one of the best 2x2s ever.
 As a disclaimer, this setup is not needed, and is definitely usable and a great cube out of the box, but in my opinion, the cube is just a bit to fast and the magnets just a bit to weak. I definitely recommend this setup though. So, amazing cube,  best with setup. Also, the box is really fun.

I first want to say that I really love this cubes performance. I got this for myself for christmas, so at this point I’ve had this for 4 months. I came of a rs3mv5 ball core and at first the v100 was waaayy too fast for me. It really took a long time to get used to the insane speed and auto alignment of this cube. The not-that-insane corner cutting of this cube was also really of-putting at the start. However after a short time, I really learned to love this cube and improved my average from 13 to 12 seconds. However three months after I got the cube, I had the core break on me (during a U move, not even by slaming the cube down). As you can see in the first two pictures, the yellow side broke of the core, which I think shouldn‘t be happening to a 40 dollar premium cube. I was thinking about contacting customer service, but I was able to superglue the core  back together, so I didn‘t bother about it. A few days later a magnet capsule fell out of the cube. Luckily, I was able to fix the issue with superglue again, however the fixed magnet now makes a clicking noise with every alignment. Earlier this day, the core broke again :-( . I’m still waiting for the glue to dry, but at this point I think it‘s time for a replacement part. So @thecubicle: I would be really glad about some spare parts! All in all I really recommend buying this cube, because I think these durability issues are simply personal bad luck, as I haven‘t seen anybody else complain about it.

The puzzle is indeed 55 millimeters, but the shape of the cube does not waste size. The v11 feels similar in size despite being about a half millimeter more.
