review_title: Skeptical at first, but boi was I wrong...
review_text:
I want you to keep in mind that I was VERY skeptical about MagLev at first. 

 I got this puzzle as a $10 mystery puzzle, so a $3.99 profit. Out of the box, this puzzle was way too fast. Automatically, I set it aside and put the extra magnets in to keep it more stable, along with using a controllable lube to keep things smooth. It's very satisfying to turn and the MagLev technology feels weird yet good. Heres what I have to say about it 

 Pros:
 Fast
 Everything the RS3M had 

 Cons:
 No stickered variant. 

 Overall, this puzzle is great. For only $13.99, it feels like it's in the $30 range.
It is an amazing cube, very controlable, but still very fast, love it.

One property of maglev cubes that many people seem to miss is that the force applied by magnets increases faster than springs. Because of this, even if you have it on a weak magnet setting, the cube will still feel very tight. Corner cutting requires a lot of force, so combined with it being faster than the standard one, it catches more. I much prefer the standard version of this cube, and I would only recommend this one if you want the fastest one possible. It's not a bad cube, but when there's the regular one to compare it to, I wouldn't recommend this.
Very good out of the box and amazing corner cutting. My only downside is if u don’t live in us like me shipping can take 4 to 7 weeks.

This puzzle left me speechless. I’ve never owned a magnetic 3x3 before, the only magnetic puzzles I had owned being a magnetic skewb and pyraminx, so I didn’t really know what to expect. Any expectations I did have were completely blown out of the park. This thing is fast. There isn’t a single point where this cube won’t corner cut, meaning lockups are truly a thing of the past. The magnets are strong, but in no way do they slow down the turning. This is truly an amazing cube, and I recommend it to anybody, not just people on a budget. If you’re looking to get serious at cubing but don’t want to spend $80 on the newest GAN puzzle, get this.

Out of the box, the FerYooCore felt buttery smooth, fast, and controllable. It immediately reminded me of my beloved GuHong Pro M — but with a much more bubbly, marbly, and poppy feel that made it stand out even more. 

 Compared to other 3x3s I own, the FerYooCore feels softer, snappier, and more lively. The magnet strength is noticeably snappier than my Weilong V10s, and it contributes to that marbly/bubbly feeling I enjoy so much. Every turn feels tactile without being harsh. 

 In solves, the Feryoocore is fast, smooth, and satisfying, though I did experience some overshooting, which I attribute more to my fast turning style than the cube itself. Corner cutting is fantastic — exactly what you would expect from a top-end modern 3x3 — and the flexibility feels just right without being floppy. 

 I haven't fully adjusted to the feel yet, but I'm confident I’ll be breaking PBs once I settle into it more. The solution experience is just too good not to. 

 As for looks, the Feryoocore nails the premium, minimalist aesthetic. If you're someone who loves clean-looking cubes and wants something ready to perform out of the box without endless setup, this is a perfect choice. 

 Pros:
 Buttery smooth, marbly, lively feel 

 Fast, snappy, and controllable 

 Fantastic corner cutting 

 Premium, minimalist aesthetic 

 Excellent out-of-the-box performance 

 Cons:
 Some overshooting is possible for very aggressive turners (minor) 

 Final Verdict:
 "The Feryoocore is a buttery smooth, marbly, and snappy cube that not only feels amazing to solve on but also nails the minimal, premium aesthetic perfectly."

The cube felt heavy (I even measured it, almost 1 gram heavier than the stock Ferrocore, 69 vs 70 grams = 1 gram of lube?? Whaaaaaat?? :-)) and slow, strangely muffled and numb. Since his setting of 5/4 
 is somewhat more loose than my 6/5 it must have been the heavy lubing. Someone here also wrote that it took some time to break in so thats what I did. But after a lot of turning and solving the initial impression remains. OK, breaking it in
 made a difference, it got faster and the numbness and muffled feeling were a bit attenuated but there was no magic. I am not a very experienced cuber but have experimented quite a bit with lubing. Of course, everyone has its own preference and this is only my take to this story. But I think while lubing almost always enhances the character of the cube or even sets it free, there is a tipping point where too much lubing destroys the character of the puzzle and it becomes just like any other heavy lubed cube. In my view, this is what happened with this yoo-cube. Again, just for my liking.
 So, in conclusion, the Ferrocore is the best cube I have ever used (and I thought I was a Gan-Fan-Boy) but setting it up seems to be a different cup of tea. The stock Ferrocore is a raw gem that only needs a little bit of set-up to become a cube of magical awesomeness - 5/5 stars. People buying the yoo-cube lube setup should always keep in mind that this is the preference of one individual - however awesome he or she may be (and I really do think CUBEHEAD is THE Mr. MAN!!).

Hello everyone. Before I begin, I just wanted to say that I don’t own this cube, I tried it at a recent competition of mine.  

 Moving on, this 4x4 is godly. Better than any other I’ve tried, including the Wuque M. First of all, the outer layers are what I think sets this cube apart from the rest. They are extremely quick but at the same time, completely controllable. The visible magnets aren’t as distracting as I initially thought, along with the honeycomb design. Corner cutting is excellent by my standards, with a piece for both forwards and reverse.  

 The inners, in my opinion are great, but do not live up to the expectations set by the outer layers, specifically because of lockups. Granted, the one I tried was pretty loose, so don’t quote me on that. I enjoy the stronger magnetic pull of the inner layers, but do believe that the color coding aspect is a bit unnecessary. Another thing to note is that the specialized nut in the center is MUCH to small, and I would’ve liked either a bigger nut or a regular screw. Corner cutting isn’t as good either.  

 Turning throughout the cube is fast, sandy and crunchy. I do not know how the owner set it up, but I enjoyed it. The honeycomb pattern does what it is supposed to do, because the pieces were really greasy. I think the turning would fit a wide range of styles, but for some, that classic GAN feel may not transfer very well to a 4x4. 
  
 Overall, I think this cube is great for just about any type of cuber. For their first 4x4, I think GAN hit a home run. I plan to pick one up myself in Stickerless and I think that you should get one to.  

 Good luck and happy cubing!

I really really wanted to love this cube. I have a GAN 356 SM and it is my absolute favorite. I love the crunchy feel and strong magnets (compared to the smooth feel and weak magnets of my Valk 3 Power M). Unfortunately this cube just has too many issues.  

 First and foremost, it is just weak. I had it about a week and already broke a corner. The stem on the corner piece is not solid, but three very thin spindles of plastic. This is just not going to be durable to either aggressive solving or occasional even short distance drops.  

 Before it fell apart, the inner layers left a lot to be desired. The outer layers are awesome making the 3x3 stage a pleasure. The inner layers a borderline awful making the center stage and any parities a nightmare.  

 I really like the double magnets on the inner layer which helps to hold the together when turning the outer layers. That was a great idea. 

 Finally tensioning this is an arduous process. In order to get the plastic tool onto the nut, you have to either really stretch the center pieces apart (which is impossible of you like tight tension) or remove several center pieces very carefully. Pull them the wrong way and "snap" they are toast. 

 Nice try GAN, but you have some work to do. Hopefully V2 will fix these flaws, which are just to much to accept for a $56 cube.

I bought this cube off the premise that it was a GAN 356 X but with a different core, no interchangeable magnets, and for almost half the price. It did not disappoint. Turning is smooth and fast OOTB with a small tad of crunchiness. Compared with the X V1 and XS (both of which I do not own but have tried), the turning is lighter but has a similar feel to the X V1, and is not as light or smooth as the XS. The magnet strength is similar to the medium setting on the XS, giving it a subtle click when turning that gives a slight bubbly feel. It comes OOTB with the blue (second weakest) springs set to 0.6 (the tightest) tension, and in this state it is usable but to me it was slightly too unstable. I tried the green (second strongest) springs on 0.6 tension and it was still slightly too flexible. As a result, I have switched it to the yellow (strongest) springs and set the tension to 0.6, meaning this is the most stable setup possible on this cube. To me this makes the cube stable and controllable, with a rigid, snappy feel, but still fast. Though I feel like the blue (second weakest) and purple (weakest) springs are too flexible to use for two-handed solving, I think that they would be good for one-handed solving as they make the cube very fast and easy to turn. As for the frosted coating on the tiles, they are slippery at first, but you do get used to it and the coating apparently does rub off eventually. All in all, even though this is still a 32$ puzzle, it does still represent good value for money compared to GAN's other magnetic cubes.

review_title: Great cube at a great price point.
review_text:
the gan 356m is a great mid range cube, has a smooth papery feel out of the box. i will go over of my opinions in the pros and cons.
 the gan 356m's corner cutting is not the best, 45degress takes some effort at times and theres a spot where it doesnt cut, though i dont think anyone would make such an extreme cut, just something minor. the magnet strength for me is a little too strong, though this comes down to personal preferences. 
 the gan 356m is a great feeling cube, i use green ges nuts to make it more stable. it feels smooth papery, enjoying to turn and very light, way lighter than gan's past flagship, the x, which is 50 dollars. i love the crunchy, tactile and hollow sound it produces. coulours are very vibrant, which i like. overall, i think this cube is great, in terms of price and performance, suitable for all levels of cubers. i definitely am happy with my purchase with this cube.

Theres good things and bad things about this cube. 
 I got this cube when I was a beginner cuber and averaging 40 seconds back in april and it has helped me get an average of 20 seconds and a pb of 12 seconds. It feels nice and the GES nuts really came in handy because the blue nuts were too loose for me so I used the yellow nuts to the 0.8 setting. The magnet strength is really good too and corner cutting is great.
 I don't like this cube a lot though. Back then I was a "cuber" who knew nothing about cubing and thought gan was the only good brand, but I was very wrong. The cube flexes and isn't as stable as I would like it to be even with the yellow ges, and the honeycomb pattern is nice but annoying to clean since dust and gunk get into the lines. There's better options that are cheaper than this. I would recommend getting a cheaper (and maybe better cube)like a Valk 3 M or a YJ MGC Elite if you want a cube that has customizability, or the RS3 M 2020 if you are on a tighter budget. If you just want a GAN cube that has magnets then get this I guess. 

 TL;DR Great corner cutting, good magnetic strength, GES Nuts are necessary, a bit too flexible, annoying honeycomb pattern, better options cheaper than this.

review_title: Great potential, but disappointing out of the box
review_text:
TL;DR: this is an okay puzzle, but only after quite a bit of work, and I am very disappointed in GAN for releasing it in the state that they did. 

 Out of the box, this puzzle is unstable and pops very easily, even on the tightest tensions allowed by the numerical GES system.  The tip magnets are also extremely strong, to the point that they would have an impact on my solves.  Finally, my first copy was missing a magnet in one of the centers, but thankfully I was able to get a replacement.  In my opinion, all of these issues are inexcusable, especially at this price point and by a company as highly esteemed as GAN. 

 Fortunately, I was able to find a solution to the majority of the performance issues that I had.  The first thing you need to do is remove the tips, which is not trivial on this puzzle.  The best way I found is to insert a plastic razor blade between the tip and the center about in the middle of the piece.  Pull out slightly and push up to remove the tip.  This requires more force than most people would expect, so don't worry too much about breaking it.  The first modification I did was adding a washer on the center stalk under the nuts.  The washers I used were from an MF3RS2, but anything of a similar size will be fine (most post-2015 3x3s made by MoYu and their sub-brands will work, along with various others).  This mod effectively tightens the tensions by reducing the amount of travel in the center piece before it hits the top of the nut.  It greatly improves the stability and significantly reduces popping, although it does not eliminate pops completely.  The other modification I did was removing a magnet from each tip.  This can be done by pushing a thumbtack through the bottom of the piece holding the tip magnets. It will leave a tiny hole, but it doesn't impact performance. 

 After the mod(s) are complete, there is a very simple yet effective setup for this puzzle.  I added Weight 5 on one of the torpedoes, the main surface of one of the centers, and on each tip.  If it is too slow, add a bit of DNM-37 on top of the Weight 5.  I am currently using green nuts on 0.6, but experiment to find what you prefer. 

 Doing all of this will result in a fast, smooth Pyraminx with excellent corner cutting.  Pops are possible, but they should not be much of an issue unless you have extremely inaccurate turning.  However, if you would rather have something that requires less work, check out the Little Magic M.  It is a solid puzzle and doesn't have any major issues out of the box.

Bare with me this could be a long review I am going to try and answer some of the questions that I see in the question tab 

 One of the first questions that I have seen is which GES nuts do what and I too was confused but it goes from purple to yellow in a reverse rainbow. The purple ones  provide a flimsy speedy feel that I personally really like. If you squeeze down on the nut it should compress really easily in your hand which makes the cube really flimsy and fast. It makes corner cutting really easy however because you are turning so fast it is easy to make mistakes. The downside to the really lose springs is that it pops all the time so I will be having a sub 5 solve with a last layer skip (I use top first because it was the first tutorial I found) and then when I go to AUF or I guess in Pyraminx ABF the edge piece slips out and boom goes the dynamite. When you use yellow springs on the other hand when you go to squeeze down on the nut it becomes harder to do and it becomes more firm. It makes turning harder and corner cutting far worse. If you like a really stable feeling cube then you will love yellow the turning is harder however I have never made a mistake on yellow springs.  

 If you look closely at the GES nuts real close you might see something that says 0.8, 0.6, and then a ban sign. On the Ban sign you can pull out the spring and change it. On 0.6 The feel is tighter and on 0.8 the feel is looser but to me I think for me it actually adjusts how strong the magnets are and 0.6 gives more of a pull. The personal settings I use are Purple springs on 0.6 but I would play around with all the settings and do even an average of 10 is what I did but if you want to do an Ao100 then I am not stopping you but do you really want to do 800 solves.  

 Now you might be wondering how to adjust settings, if you have used any other Pyraminx then you know to pop off the tips. You might however find yourself struggling to pop them off because they move but don't all at the same time. Some people might be able to find a way to uses their nail to get under it because if you feel under the cap you will find a lip. I don't have good nails so I often use my keys. You will thank me later.  

 One of the other questions that I see is: is the customizability worth it. The short answer is yes the long one is maybe. If you can customize then it is always worth it. However if you do not want to do some solves to find settings or you are a beginner and just want a really cheap functional cube get the Qiyi MS I have heard great things about it and I know that the Qiyi MS 3x3 used to be (or still is) Phil Yu's main. Besides the point I know that the MS line is Qiyi's good budget cube alongside the RS3M and the Monster Go I guess. So if you are looking for a good Pyraminx get that one because it is fine and functions well but it is a budget cube. But if you are like I got this cube as person who had only once solved a Pyraminx once before I became a cuber and someone in class had the ShengShou so I tried it out and was happy when I had solved one layer and the rest of the puzzle happened to be solved. Unrelated but what I am saying is that if you want to spend the money spend it. 

 So I hope I have provided enough insight. It is a great Pyraminx if you want to make it great. I would most definitely recommend it.

review_title: Great puzzle, but you can get something similar for half the price.
review_text:
Before I got this my main was a MoYu WR M Maglev, but I wanted to try something different and finally check out a GAN cube.  Now that I have the 11 M Pro my main is...    ...still the WRM.  The GAN cube is slightly more stable feeling than the WR M, but I've gotten used to the smooth feel of the MoYu cube and kind of prefer it.  I would say that both those cubes are pretty close in quality and which you prefer is really a subjective thing.  I average in the mid-teens right now, so the differences may be more pronounced if you are sub-10.  The only other cube I have that feels similar to the 11 M Pro is my DaYan TengYun V2.  I feel like the Gan has a slightly nicer feel and color scheme though (and I never cared for the TengYun's white internals).  But again, it really feels like which cube is better comes down to personal preference.   

 The elephant in the room is of course the price.  If you can afford to blow $50 to try out a high-quality cube then this is definitely a good one.  But if money is tight, just be aware that other flagship cubes are pretty comparable to this and you may end up liking them better anyway.

review_title: Best out of the box experience
review_text:
Now, I know this cube is not for everyone, but my turning style favors light and fast cubes like this one. Magnets are moderate, sightly stronger than the ones found on the Tornado V3 and the turns are papery smooth. Corner cutting is similar to the 12 in terms of range, reverse is slightly worse than the 13 and feels a bit less snappy than the T V3.  Smaller cuts (which are the ones that actually matter) are perfectly fine with all four. What really surprised about the 11 compared to the 12 and 13 is how usable it was out of the box. The 13 was just a mess, 12 was good but a bit too loose, while the 11, although more flexible than what I prefer, felt really solid, which is ironic for a cube this light. It is also the first time I feel comfortable with factory lube, so I didn't have to apply any of my lubes (for now). After setup, I'm still not sure if this will be my new main over the 12: I perform similarly with both, and in terms of which one feels better, there is no real winner for me. I would rank it slightly above the T V3 and definitely above the 13. On a side note, the black internals look great. 

 Now onto the not so great stuff: what I REALLY don't like about this cube is the center cap design. Even though the 12 and 13 have the same problem, it is not as bad as the 11. I have actually broken a nail trying to take one out. I know this seems like a nitpick, but considering this is a highly customizable cube (dare I say more than the 13, since more than half of its settings are too loose in my opinion) that encourages the user to test different settings -which implies taking off the center caps a decent amount of times- I don't think it is a good design. This is the only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars.  

 Nevertheless, the cube is great and I would highly recommend it even today.

review_title: Absolutely amazing but not for Roux solvers
review_text:
My setup:
 Corner-Center magnets: Triangle (the weaker ones)
 Corner-Edge magnets: 2 (The medium setting) 

 Center Distance Travel: 3 (the light blue nut on setting 3)
 Spring Compression: 3 (highest setting up is 1 and continue counting from there) 

 Lube: 50K on the tracks + 30K and a little bit of 10K on the pieces + 2-3 drops of DNM 

 This cube, when compared to the X or XS is absolutely amazing. It's easier to turn, it's easier to control and it's easier to hold (it's somehow even lighter than the XS). The corner-center magnets are the key to that. If you remove the corner-center magnets the cube becomes too flimsy for my taste even with the maximum corner-edge magnet settings. 

 However, there is one major flaw. Slice moves on the 11M Pro are hard. They're considerably easier on the XS. I am a CFOP solver, although I am roughly half as fast on Roux. I find solving on Roux to be much more tiring on the 11M Pro. Removing the corner-center magnets makes it too unstable and flimsy. I wouldn't recommend this for a Roux solver but if you use CFOP/ZZ or aren't that dependent on slice moves, go for it.

I am very excited to finally review this cube! My previous main was the GAN XS and I'm happy to say that the GAN 11 M Pro is my new main! And if you're in the market for a fast yet controllable cube, it is very difficult to beat GAN's newest flagship! 

 Before even ordering the GAN 11, the ability to choose between black and primary internals is really cool! This allows people who prefer primary internals and brighter colors to select that and get the exact same performance as the black, darker-colored version of this puzzle, and I think that makes this cube very accessible. 

 Out of the box, the first thing you notice is the weight of this puzzle. The fact that GAN added more magnets in their core and STILL made it even lighter than the XS absolutely blows my mind. This cube is very light, and this can translate to less fatigue and faster performance if you are able to control it. Speaking of the magnets, the GAN 11 M Pro features core magnets as well as magnets in the bases of the corners that attract to the core! You'll also notice the accessories box, which is essential because this cube has the most customization settings yet! On top of the GES nut that the XS includes, you are also able to adjust the corner magnets to not 3, but 7 settings (3 on the triganular magnets, 3 on the hexagonal magnets, and the option for no corner magnets at all). Changing the settings is as easy as ever. The GES nuts function identically to how they function on the GAN XS, so if you have one, you'll feel right at home with adjusting tensions. Changing the strength of the installed corner magnets is fairly easy. It does require a screwdriver, but one is included! You can also twist the magnets and remove them from the corners entirely to swap them out with stronger magnets (though I don't recommend this, and I'll explain why later). 

 As for performance, it's a GAN cube, what can I say? It's no surprise to anyone familiar with GAN's 3x3s that they all have rock-solid performance with great corner-cutting. The lightness of this cube makes it very effortless to turn, and it's clear that this is meant to enhance speed. The GAN 11 M Pro is designed to support a fast setup with its light weight and its core magnets. This puzzle works very well when set up to be fast, as you get the speed of a fast GAN cube with more stability than ever thanks to the magnets, so I think it is a good idea to exploit this and set this cube up to be fast to play to its strengths. It's a very unique cube in that regard, as you typically lose stability by making it faster, but this cube manages to stay stable despite that. If you like fast cubes, you'll probably love the GAN 11 M Pro. The only people who may not like this cube are people who use M slices frequently, like Roux solvers for example. This is because the core magnets greatly increase the amount of force needed to perform them. 

 If you don't like the cube out of the box, setting it up is fairly easy! The settings are easy to adjust making it easy to find settings that you like! The GES nuts also make lubricating the core very easy, and you can do this with a large variety of lubricants! I found that this cube works very well with Cubicle Weight 5 on the core and the tracks of the pieces and DNM-37 on the outer surfaces of the pieces. This setup can be hard to control on most other cubes due to its speed, but the corner magnets really do help make this cube way stabler than you'd expect! I find that the corner magnets work well on setting 2 with the pre-installed magnets, as this adds enough stability to the cube to support that fast setup without increasing the force needed to turn too much. You can swap the physical magnets out and use the other magnets included, which are slightly stronger, but I don't recommend this, as it leads to the only issue I have with this cube. 

 The spare hexagonal magnets fit looser in the corner pieces than the triangular ones, making them rattle when you turn, greatly reducing consistency with the alignment. This not only gives the puzzle an awkward feeling and makes the cube louder when solving, but can actually lead to some pretty major lock-ups, especially if you have an aggresive turning style. This happens frequently with the hexagonal magnets, so much so that I recommend you don't use them. This disappointed me because even though the magnets have 7 different settings in theory, in practice, they really only have 4 that don't cause the cube to lock up. However, 4 is still plenty of settings, so I see no reason why I should dock stars because of this, which leads me to my conclusion. 

 The GAN 11 M Pro is an amazing feather-light cube with easy-to-adjust settings, and the core magnets add stability that make this puzzle excellent for cubers who like fast cubes. It has excellent performance and the best customization system out of any GAN puzzle, so if you're looking for a fast and stable cube, I highly recommend you give this a shot if you can afford it!

The feel of this 3x3 is super papery and silky smooth before lubrication. I have combined a slew of lubricants in this cube but i'll try to list them here in order of which I put it in. MAX Command, MAX Fleet, DNM-37, Mystic, Cubicle Labs Silk, Compound X and then more MAX Fleet to create a slightly unstable (but still more so than my XS) and controllable 3x3 with a crisp snap when turning in succession. Funnily enough, Im not loving this lube combo, so I'm thinking about relubing with a simple Angstrom Setup. However, I set it up with Mystic and Angstrom Dignitas, which gives it a nice, plush feel while slowing it down a bit to a speed a lot more controllable but still at a relatively fast speed. I think that the magnets work best at the medium-strong area, depending on personal preference. I personally prefer the strong magnets as it counters the fast speed and makes it very stable. The core magnets add even more to the stability whilst maintaining the original speed from the cube itself. I have not encountered any major lockups since I received it and the corner-cutting on out of the box tensions is past the 50–55 degree mark. Alright so first of I'm an average at best cuber with a relatively disposable income. I think it is important to note that as I am not a pro but I'm speaking from a relative casual cuber perspective. Also, this is a Roux perspective heavy review.

 My first thoughts about this cube was a shockingly similar reaction to a number of unboxing videos. I picked this out of the cube box (which I'll actually use compared to most that come with cubes) and I was littlerally dumbstruck by the weight. I literally could not understand how light this thing is. I'm still shocked and worried I might break the thing every time I touch it. The weight drop seemed insignificant on paper but is ridiculous in practice. 

 Alright so the details. This cube is insanely easy to turn right out of the box. It's like pushing air. The magnetic bump is barely there when you are starting a turn (its especially nice when doing M' and M) yet firm when the cube reaches the end of the turn. It is honestly a little magical. 

 What about the stability you say? This cube is incredibly stable because of the magnet system. It isn't like the Valk Elite where the magnets feel a little like a wall, its more like a Gan but it is actually loose feeling and has the flex that makes the cube awesome. 

 Corner cutting, alright it is a Gan so it's good. I wouldn't dare say any less. 

 Lock ups and corner twists. Alright so I'm about 80 solves in and I haven't experienced a corner twist. In fact, I've never had this issue on any cube (maybe I'm just lucky?). As for lock ups, I have only experienced this a few time with algs that are newer to me. I haven't had any issue with my tried and true Roux. I can see how this are likely to happen with this cube, but I believe getting used to the cube will likely remove the issue. 

 So time comparisons. I have already gotten better averages on this cube but nothing near my pb singles (which I'm certain is the result of not getting a lucky scramble for me yet). 

 This cube will likely be my main over my Moyu WRM 2020 but I'm not sure yet. I will say that this cube will likely be what I do long cubing sessions with because of its weight and how easy it is to turn. I can't imagine getting tired solving on this cube. 

 I would highly recommend this cube to anyone who is willing to spend the money on it. It's, if nothing else, interesting. In my opinion it is a fantastic technological advancement that may lead to some great innovation in the way of cubing technology.

review_title: Fun to Play With, not to Eat.
review_text:
Now I know what you're thinking. "But, if it fits in your mouth, it's edible, right?" But that's not the point of this, silly! This is a review!  

 A lot of people expect the GAN 11m Pro to be above and beyond for its price. A lot of people wonder if they should just settle on a MoYu RS3M 2020 (since its a ton cheaper). A lot of people want a cube that custom fits your style, without a crazy amount of hassle. This is exactly the cube you are looking for. It is above and beyond for its price. It is, in my opinion, better than a RS3M 2020 (which I mained a Mystic version of for five months. Trust me, that's an amazing cube. Then I tried this one), and does not require a crazy amount of hassle to fit it to your standards. What makes this cube so great is that you can make it whatever you want it to be. You don't have to worry about getting the tensions wrong unlike in any cube with screws, since there are 6 levels of tension, and 4 levels of spring travel. Not to mention, how crazy diverse the magnets can feel. You can have the option to remove the corner magnets, along with set the piece magnets to weak to give a really light magnetic feel, or put in the strongest corner magnets and set piece magnets to strong, and it give a truly satisfying magnetic bump. What's odd is how light this cube feels with such strong magnets at the strongest settings.  

 I personally put my magnets at all of the strongest settings, put in the dark blue tension nuts and set them to 2. I also set my actual tensions to 3. I then used MAX Fleet as the core lube (which worked great since this cube has a plastic core, no need to use Lubicle Black). I then put in some DNM-37 and Mystic to replicate that fast yet cushiony comfort.  

 Once again, the GAN 11m Pro is worth the price because of its diversity. It is staggering that this cube is this light, and has this many settings to all be custom tailored to your liking. Sure, there are cheaper cubes. The RS3M 2020 is a great competitor. But in this case, you're buying amazing quality with incredible features.  

 However, I'm still not too sure on the taste. 1/10 would not eat again :P

I expected a lot from this cube, due to its high price, and everything i hoped this puzzle would offer, turned out to be even better. After setting it up, the corner cutting is probably the best of any 3x3 you can get. it is completely effortless even above 55 degrees. The typical airy feel of a gan cube is now combined with the stability you see in moyu cubes, most likely because of the core magnets, and i absolutely love it. My tps during LL is so much higher now. The only thing you might have to adjust to, is the cubes weight. With only 63g its a lot lighter than most flagships from other brands, but I was already used to it from the Gan XS. Nonetheless, i highly recommend getting this puzzle if you already liked Gan´s previous flagships, but missed stability when spamming tps, which this cube now has.

It is VERY important to remember the weight of this cube is at most 63.0g and compare that to the weight of your current puzzle.  My current main is a GAN 356x which which weighs in at 81.1g; it might not seem like a big difference... roughly 20 grams, but is is almost a 25% drop is weight.  This puzzle is effortless to move and to get it going the same speed as much 356x (not 356xs) I barely need to touch it.  This is allowing me to focus on things like turning accuracy and trying to turn slower. 

 My only con with this cube is that I will need to retrain how gentle I turn the cube and try to figure out how to do my OLLs and PLLs quick due to how fast the cube is. 

 Another thing to remember about this cube is the core magnets.  Since the core magnets have a short radius, it allows the cube to have less of a "bump" when aligned due to the magnetic attract not dissipating as much as the older system of magnets that are only edge to corner.  I am currently getting A LOT of timers under my current average, but I need to get used to the speed of this cube and effortless turning to remove those extreme large mistake I am making.  I would assume within 2 or 3 weeks I will be used to this cube.

review_title: Void Pyraminx is Simple and Nice
review_text:
This puzzle is almost (exactly?) the same size as original Pyraminx.  It has nice stickers in 4 four vibrant colors.  This is a VERY easy puzzle for experienced cubers, but should be a gentle introduction to newbies. 

 There are 2 main differences from original Pyraminx: there are only 3 non-corner blocks (Pyraminx has 6) on each face, and the corner blocks can NOT be twisted individually.  These two issues (mostly) cancel out: over-all, the difficulty is about the same as (perhaps a bit easier than) the original Pyraminx. 

 The quality is good overall... never had a problem with popping pieces, and only rare alignment/lock-up issues.  Like most void puzzles, the mechanics are not good for speed-solving, but otherwise no problem. 

 This is a great puzzle for newbies or a collector.

Like I said, turning is great, so it made up for it, and it only took me 11 hours to solve instead of 20. I really like non-wca puzzles and figuring them out on my own.  I have heard this solves like a "Rex Cube" but I personally do not have one.  Just like all of Qiyi's other non-wca puzzles this one did not disappoint with it's quality.  The puzzle does come with a solution, but if you understand how 4 move cycles work with set up moves this will be right up your alley. 

 ****Sidenote:  If you are interested in blindfolded solving, puzzles like this are a great introduction.  You take one alg that commutates a couple pieces, run set up moves before hand, then undo those moves.

What happens when you fusion a Dino cube with an Ivy cube? You get one of the best experience ever. Granted, most of the time solving this puzzle is just permutating petals pieces but that's part of the fun! 

 The Rex cube was arleary one of my favorite puzzles of all time, and what makes this the better choice is how well it turns, and the "click" mechanism, oh boy, it's just so good. Just breaking in and mess around is already fun enough. 

 Definetly a must-buy for puzzle enthusiasts and collectors. An 8 out of 5 in my books.

It feels high quality with the frosted tiles and the nice weighty feel, and the solve is tons of fun (especially if you try the method I used: one that reduces it into a standard Ivy Cube). Combine that with a perfectly reasonable price tag and you've got the perfect cube to ad to any cart. 

 My only gripe with it is that it is 56.5 mm in size - JUST too large to fit in my 56 mm gan cube box. That's really, really, really bugging me, but that's literally the only thing wrong with the cube. 

 I can't recommend this cube enough. Buy it. Right now. Or else. :)

The beginner solving process is very different from a 3x3x3 -- it's less algorithm heavy and instead relies more on "setups", which provides a refreshing and mind-expanding change of pace.    If I had to nitpick, the cube is a little heavier and takes a little more force to turn than a speed cube.  The solution guide that comes with the puzzle is also not the best -- for solving the corners, Cuber Stu's tutorial (at 7:58) is much better to work with.  But these are truly nitpicks.  The bottom line is that solving the cube is an enjoyable experience -- it has a much more interesting solve than some WCA competition puzzles, and its construction is second only to speed cubes.

review_title: Beautiful update of a classic cube
review_text: This is my new favorite cube! I've been obsessed with it since I got it a couple weeks ago. It's kind of challanging but once you get it it's really fun. There's a couple pretty good YT tutorials (if you search for rex cube) using two different methods. I use a combination of the two which works good. Like others have said it's basically a rex cube but it's majorly improved. Since solving the petals are like 80% of the puzzle, they made them bigger which makes perfect sense. Also the centers are bigger so it's easier to see and it turns waaaay better and clicks into place like a skewb. Feels sturdy and really well made. Awesome puzzle!

As mentioned, this is basically a rex cube with deeper cuts. The main advantage is that the inner petals are way harder to misalign and pop compared to the usual rex cube.  The pieces have a nice clicking into place, so It takes a bit of force to start the turn, but it's very hard to overshoot it accidentally. The turning on this cube is smooth and satisfying. It hasn't locked up on me yet, which I have had before with a rex cube. I haven't used this one as much though, but so far it's been great. 

 The only disadvantage I can see is that the edges being as thin as they are, are harder to spot than a traditional rex cube. Getting used to this will diminish it, but it is harder to identify them than it would be on a rex cube.  

 Looks are subjective, and you can find your preference looking at the images for both, but this cube is really nice to look at. The deeper cuts with the bigger center and petals give it a smoother look. I prefer it over the usual. Another thing that I love about this cube, is that while being stickerless, it still has the classic black outline from stickerd cubes. The inner pieces are all made so that the plastic is black, and they have some faceplate made from colored plastic. Edge pieces don't have an outline between the two colors, as a stickerd cube would. I am a fan of the look in-between one and the other.

review_title: Average cube out of the box, with some adjustments it gets a lot better
review_text:
Had to get these on sale because someone said it's better than the MF3S (which I disagree with.) If this cube were more expensive, it wouldn't get 5 stars. But on sale, it's a good cube after you spend a few minutes tweaking it. 

 Out of the box, I didn't like it. It's gritty, doesn't turn particularly quick, feels very tight, and the colors are pastel-based. Corner-cutting is decent, about 45. 

 Where this cube starts getting good is when you pop off the center caps and loosen the screws about 1/2 turn. They come from the factory fully cranked down. Then add a few drops of your favorite thin lube and this cube starts to feel completely different. Turning resistance drops greatly and the lube takes a lot of the gritty feeling away. It is a bit loud, along the lines of a Thunderclap design. 

 Very good for a budget cube, after those minor tweaks. It's no GTS2, but it's also ~1/10 the price. I hate the colors, but that's about the only thing you can't easily change.

review_title: Excellent value, quality-feeling, beginner speed cube.
review_text:
The QiYi Warrior W is an excellent introductory speed cube at a budget price. If you have recently learned beginner method on an old-style cube and would like to try your hand at speed solving, this cube would be a good choice. The QiYi Warrior W is a very smooth-turning cube that is quite forgiving with misalignments, and has adequate corner-cutting ability. The surface of the cube is not 'glossy' like the Mofang Jiaoshi stickerless, nor is it 'frosted' or 'pebbled' like the Shengshou Gem; I would call the texture of this QiYi 'matte-textured.' It offers a nice, controlled grip without being slippery or 'grabby.' It has a spry and flexible feel without being unstable.
  I tightened the factory tension of my wn cube ever-so-slightly, rotating each screw just 90 clockwise to achieve a good balance of smoothness and stability. You may want to tighten or loosen the tension to achieve your desired feel.
  Overall I'd say that you're not going to find another low-priced cube that will give a fledgling speed cuber the quality feel and performance of of the QiYi Warrior W. 
 *Plus, it has a nice pic of Mats on the box XD

review_title: Good starting cube, bad learning cube
review_text:
I've been trying to learn and practice fingertricks for the first time but I can tell that the cube itself is holding me back because it locks up very often and corner cutting leaves a lot to be desired. It's great to learn cubing itself, however if you want to go fast, opt in for something like the MoYu RS3 M 2020. Furthermore, it doesn't feel like it's very stable and it goes out of shape when I try fingertricking really fast. It feels nice to the touch for sure though and it is very nice to look at though blue still throws me off every once in a while; standard speedcube stuff. 

 Definitely fine for $5, but you should spend a bit more for the aforementioned cube. Cube hardware has advanced significantly since 2016.

This skewb is perfect for a first skewb or anyone who averages over 15 seconds. However, I average 6 on the X-Man Wingy, but I struggle to get 8s on this cube. 4 of the corner caps pop off if I turn somewhat fast, and this gets quite annoying for a speedcuber like me. This cube turns smooth, but the ball bearings are almost as annoying as the corners. Overall, I wouldn't get this cube. The MFJS skewb is MUCH better, and I can easily get 7s. No matter how fast you are, don't get this. The MFJS is cheaper and better.

This is a good budget skewb. It's smooth, and the ball positioning is good. But if you turn fast then the caps will get really loose or even fall off. I would recommend this to all  beginners who are just getting into skewb.

This cube is very very simple, and can be solved intuitively fairly easily if you have any experience with cubes, or adapting Skewb algs, though it is much much simpler than that. 

 The cube itself is extremely buttery-smooth, and does not have any resistance at all when turning. If you do not turn it accurately you may find its lack of locking-up even mildly annoying, as it will not stop after a full turn; but again as it is an easy, simple solve, it's no big deal. Adding a tiny bit of silk to it initially made it far too slippery but after drying up a little bit it's even smoother and nicer than before. One corner creaks very audibly when turning but the rest are silent. I don't think pops are possible, so that's not an issue.  

 I personally love the shades, the yellow is maybe a bit too highlighter-bright for my tastes but they are unarguably easy to tell apart even in low lighting. The stickers are otherwise also high quality, I have not solved it so much that I would expect them to be peeling but either way they are still smooth, no chips or anything- the cube still looks new after several months.

review_title: Incredible; closest to the perfect cube (for me)
review_text:
I started cubing back in mid-2017, back when the GAN Air SM and GTS2M were the most popular cubes on the market. Since then, I've only switched mains a few times, so when I do, there's usually a good reason. Either my old cube is a couple of years old and is dying, or I get a new cube that instantly blows me away with the combination of feel and performance. I have to say, the Weilong V11 has surprised me the most out of any new cube I've received. 

 Out of the box, I was immediately excited about how the cube felt. I had been using the Weilong V9 Picube special edition for a couple of years, and the UV coating of the V11 somehow feels more premium and polished. They've likely perfected their UV coating in recent releases, but it's important to note it feels near perfect in this version. The turning out of the box also felt incredible. The feeling reminds me of a mix of qualities in recent Moyu releases or from other brands. The best way I can describe the feeling is smooth and crispy, stable, extremely fast, and good performance qualities similar to the Tornado line and modern GAN cubes with obvious similarities to the V10/V9. The 8-magnet ballcore version with springs is still exceptionally fast, so I believe the 20-magnet with maglev wouldn't be most people's choice. 

 I set the cube up with a thin layer of weight 5 on the pieces, a couple drops of FZ calm, and a couple drops of XMT 10. This setup is near perfect for me, but if you like other setups, I believe lube reacts really well in this cube generally.  

 Overall, this cube combines everything I've been looking for in a main, both in feeling and performance. It's pretty rare to find this combination, especially with the saturation of recent releases in the market, but the V11 is quickly becoming one of my favorite cubes. I'm not positive I'll switch from the V9 yet (mainly because I still love that cube and have for years), but it's very likely to overthrow it both at home and in competition. For reference, I average around mid-9, so intermediate to advanced solvers will probably like it as well.

review_title: Kind of dissapointed with the cubicle
review_text: My first encounter with the feryocore was when my friend showed me his matte one. I was very surprised with the quality and feel of the feryocore. The corner cutting was exceptional, and it had this great feel, so a few weeks later, I decided to order the UV-coated version of the feryo core, expecting the same results, if not better. Fast forward a week, and I finally get my Feryo core. out of the box, without break-in, it was very slow in my opinion, which was completely different to my friend's cube when he claimed it was "very fast out of the box", but I paid no attention to this as I just assumed it was because I didn't break it in. When I met my friend the next day, he said it was VERY different to his very own feryocore. When he thought something was wrong, I let him take out some of the lube from the cube, as I like faster cubes, and after like an hour of break-in, it was still very slow for me. After he looked at the edges and corners, he saw some grey lube, which is very interesting, as there isn't any DNM, but there was Mystic, although there was just so much that unless they put like 20 drops inside the tracks, it would never appear. My friend also said it felt like a Moyu RS3M v5 instead of a Weilong v10. The tension also wasn't tensioned correctly, as the website claims it should be 4,5, but mine came as 1,1. In the end, I believe that it most likely is a cubicle person's fault. I still believe that this is a very good cube, if correctly set up. In the end, I mean no hate to CubeHead, I am just very disappointed with the people who set this cube up. When I have ordered before from the cubicle, I've always been so impressed with its quality of cubes, shipping and how the cubes get here, and their customer service. All in all, I would still main this cube, as all my other cubes are not very good, and I am a D1 cubehead glazer (use code cubehead in the cubicle shop for a huge discount). Also, when I tap the cube, there are some spring noises, and also some vibrations. The vibrations I can sort of understand, but the sound is DEFINITELY NOT supposed to be there.

Sometimes, it is never too late to review a cube that is purchased 4 months ago. Anyways, the MoYu AoSu WR M is a 59mm 4x4 that cost 43 US dollars. My version of this cube is the Pro Shop, but it's still the same thing as the stock version. Out of the box, the feeling of this cube felt very gummy (because it's a premium tailored cube) and slow along with a hint of softness in turning. Once I broke this cube in, it became a very fast, stable, and soft feeling that reminded me of older MoYu 4x4s like the original AoSu. Along with that, the 59mm size is very comfortable to hold once I got used to it. In case you are wondering, is this any better than the AoSu GTS2? Well, there are 3 differences. First, he WR M had me spamming TPS more due to being more stable and softer than the GTS2. Secondly, the WR is more compact than the GTS2 and that allows it for more comfortability in handling. Lastly, the feeling of the GTS2 is more effortless to turn than the WR M (which is why I turn more faster and aggressively on the WR M). Also, there is one similarity in the 2 4x4s is the speed and on par stability. I have expericed no lockups and pops. Overall, people's turning styles may vary on the WR M and I recommend you to not force yourself buying one if you already feel comfortable using your perferred cube.. This is a well-built cube and I highly reccomend it.

review_title: Do not buy this.  Get the mgc, or search long and hard for a gts2m
review_text: The aosu wrm.  This is in my opinion one of the worst 4x4s on the market, for 2 reasons.  The catching/corner cutting, and price.  The main issue with this is that there is literally no reverse corner cutting, and you cannot do M slice pll parity without locking up.  While I am doing turns, the pieces will catch on each other, and it will either pop, or just stop turning.  This cube feels super scratchy all the time, no matter what lube I add, and it is a speed where it just isn't enjoyable to turn.  The only good thing that comes out of this is the size, but if you just want a small cube, just get the zhilong mini, or just deal with 1 mm more on the mgc.  My main right now is the Aosu gts2m, and I will just say, there is no 4x4 that even comes close to this.  The corner cutting is phenomenal, speed is amazing, and the shades are beautiful.  The only thing I don't like is the size, but you get used to it after a while.  Now, a lot of you will say, "just tension it right, and lube it."  And yes, I have done that.  I spent literally 3 days tring to find good tensions for this cube, and you either get 2 options.  A somewhat fast and scratchy cube that cannot corner cut, or get a decent speed that pops, catches, corner twists, locks up all the time, but corner cuts slightly better.  Most people were saying its just up to personal preference, but I do not see how anyone can prefer this over the aosu gts2m.  I'll say this again, 2018-2019 moyu > 2020-2021 moyu.

review_title: The best I've felt, but not guaranteed to be the best for others
review_text: To preface this, I've been maining the Valk 4 Strong Edition for about 6 months before getting this. Upon unboxing, the first thing I noticed was how much lighter this felt in comparison to the Valk, but also in a way cheaper. It felt less premium out of the box compared to the Aochaung WRM, which I just got a week earlier. Regardless, it was a little fast for me in the stock set-up, and noticeably faster than the Valk. I didn't find the size difference to be all too impactful. That being said, my times have dropped by around 10 seconds, which is probably a mix of this cube and me actually practicing 4x4 somewhat seriously. I set it up with a few drops of Compound X and Mystic, which has drastically reduced the somewhat cheap feeling, and has gotten it to a good speed for me. My one gripe with the cube is that the inner layer magnets are rather weak in comparison to my Valk, which leads to some decently ugly lock-ups on OLL parity. However, compared with the lock-ups I would get on 3x3 stage on my Valk, it's much less. So overall, I would recommend this to people with disappointingly small hands such as myself, or those who are actively looking for a new 4x4 main. If you're content with your current main, I don't see a great need to get this.

review_title: I couldn't have asked for a better 4x4
review_text: To put it in perspective, I'm not a super fast 4x4 solver.  I've only owned a handful of 4x4s since I first solved one in 2008. The Rubik's Revenge, a V-Cube 4, Moyu Weisu, and the original Moyu Aosu is what I've used since about 2015. Although each 4x4 has been progressively better (some more than others), I've always been a bit disappointed by 4x4s. They've always seemed to pop on me a lot even with relatively tight tensions, and be fairly sluggish. I bought a Qiyi MP before this (because the YJ MGC was out of stock). That was an upgrade from the original Aosu. It didn't pop much at first (until I lubed it and then small internal eges would come out fairly often), and it felt okay to solve. It definitely tired out my hands quickly, however. I think the magnets are too much on that cube. The Aosu WR M was a different story. It was immediately incredibly fast (actually uncontrollably fast), and it took many solves before I got a pop. I will say that, when I do get a pop, It's incredibly hard to fix. The internal edges are harder to get back in than any cube I've used before, but it pops so infrequently that I'm completely okay with that. I had to use some Angstrom Gravitas to slow it down a bit since it was so fast. My times with this cube are quite consistent. On my original Aosu I was kind of all over the place between 1:3x.xx and 1:05.xxish. My best solve was around 51 seconds. With the Qiyi MP I was only able to get one sub 1 minute solve, and the rest were not much better than the original Aosu. On this cube I'm averaging right around 1 minute. I get sub 1 minute solves every day, and I've gotten my pb solve of 50.23. I feel so much more confident solving on this cube, and my speed and consistency is very satisfying. I can't recommend this cube enough. It really was worth just splurging for a $40 cube in this case.

review_text:
This cube completely blew me away- it feels like no cube I've ever tried before, and I mean that in the best way possible. It's simply a compulsory purchase!
 Out of the box, the cube is incredibly smooth, but also unusably fast, with strong magnets but not nearly strong enough to counter the instability the loose tensions and fast factory lube it comes with. With the screws tightened about half a turn and compressions tightened by around 4 or 5 clicks, though, it really comes into its own as simply one of the, if not the best, cube(s) ever produced. 
 Immediately noticeable is, it has very strong magnets, and they produce a very controllable feeling when tightened but are a hinderance when the cube is loose. It's also extremely smooth on almost any tensions, but the most amazing characteristic of it is its effortless speed. It's sooo easy to get a vast amount of speed of the cube, all the while it feeling light and almost without any effort needed. This makes for a wonderful solving experience- one of the major advantages of this is that one can go for long sessions with reasonable ease, because the cube isn't at all tiring to use. Out of the box it definitely needs lubing, the factory lube is a bit light so it doesn't help to slow the cube down- however, the skirts act somewhat like shields against factory lube getting all over the pieces and outside, which is useful. The core magnets are very noticeable, both in the extra stability they provide with corner-core, and the extra speed boost from the edges. There are only a few main problems with this cube- in fact, the only real one I can think of is that it is very fast, and for those that prefer slower cubes, it's hard to slow this one down to being an actual 'slow' cube, as this impedes it too much. All in all, though, it's truly an incredible cube. It's not the cheapest, but is so very worth the price!

product_name: MoYu WeiLong WRM V9 3x3 (Ball-Core + MagLev + UV)
review_text:
I don't even know where to start with this thing. When I got it back in July, I was expecting something good, but this shattered any expectation I had for it. It truly does everything well. Out of the box, it's extraordinarily fast, but it is very possible to tame this speed. The corner cutting is perfect, and flows very well in solves. I have a very clumsy turning style, and this cube is good enough to keep up with my inaccurate and weird moves. My times dropped off a cliff after I got it, too. Before, I could barely manage a sub 10 solve, and was averaging around 15s. With the help of the v9, I've got a bunch of sub 8 singles, and my average is down over 3 seconds. Part of that may be due to the crazy amount of solves I've done on this cube, which is probably close to 15000 at this point, but I would never be here if the cube wasn't so pleasant to use.  

 With that said, it's not all sunshine and rainbows. There have been a few days where I completely screw up my solves due to terrible alg execution before blaming the cube and giving up. How much of that is due to the v9? Probably not much, but it's worth mentioning. Additionally, the cube makes a bit of an irritating noise. While not the end of the world - you can just wear headphones while you solve - it's nowhere near the more pleasant sounds of a X-Man Tornado or Dayan cube. The only other issue is that you cannot remove the logo, and websites have stopped selling replacement blank center caps. Maybe it's just me, but I hate having a logo on my cube, so I'm glad I was able to buy a blank white cap when it was available. Having said that, those are pretty minor gripes in comparison to how great the performance is. 

 One thing I've seen mentioned a lot is that this cube lacks adjustable magnets, and after using it for a while, all I can say is "Who cares?". Adjustable magnets feel a lot more like a gimmick to me, and I don't feel their absence at all. This cube also uses the same MoYu double adjustment system that's been in action since the days of the GTS3M, and it's still a great system. Gan can brag all it wants about the 14's "1296 combinations", but a screw gives you far more control than anything else. The easy use of the spring tension adjuster is also great, as you can easily tell your setting without the use of a microscope (unlike some other cubes...).  

 In the end, this is the best cube I've ever used, and I can't recommend it enough. It's adjustable enough to fit a wide range of turning styles, and the price is completely fair in my opinion. 10/10.

review_title: Very solid cube with a horrible OOTB experience
review_text:
Initially, this cube had a terrible feel straight out of the box, likely due to its loose tension and the edge-to-core magnets. It's too fast and prone to corner twists. To fix this, I suggest tightening the screw at least half a turn and adjusting the tension by 3-4 clicks. Additionally, adding some lubricant (it eats lube like most WRMs), can slow it down slightly.  If you are a forceful turner, you might prefer a strong lube.   

 After the setup, this cube provides an unparalleled cubing experience compared to current flagship cubes. It resembles the WRM 2020, which was my favorite iteration of the WRM but with the added corner-to-core magnets, maglev, and edge-repelling magnets. Although my main cube was previously the Tornado V3, which is still excellent (I use it for one-handed and blind solves still), the corner-to-core magnets on this cube feel perfected and necessary. The Tornado V3 has corner-to-core magnets, but they do not auto-align like the Gan 13 or the RS3M Super/YS3M. The WRM v9 aligns well without overpowering the turn style. 

 Moreover, the UV coating on this cube gives it a sturdy and well-made feel without adding too much weight. Although I previously did not understand the hype around UV-coated cubes, I now appreciate their benefits. 

 The only downside of this cube is its loudness compared to the V3 and older WRMs. However, using the right lubricant can minimize the clacking sound. 

 Also, Moyu, please stop making so many versions of your cubes.  They could have gotten away with just making this version and calling it there (Maybe one with UV and one without UV coating).  The other 2 versions of the V9 are entirely unnecessary with the YS3m and the RS3m Super on the market.  

 If you want the best flagship experience on the market and you don't mind parting with 40 dollars, then get this cube.

review_text: This cube is absolutely amazing, until now I've been maining the UV Coated GAN 13, which is a great cube in its own right, but for me personally this absolutely blows the GAN 13 out of the water. Out of the box it's completely dry, which some might see as a bad thing, but it's great for customization, I personally use the angstrom lubes with some DNM and mystic and this is the best turning cube I own now. Out of the box it's extremely loose and it auto-aligns from basically any angle, after lube and tensioning it doesn't auto-align as aggressively but it still auto-aligns more than any other cube I've ever used. It's so snappy and crunchy, and it's a feel that I'm in love with. There is one huge downside though, the dual adjustment system. You have an adjustable ring for compression which works pretty well but is completely unmarked, you just need to figure out how many clicks you're on by resetting to 1, but that's not a big deal, what is a big deal however is Moyu still using a screwdriver... this allows for uneven tensions on each side, which is a huge issue. Moyu is using the same dual adjustment system they've been using since 2018 and it's time for a new one. I tried as hard as I could to keep my tensions even but sometimes it feels like my sides are just slightly different tensions and it bothers me A LOT. That combined with the lack of magnet adjustment is what knocks this cube down to 4 stars, if it had magnet adjustment and a better dual adjustment system this cube would be perfect. As is, it's an absolutely fantastic cube and can work as a main for anyone who likes a crunchy and snappy feel, but the adjustment features are lacking and that brings it down.

 However, this cube is old technology.  

 Let me explain. 

 If you compare the piece design of this cube to the GTS3M, it's exactly the same, minus the ridges. The feet of the edges and corners are from the WR M 2021, and the ball-core design and dragon-scale pattern are from the YS3M. This cube is an amalgamation of MoYu's previous technology, and although the result is a cube that performs exceptionally well, I would like to see some actually new stuff from MoYu. review_title: Go for better options...(Full recommendations and information for cubers)
review_text: It feels more premium than other cubes of this price and under, but is it worth it? I think it isn't necessary for its price. Generally the cube has issues. It can catch under inaccuracies which are common in solves. These inaccuracies are not even turning inaccuracies, but moreover the cube flexing and then catching rigidly, ruining fluidity in solves. Also, the settings are not good. Observing it without Maglev, it has completely unreasonable tensions. The cube, when on some very loose setups, cannot even properly reverse cut in some positions. The cube feels somewhat stable on loose setups like 2 for tension, 2 for compression, but still locks up and catches. Even though the cube is smooth, it fails to give lighter turning and is still mid-tight with the second lowest compression and tension. I said the cube is tight, but it still corner twists a lot with certain turning styles on "low" settings. Going back to out of the box experience, the cube felt sandy and the layers spun uncontrollable, feeling flimsy. Beginners probably won't be happy with the cube out of the box, continuing for a while, and may continue to not enjoy the cube for some time. The better option is to buy at least some lube(a couple to experiment with, or at least one or two you are certain to rely on). After between 6 and 7 months, the cube proved how unreliable it really is. The plastic core which held the springs and centers(and the whole cube in technicality) snapped when I was practicing algorithms. One center fell apart and the cube exploded very violently. I wasn't able to fix the cube because of how the part of the center holding the dual adjustment system snapped off. I can conclude that the plastic wasn't long lasting and wore away. Although I got a decent smooth feeling from the cube, it didn't last long which disappointed me. You would probably be happier simply buying two/three premium or standard lubes(Moyu lube or Gan lube, if you have to) along with the Rs3m 2020, 2021, Or Super Rs3m standard. If you really are into getting a Weilong, go for the standard Wrm Weilong v9, seeing that it is more fluid, less tight, having better corner cutting, and reinforced with a metal core for all versions, making it have longer-lasting performance. It also is satisfying to turn and nice. It may be 4 dollars more, but just not having to buy replacement plastic cores within what is probably a year or less is enough to compensate for that. Otherwise, go for the Weilong v11 Magnetic version, and purchase a setup as simple as Moyu Lube and Dnm-37, and you will get a more tactile, fluid, light and soft experience still having high stability. Uv coating for five dollars is nice if you really want it, but then the cube is worth the Rs3m V5 Ball Core UV, so consider that too. But the matte finish on the New v11, like the v10, is very good and will develop to become nice and responsive. I'll tell you that that cube also has some issues with it falling apart, so be warned. Overall, thanks for reading and home you learned something, but get an Rs3m or other standard weilong, and turning styles will be received better.

review_text:
I received the 20 Magnet Ball Core UV coated spring version, and could not be happier. I have never tried the WRM V9 so I cannot speak on how it performs against that cube, however I have used the YS3M 20 Magnet Ball Core and the RS3M V5 Ball Core extensively. If I had to describe this cube I would say it is the perfect mixture of those two cubes. It has the plushness of the RS3MV5 while also having the stability and tactility of the YS3M. I set up my cube on settings 2 for compression and 1 for tension which gives the cube a stable yet speedy feel. I lubed one edge with Angstrom Dignitas and added in about 5 drops of FZ Calm, and the cube simply feels amazing. 

 I get fantastic times on this cube and am very consistent achieving good averages for myself. I was always slightly inconsistent depending on the day when I used the YS3M or the RS3MV5, but I seem to be having no such problem with the WRM V10. I was always a bit annoyed with how clacky the YS3M was and simply how tactile it was, but the WRM V10 fixes this issue. It has just the right amount of tactility and stability while not being too much to the point where it is overly noticeable during solves. It also has a sort of GAN feel to it with a slight airiness that I haven't experienced in any brand of cube. However, in contrast to the GAN it somehow feels a bit heavier and thick than the GAN 12 Maglev. Not sure if that makes sense, but if you like the GAN 12, you will probably like this. 

 Doing my first average on the cube I managed to set my PB Single of 8.66 which was pretty interesting considering it was only about my 25th solve on the cube. I could not recommend the WRM V10 enough, and I would recommend definitely staying on the looser sides of the tension and compression as the tighter settings are indeed VERY tight.

I ordered this 2×2 with the standard lube service, and honestly, I wasn’t very impressed. I don’t think I’d do that again. I’m not a big fan of someone else touching my cube before I do. I know… that might sound silly—but it’s just a personal preference. 

 Getting back to the cube itself: my first impression wasn’t great. On my very first solve, I experienced a corner twist. I suspect this may have been because the cube was left a bit too loose after the lubing service, though I can’t say that for certain. 

 After tightening the cube and re-lubing it myself with GAN No. 1 Lube, the turning improved significantly. Right now, it feels smooth and controllable, and I’m enjoying the performance much more. 

 That said, I’m not a big fan of the price point. At its current cost, I don’t think it’s easy to justify—especially when there are solid alternatives available for less. I also feel that higher prices make it harder for less-fortunate cubers to get the cubes they want. 

 Because of that, I wouldn’t recommend this cube at its current price. If it were priced around $24.99, I’d gladly give it a 5 out of 5 stars. As it stands now, I’d rate it around 3.5 out of 5 stars. This one is hard to judge, though—there’s a good chance I might bump it up to a 4 out of 5 after more time with it.

review_title: Unlike the year this cube released in, the GAN11 M Pro is actually phenomal.
review_text:
I've mained GAN cubes since the Air SM in 2017, and the 11 M Pro is no exception. Right out of the box, it was an instant main; it was solid, sturdy, and stable, and the weight wasn't a problem like I anticipated. It's lightness actually makes it much more satisfying to use. 

 I set mine up with a mixture of heavy silicone lube with some Lubicle Silk and DNM-37, and have the light blue tension nut on 1, tightest spring compression for the GES, and the triangle magnets on 3. This setup has a very strong magnetic feel, which I enjoy, but it glides effortlessly when turning quickly. The puzzle is buttery smooth, controllable, and fluid, and is light and crispy while maintaining the traditional GAN smoothness. It's stable and sturdy, and doesn't flex as much as the XS thanks to the next omnidirectional magnetic positioning system. 

 All the customization options are cool, but I do think they're a bit overkill. The tensioning and spring compression from the XS is perfect, but the new magnets are a bit much. I think having two sets of corner magnets, the triangle and hexagonal ones, it completely unnecessary. Having the adjustable 1, 2, and 3 in the corner piece is enough, and removing the stock corner magnets was pretty much impossible anyways. 

 As for the UV coating, it makes the cube look spectacular, but in terms of grip, I don't notice much of a difference. One thing that's weird with the UV coating though, is that it seems to retain sweat a lot easier, so if your hands are sweating, the cube becomes really slippery, and it takes a bit more effort to dry it off. 

 Overall, the 11 M Pro is a superb cube. But for $70, I don't think you'll be missing out on too much if you go for other, cheaper options that are almost as good.

review_title: Essentially everything that I wanted out of a smart cube
review_text:
Pros:
 Overall great turning: fluid, good corner-cutting, and very few lockups
 User Base: As of 1/27/22, the app had plenty of people available to battle/friend around the clock.
 Battery: Never had issues with running out of battery even with long cubing sessions
                                                                         
 Cons:
 Limited Customization: Customization does exist and is noticeable, however, it is not as impactful as with other GAN cubes
 Gyroscope: Mild complaint but gyroscope becomes slightly desynced with cube over a long period of time (Can be easily fixed by adjusting view of cube in app)
 App complexity: Although many of the main functions of the app are obvious, certain things like solve reconstructions, rewards, and custom algorithms (For training) can be somewhat hard to find
 Price: Kinda expensive. But there are more expensive cubes on the market nowadays.
                                                                         
 My thoughts: Overall super happy with my purchase. This was the first smart cube that I own. The app worked well with my cube and personally, I had no issues getting past loading screens (Galaxy S9, Android V.10). I'm not an extraordinarily fast cuber or anything (Average 18-19 seconds) but, I was able to achieve similar times easily with this cube. The cons that I listed were just so you know what things to expect but I found that they were rather mild in comparison to the pros. If you do not yet own a smart cube and are interested in getting one, I would highly recommend this one so long as you are willing to pay the price.

I have a 19 second average using full CFOP and this was my first smartcube. It’s definitely worth the price 

 The cube turns well, is sturdy, and has never locked up on me. It has a nice magnetic feel and was well-lubricated and tuned out of the box. Although the charger is bulky, the 15-hour battery life is incredible and it charges very quickly. 

 There have been people complaining about the app, but I’ve yet to have an issue. Many of my hours have been wasted battling people online. The matchmaking keeps it a fun challenge, but takes a while to catch up with your skill level. I have a friend with a smartcube and it’s been fun racing online when we’re not in person. 

 Not having to manually stop a timer is very helpful and the app records all of your solves. After each solve, the app gives you run down of how long you took on each step. (Currently that part only supports CFOP and Roux) The gyroscope is neat because it tracks how many cube rotations you made. I set my record with this cube (13 sec) and it’s my new main. 

 Aside from the timer and online dueling, the app has a few other neat features. It can log custom algorithms and help you practice them, function as a timer for non-smartcubes and a few other things that I haven’t tried out yet. 

 Unfortunately, the leaderboards reset was scheduled for only about a week after getting my cube, (R.I.P. 600 trophies 🏆) but that meant I was momentarily placed 22nd in the world! (Sure, there were only 22 people on at that time, but no one needs to know that. 😏) 

 Bottom line: This is a high-quality Rubik’s cube even without the smartcube aspect of it. When you factor in the online matchmaking and training tools, it becomes that much better. This is 100% worth the price.

The gan356 maglev is a decently fast cube with noticeable auto alignment and very reasonable magnet strengths. According to gancube this release is intended to bring back some of the characteristics of the older gancube releases such as the gan356 X from 2018, while having some of the new technologies such as maglev and corner to core magnets, I have to say they did a great job with that. The gan356 maglev uses the gan356 X piece construction making the turns feel slightly heavier which I enjoyed. Inside the center piece, you can find the exact same maglev and dual adjustment system as on the gan13 maglev, the addition of maglev gives this cube a clean and fast feel, it would also eliminate core friction and spring noises. For the edge and corner pieces, it uses the classic magnet capsules design but this time is blue, this ensures that the magnets can be placed as accurate as possible and reduces the distance between two magnets making the magnets feel stronger without having to use thicker magnets which could help with weight reduction. The gan356 Maglev does not have adjustable magnets like on the gan13 and gan14, but there still has corner to core magnets, it's small radius magnet placement enables for large angle auto alignment even without edge repelling magnets.
 Overall, the gan356 Maglev is a great cube at a reasonable price, if you're looking for a gan cube with maglev and core magnets but don't want to spend that much for flagships like the gan14, this would be the perfect choice for you.
