I was very pleasantly surprised by this cube. I bought 5 when they were on sale for multiblind purposes. I wasn't expecting much from them...kinda thought that they would be a small upgrade to the guanlong or something. I was somewhat right -- it is an upgrade to the guanlong, but not a small one at all. This cube is seriously good for a budget cube. After breaking it in I got a 13.50 ao100 on it and for reference, my PB ao250/global average is 13.42. 
 As for performance: its very fast, even at tight tensions. When set up right it can corner cut 45 degrees without too much effort (but this isn't really necessary for a cube to be good), and its stability is very nice too. The only thing that leaves it feeling like a budget cube is it's lack of reverse corner cutting. It can only reverse cut a little bit, comparable to the guanlong, and that leads to lockups here and there when your turning isn't perfectly accurate.
 I'm very happy with this purchase and I'll probably end up getting more when I get a successful 20 cube multiblind and want to try more.

Don't disrespect this thing by comparing it to a guanlong, it's so much better! I've been using a Weilong GTS as my main for months and I literally got a PB within my first 5 solves with this cube out of the box. No lube, no tensioning. 

 Am I saying it's better than a weilong? Of course not. But as far as cheap cubes go, this is officially the king as far as I'm concerned. Fast, crisp, controllable, doesn't catch, corner cuts reasonably well, and just plain cooperates with any moves. Plastic feels a bit thinner compared to more premium 3x3s, but for the price, that's expected. I would recommend this to anyone: beginner, intermediate, or pro.

The mechanism of this puzzle is very similar if not almost identical to the YJ Guanlong. The corners are essentially the same, however the biggest difference comes from the grooves (which are meant to reduce the amount of friction between the pieces) to on the edge pieces.  

 Overall, this puzzle is quite good for its price. It certainly feels more substantial/less flimsy than the Guanlong. And it's stability is comparable to other cubes in its price range. When I first turned this cube I was initially reminded of the Cong's Design Meiying, not because of the feel, but because of how they share a ratio of good speed to control-ability. This cube is also a bit loud and clacky (which may be a turn-off for some). The corner cutting is definitely lacking compared to puzzles in higher prices ranges, although after the 500+ solves I've put into mine I can't seem to recall any infuriating lockups (this may be a result of my turning style). 

 Pros: 

 -It's $4
 -It fast but controllable.
 -Is relatively smooth and good feel.
 -You can never go wrong with standard Moyu sticker shades.
 -Doesn't feel flimsy/very light like the YJ Guanlong. 

 Cons: 

 -Loud and kind of clacky
 -Corner-cutting is mediocre/inconsistent 
 -Thicker lubes don't seem to have a significant effect on it (in the long term). I dumped Traxxas 50k in mine and after 20ish solves it felt as if I hadn't lubed it.

Turns well. Build quality is quite good. This is clearly in a different league than the weilong GTS; and that's fine. I am purchasing 30 of these for my daughter's 3rd grade class. At $4 each this is a superb value.  

 It is very fast, and lacks some stability relative to the 'pro' cubes. But fine for teaching the basics. Far superior to the classic Rubik's cube of my youth.

review_title: Proably The Best Mirror Cube, But Definitely Could Be Better
review_text:
Let's start with the good parts: Pretty smooth turning, as long as the layers are aligned of course. It can corner cut 45 degrees (in relation to center rotation) some sides, though others cut less depending on the pieces. Still' cuts more than others from what I seen however. Why cutting varies has to do with the way the pieces interact with each other as larger ones tend to cut easier than smaller ones, not really the side tensions like it would be on evenly-proportioned puzzles. Reverse cutting is about as much roundness as a piece has since it can't have any sort of internal curves due to how the pieces being such different proportions. Though the curves are enough to prevent pieces from catching unless they are misaligned to a large enough degree. It also doesn't pop as long as the tensions aren't too loose, like most any puzzle nowadays. The spring power is also just right as it's fast, yet not uncontrollable. It also comes pre-lubed so you don't have to use any for a while unless you want more or a different feeling kind of course. 

 Now for the couple of bad parts: The varied proportions of the pieces catching on your fingers coupled with there being no sort of internal corner-twist prevention mechanism means it corner twists a lot. If you want to tension it, which I bet you will, then you will also have to remove (and probably inadvertently mar like I did) a sticker on the thinnest side as the cap is embedded UNDER the sticker rather than being the entire top. The rest have normal caps. Though I really don't like the stickers anyway. The edges catch on your fingers a lot (not even just your fingernails) and chip up. The brush marks that are all too common on mirror cubes are also present here, which I hate because even when you have it solved (all sides flat), it may not look solved because centers may be rotated and thus shine differently. I don't know why most mirror blocks have these sorts of stickers anyway as they don't even look "mirrored" and just make you do a center-rotation algorithm on a non-supercube to make it look right. I'd remove the stickers entirely and make it all black, but the thinnest side would look even more "marked" than having a marred sticker because of that single below-surface cap.

review_title: I Think I Like This More Than My Expensive Cubes
review_text:
I bought this cube because I have a serious speedcubing problem. If a cube gets enough positive reviews, eventually it finds its way into my shopping cart. 

 This time, I'm glad it did. 

 The Swift Super MagLev UV 3x3 is ridiculously good for the money. The first few turns caught me completely off guard. I was expecting a decent budget cube. What I got was a cube that had me looking at the box again to make sure they didn't send me the wrong one. 

 The turning is smooth, quick, and forgiving. It feels like a GAN and a WeiLong got married and had a budget-friendly baby. 

 The UV coating feels great, the magnets are strong without being annoying, and the cube just wants to solve itself. 

 The cube does sound a little hollow, but so does my head before my morning coffee, so I'm not going to hold that against it. 

 The biggest surprise is that I keep reaching for this cube instead of some of my more expensive ones. That's probably the highest compliment I can give it. 

 If you're looking for a cube that performs way above its pay grade, this one is worth a look. 

 That's all I have.

review_title: This 3x3 got me back into cubing
review_text:
I recently got back from a 6 year break from cubing and decided I wanted to upgrade my 3x3. I used to watch Cubehead a lot as a kid and found out about the Ferrocore v2, so I thought now was the perfect time to buy his cube.  

 When I received the cube from the mail, I was astonished by how much 3x3 technology has improved. I used to main the Gan 356 air m, while it felt premium, I would always would lock up and it felt like the cube was fighting my turning style. After my first day with the Ferrocore v2, I was hooked. Despite my aggressive turning style, I barely lockup now, and when I do, I somehow don’t mind it. Right now after a month of relearning how to cube, I’m consistently averaging sub 15 when before my break I plateaued at sub 20. Like the packaging states, this cube really brought back my addiction for cubing.  

 Thank you Cubicle, Cubehead, and Moyu for making this cube.

I'll start with the tldr: this is a fantastic cube. It is smooth, has great corner cutting and is incredibly stable and it will make any cuber at any level happy. 
 In more detail, this cube has both positives and negatives as all cubes do. Starting with the positives, it feels amazing. Just turning it is so crunchy, satisfying and smooth and it truly as highly addictive as advertised. Coming from the rs3m V5, it feels so much more premium and elegant and it makes the rs3m V5 feel so cheap that I can't use it consistently anymore. Basically every positive thing that CubeHead and the Cubicle had to say about this cube is true. The cornercutting is one of the best I've seen although it may be a bit snappy and the UV coating on the cube is fantastic (although this is a given considering moyu has great UV coating). The autoalignment is so natural and instead of being so noticeable it can get in the way like it was on the GAN 12, it just makes sure that everything you aren't controlling when turning is where it should be and that you never over shoot your turn.
 Now going onto the negatives of this cube it definitely has some flaws that may be a dealbreaker for some people. Firstly, it has that half blocky feel of the stock moyu v11. I've tried a few v11s with different setups and settings and the feryoocore v2 is definitely not as blocky as them but it still does have that snappy feel that the stock v11s have. Some people really like it including me, some people don't but this cube is in that middle ground where it may either end up pleasing everyone or no-one. Secondly, I'm not the biggest fan of the setup this version of the cube comes with. It is such a naturally fast cube that adding such fast lubes in mystic, stealth and dignitas almost feels wrong. With that being said, the feel that the cube has is exactly how CubeHead described it where it is fast and controllable, it is just that I personally don't think it fits this cube well. For me, I added some pilube blue 10k and lubest xmt just for that gumminess and it felt so much better and I started to average faster than I did on my previous main. Finally, the magnet strength is incredibly strong. Not just "ah there is a bump" strong, but "OH THERE IS A BUMP" strong, especially when the cube is completely dry. Once lubed, as Phil said in the overview video, the magnet strength becomes manageable but I will say it is still pretty strong. Because of the magnets, it took me some time to get use to the cube and truly become my main but once I did get use to it the magnet strength did add some well needed controllability to the cube so I guess it is a positive and a negative.
 With that being said, this is still a fantastic cube and should be a contender if you are looking for a new main and it is within your budget. CubeHead's spring and screw settings are fantastic so copy those if you are not sure, but his lube setup may be too fast, although it is also a good place to start if you are stuck on which setup to try on this cube. As critical as I was in this review I just want to say that this cube is definitely my new main, it beats any GAN 16, GAN V100 or V11 and I can guarantee that if you get this cube and you set it up well, you will enjoy it a lot even if it does not become your main right away.

review_title: Feryoocore V2 UV — CubeHead’s Setup vs. the Standard Ferrocore V2
review_text:
To start, I own the Feryoocore V1, four Ferrocore V2 UVs, and the Steven’s Signature Ferrocore V2. Now, with the Feryoocore V2 UV, that brings my total to seven Ferrocores overall—six V2s and one V1. So, it goes without saying that I absolutely love this cube. It is definitely my main. 

 To give some perspective, I’m not really a speedcuber. I mainly attend speedcubing events to have fun. I use this cube because of how smooth it is. It rarely snags, even with my bad turning. 

 I decided to make the Ferrocore my main partly because it finally let me stop buying other cubes. Some cubes are great, while others are just… not so great. Personally, I prefer the regular Ferrocore V2 exactly how it comes right out of the box. I didn’t need to adjust anything. 

 The Feryoocore is set up to CubeHead’s specific preferences, and I like it as well, but I still prefer the standard Ferrocore V2 a little more. 

 Overall, I would definitely recommend this cube. Great quality, great design, and perfect turning.

The MoYu Ferrocore V2 UV is honestly one of the most satisfying cubes I have used. The turning feels incredibly smooth, but it still has a small amount of feedback that makes every turn feel controlled and responsive instead of overly soft or taut. The corner cutting is also very impressive, consistently cutting around 40–45 degree angles with very few lockups, even at higher TPS. Because of this, the cube feels extremely forgiving during solves and handles imperfect turning very well. 

 One of the best parts of this cube is the balance between speed and stability. Compared to some premium GAN cubes that can sometimes feel too fast or flexible, the Ferrocore V2 feels much more stable while still being quick and effortless to turn. The slight "tug" during corner cuts also adds a really satisfying feel that makes it hard to stop solving on, which is probably why people describe it as "highly addictive." 

 The Yoo setup from The Cubicle is a great middle ground. The tensions, compression, and lube combination make the cube feel balanced and stable without relying too heavily on strong magnets or an overly tight setup. It also has a wide range of customization, so you can make it tighter for more control or looser for a faster feel depending on your preference. 

 For around $70 USD with the Yoo setup ($60 USD for no set up), the Ferrocore V2 honestly feels like one of the best value flagship cubes currently available. Compared to some more expensive premium cubes, especially certain GAN models, it delivers a smoother and more forgiving experience while still feeling extremely high end. 

 Overall, I would easily give this cube a 5/5. It combines smooth turning, strong corner cutting, stability, and customization into a cube that feels both premium and very enjoyable to solve on.

Out of the box, the FerYooCore felt buttery smooth, fast, and controllable. It immediately reminded me of my beloved GuHong Pro M — but with a much more bubbly, marbly, and poppy feel that made it stand out even more. 

 Compared to other 3x3s I own, the FerYooCore feels softer, snappier, and more lively. The magnet strength is noticeably snappier than my Weilong V10s, and it contributes to that marbly/bubbly feeling I enjoy so much. Every turn feels tactile without being harsh. 

 In solves, the Feryoocore is fast, smooth, and satisfying, though I did experience some overshooting, which I attribute more to my fast turning style than the cube itself. Corner cutting is fantastic — exactly what you would expect from a top-end modern 3x3 — and the flexibility feels just right without being floppy. 

 I haven't fully adjusted to the feel yet, but I'm confident I’ll be breaking PBs once I settle into it more. The solution experience is just too good not to. 

 As for looks, the Feryoocore nails the premium, minimalist aesthetic. If you're someone who loves clean-looking cubes and wants something ready to perform out of the box without endless setup, this is a perfect choice. 

 Pros:
 Buttery smooth, marbly, lively feel 

 Fast, snappy, and controllable 

 Fantastic corner cutting 

 Premium, minimalist aesthetic 

 Excellent out-of-the-box performance 

 Cons:
 Some overshooting is possible for very aggressive turners (minor) 

 Final Verdict:
 "The Feryoocore is a buttery smooth, marbly, and snappy cube that not only feels amazing to solve on but also nails the minimal, premium aesthetic perfectly."

The cube felt heavy (I even measured it, almost 1 gram heavier than the stock Ferrocore, 69 vs 70 grams = 1 gram of lube?? Whaaaaaat?? :-)) and slow, strangely muffled and numb. Since his setting of 5/4 
 is somewhat more loose than my 6/5 it must have been the heavy lubing. Someone here also wrote that it took some time to break in so thats what I did. But after a lot of turning and solving the initial impression remains. OK, breaking it in

Of course, everyone has its own preference and this is only my take to this story. But I think while lubing almost always enhances the character of the cube or even sets it free, there is a tipping point where too much lubing destroys the character of the puzzle and it becomes just like any other heavy lubed cube. In my view, this is what happened with this yoo-cube. Again, just for my liking.
 So, in conclusion, the Ferrocore is the best cube I have ever used (and I thought I was a Gan-Fan-Boy) but setting it up seems to be a different cup of tea. The stock Ferrocore is a raw gem that only needs a little bit of set-up to become a cube of magical awesomeness - 5/5 stars. People buying the yoo-cube lube setup should always keep in mind that this is the preference of one individual - however awesome he or she may be (and I really do think CUBEHEAD is THE Mr. MAN!!).

 While trying to set a new PB single, I inadvertently set new PBs in Ao5, Ao12, and Ao100. 

 I have a main cube (Super WeiLong V1) and a practice cube (Gan 15/WeiLong V10) but now with the FerYooCore I have a legitimate all-around main that I enjoy turning all day in any situation. 

 If you love the RS3M V5 and/or WeiLong V9/V10, buy this cube because it oddly manages to take the best elements of all three cubes to make the perfect hybrid.

 Overall, this is a phenomenal cube and it has completely transformed my perspective on what a cube should feel like. I’d recommend anyone (even beginners) to purchase a properly set up cube like the FerYooCore cube at least once. From now on, when I set up my own cubes, I have a new baseline to refer to.

review_title: Kind of dissapointed with the cubicle
review_text: My first encounter with the feryocore was when my friend showed me his matte one. I was very surprised with the quality and feel of the feryocore. The corner cutting was exceptional, and it had this great feel, so a few weeks later, I decided to order the UV-coated version of the feryo core, expecting the same results, if not better. Fast forward a week, and I finally get my Feryo core. out of the box, without break-in, it was very slow in my opinion, which was completely different to my friend's cube when he claimed it was "very fast out of the box", but I paid no attention to this as I just assumed it was because I didn't break it in. When I met my friend the next day, he said it was VERY different to his very own feryocore. When he thought something was wrong, I let him take out some of the lube from the cube, as I like faster cubes, and after like an hour of break-in, it was still very slow for me. After he looked at the edges and corners, he saw some grey lube, which is very interesting, as there isn't any DNM, but there was Mystic, although there was just so much that unless they put like 20 drops inside the tracks, it would never appear. My friend also said it felt like a Moyu RS3M v5 instead of a Weilong v10. The tension also wasn't tensioned correctly, as the website claims it should be 4,5, but mine came as 1,1. In the end, I believe that it most likely is a cubicle person's fault. I still believe that this is a very good cube, if correctly set up. In the end, I mean no hate to CubeHead, I am just very disappointed with the people who set this cube up. When I have ordered before from the cubicle, I've always been so impressed with its quality of cubes, shipping and how the cubes get here, and their customer service. All in all, I would still main this cube, as all my other cubes are not very good, and I am a D1 cubehead glazer (use code cubehead in the cubicle shop for a huge discount). Also, when I tap the cube, there are some spring noises, and also some vibrations. The vibrations I can sort of understand, but the sound is DEFINITELY NOT supposed to be there.

review_title: Great, but after heavy modding, and I mean H E A V Y
review_text:
Apologies for any grammar/spelling mistakes. English is not my first langauge. 

 Before I bought this cube, I'd had a Volt v1 as my main. I was just done with replacing an edge every 2 seconds, needless to say, this was an instant main. 

 The corner-cutting was far from ideal out of the box, so I modded the core to be more flexible. I also "florian-modded" the core to make even room for the pieces. 

 For me, that wasn't enough. 

 I sanded the edges/corners' feet (they're really round now, lmao) and the reverse corner-cutting has significantly improved. I also stretched (yes, stretched) the spring a bit to help with the cube's stability (If you have a modded core, you might notice that some pieces can wiggle around when you shake your Square-1. You don't want that to happen because it can cause some nasty pops). The pieces flow really well and I can pretty much spam TPS on it and not get stuck mid-alg. Pops are rare, but they can and will happen. 

 Did I mention I used this to break the NR average in my country? Yeah, It's pretty good. You just need to put some work and effort into it.

review_text: The slash turns are excellent. If you are reluctant to commit to solving a Square-1 (given its unique solve), the price point and quality can't be beat.

My Yuxin Little Magic just arrived today, and holy, I have concluded that it's the absolute best budget 3x3 on the market. It's even better than my Valk3 was out of the box. One of the reasons that I didn't like the Cubing Classroom cubes is because I don't like their color scheme, both stickered and stickerless. Their orange and yellow are too light and difficult to distinguish in certain lighting situations. The Yuxin fixes that problem, the colors are vibrant and high contrast, and are nice to look at as well. It's also very stable. OOTB it had loose tensions, but it still holds its cubic shape very well and feels very solid, despite being a light cube. The MFJS cubes tend to be more flexible, even on tighter tensions. The Little Magic has very good corner cutting, and a really smooth scratchy feeling. There are no bumps along the way when you turn, similar to how a Valk turns when you turn it slowly. It feels a bit cheap, but it has no quality issues - no flash in the contact points, nothing looking like it's going to break.  

 However, I have two complaints. The first is small: the logo was placed off to the side, and a part of it is hanging off the side of the center cap. That's not a big issue, but it triggers my OCD. The second issue is a bit more substantial. This cube is very difficult to tension. Like I mentioned earlier, the tensions are very loose out of the box. However, even with 5 to 7 turns, the tension barely changes. I took it apart and saw that the core and screws are extremely tiny, actually the same size as the MFJS mini cubes. The threads are very thin and tightly packed, and the core is also very small. For this reason, a normal turn on any other cube would be equal to 5 or 6 turns on this cube. It's not too big an issue, but it's just something to keep in mind when you are setting it up.  

 No, it's not going to replace my Valk or my GTS2, but I'd rather take this one outside than risk my nicer cubes.

review_title: Performs as well as high end 3x3s
review_text:
TL;DR Top of the line 3x3 after lube and magnets, great speed and flow, slightly bumpy and fast feel, I would highly recommend this cube to everyone, regardless of budget. 

 BREAKDOWN:
 To describe this cube, it has a slightly bumpy feel. It is fast but can be a little uncontrollable. OOTB, it was super scratchy and uncontrollably fast, though this was before I broke it in. If overlubed, it becomes more controllable, but the feel suffers. Corner cutting is good for a budget cube, but lacks the corner cutting that flagship cubes have, and it catches sometimes if you try to corner cut too far. I like the sticker shades on stickerless, the blue is perfect for me, but for most other people the blue is too dark. The stickerless version has a frosted feeling which is a little bit annoying, but it seems like it wears down after a while. If you get a black or white plastic cube, be aware that the sticker placement sucks and the sticker quality is low. The stickers peel. Magnets make this cube INCREDIBLE. I added N38 4mmx2mm neodymium magnets and it added a more tactile feel, and overshooting became less of a problem and stability was greatly improved. Proper lubing is necessary to bring this cube to its full potential; I recommend Lubicle Black or Traxxas 50K on the core, some lighter Traxxas lube (30K and 10K) on the pieces. DNM-37 and Silk certainly help. This combination of lube brings the cube to the excellent description as I said above. 

 BACKSTORY:
 I bought this cube back in November because I heard good things about this cube. The day I got it, I lubed it, magnetized it, and it became a beast. I had my first competition the next day and mained it over my GTS2M. I got a great average. THAT is how good this cube is.

 Anybody considering buying this cube has probably heard that the sticker quality isn’t the greatest. 2 weeks into breaking the cube in, I already had multiple stickers chipping away. Overall, I would definitely recommend this cube to anybody who has heavy lube and an extra set of full-fitted 55 millimeter fluorescents :)

 I used the Cubicle Light Magnet kit (DMcubing on Youtube has an incredible guide that anyone can easily follow if it's your first time magnetizing a cube), 30k on the core, and 10k on the pieces. Best

Yuxin Little Magic is a well known product when it comes to budget cubing, getting the standard non-magnetize cube at only $5 and magnetized version slightly over $10 (discontinued but you still can order a cubicle version of a Little Magic M for $23). Although it may be cheap and quality of its plastic may feel low when it comes to quality, it makes up for it with performance. At the price, it offers you great corner cutting, speedy cube right out of the box, any easy set up should make you feel comfortable with solving it as your first speed cube. Corner twisting or pieces popping out does not seem to be an issue with this cube as far as I know and factory stickers doesn't seem to peel off or get scratched that easily compared to other budget cubes that I've tried. 

 But it has to be some negatives being at this price, right? Sure there are few things I wish it'd change to make it a better cube. I don't really like to colors of the stickered cube out of the box, this may just be personal preference but by making the reds darker and orange brighter will make it easier to see while solving (get stickerless if you want a bright set). If you applied more than enough lube to it, it seems to fall out to the surfaces of the cube at first few solves as groves are connected to the edge of the pieces. 

 Overall, you can't expect much from a $5 cube. But with good care and decent enough set up you should be ble to use this as your temporary new main as I've done so in the past.

review_title: Amazing Cube, defiantly seen on your future shelf
review_text: This cube is an amazing cube that everyone loves. The cube is amazing in turning + corner cutting. Over all, this cube is the best budget cub ever! Its price is worth it. If you do not buy this cube now, just know there is a 99.99% chance you will se this cube on your shelf in the future. Everyone will need this cube in their collection. I would definitely  recommend this for all level cubers!

For the price, it's very difficult to touch this cube. It performs like a much more expensive cube, and there are multiple reasons why. 

 The design is VERY high quality. The corners and edges fit together in a way where they are very stable and well put together, but there is plenty of room between the edges and corners. The shades of the stickerless variant are also very nice and easily recognizable.  

 The design causes this cube to be very light. It has an airy smooth feel and I find it to be one of the most satisfying cubes to turn. 

 The performance is rock solid. When properly tensioned, it easily cuts 45° and reverses almost line-to-line. Lock ups are rare, and the cube moves pretty fluidly. Even when you tension it tightly, it moves fluidly, and even with a very loose tension, it feels controllable. This cube also has the potential to get very fast, faster than I can control. 

 Overall, I cannot recommend this 3x3 enough. If you're looking for a dirt-cheap cube, nothing even touches this. I hope this review was helpful :)

When I first got this cube, I was blown away by it's performance.  It was really fast, corner cutting was comparable to flagships, and the shades were pretty nice.  The plastic felt kind of cheap when turning, but I kind of liked that.  The turning feels blocky and crispy, and I get close to average times on this cube.  A few problems are that it is pretty unstable, so magnets would probably help a lot.  It is fairly difficult to magnetize though, and I ended up failing in the end.  Another problem is that it might be too fast and uncontrollable for some people.  I have a fairly light turning style though, so it wasn't really a problem for me.  OOTB, it's quite dry, and it could be a problem for beginners who don't know how to set up cubes or don't have any lube.  All in all, this cube is really amazing, especially for just 5 bucks.  I would definitely recommend this cube for people that are just starting out, or if you want a decent non-magnetic cube.  However, I do think that now, there are better options for slightly more money, such as the RS3M 2020, the Meilong m, and the Qiyi MS, which are magnetic, but you can't really complain, as this cube came out nearly 2 years ago.  Great job Yuxin!

review_title: worthy of the Little Magic name
review_text:
Yuxin is releasing some really cool puzzles lately and this one is no exception. This is a very light turning skewb with ball bearings - the light weight, quick turning and excellent performance definitely earns it a spot among other 'Little Magic' puzzles like the LM 3x3. 

 Feel wise I'd say the Moyu magnetic is closest in feeling, but this feels even lighter and quicker. For those who haven't tried ball bearings, at least in Skewbs I think they make a totally reasonable alternative to magnets and give a nice tactile click when the puzzles aligns. The stickerless shades on this are glossy and match the Huanglong and LM 2x2. 

 I think this is definitely a contender for best 'budget' skewb - if price is a major factor in your purchase this will give you something that performs a lot better than some of the other $6 skewbs on the market. Can it hold its own against the flagships? Possibly. I still need to set this up, adjusting the OOB tensions already helped make it more stable. I'm only giving it a four because some of the tried and true great skewbs aren't that much more expensive. 

 Oh if you're wondering about the difference between this and the Kirin Black - the Kirin Black has frosted, slightly lighter shades and uses a plastic tab in place of the bearing, giving a stronger click sensation and more papery turning. Also a cool skewb with a unique feeling. I prefer the glossy sides of this one hands down.

I own both this and the Little Magic skewb from Yuxin. Compared to the Little Magic skewb, this skewb uses frosted stickerless plastic and has a plastic tab with a bump on it in place of the bearing - the bump snaps into a depression in the centers in the same way a bearing would, and helps align the puzzle during turning.  

 This is a great skewb overall especially in the budget range - it turns fast and smooth, hedges and sledges are effortless on this puzzle. Compared to the LM there is a little more texture to the plastic on the pieces, this seems to give the puzzle a more substantial and stable feeling and it feels a bit slower. I prefer glossy plastic on stickerless puzzles but in the case of this skewb I don't have any problems gripping the puzzle. 

 The tabs are unique and I think work out well - the whole puzzle POPS when the pieces come into alignment - its not loud, but you really feel it in your hands.  

 I think either of the new Yuxin skewbs are excellent for the price, and if you're on a budget they may be the best bang for the buck, both are fast and easy turning and don't get in the way. If you like trying new puzzles this one definitely stands out to me, I don't know of another skewb that feels this way and the plastic tabs work out a lot better than I thought they would. Dropping one star because even the undisputed best skewbs aren't that much more price wise and may perform a bit better.

For $10, you're not going to find a better cube than the Kylin V2M.  

 TL:DR: Light, smooth turning that feels very good. Decently controllable, and flows well during solves. It doesn't feel as premium as an expensive flagship cube, but for the price, it's excellent.  

 Right out of the box, the turning felt great (after I loosened the extremely tight tensions). Turning was very light and effortless. A bit too effortless, actually, so I slowed it down a bit with some thick lube on the tracks. The turning felt a bit dry and sandy at first, but it broke in quickly. The cube doesn't feel soft or buttery, but it does feel very smooth in the sense that the internal mechanism glides with very little friction and with no bumpiness.  

 The corner cutting performance is a bit lacking compared to premium cubes, and cutting feels a bit harsh. Despite this, the cube flows decently well, and I don't think the cube suffers from any major catching issues.  

 The cube has a fairly cheap-sounding sound signature while solving, and the mechanism is clearly not too fancy, but it's a $10 cube, after all.  

 The magnets feel fairly light, but I think they work well. Overshooting or undershooting was not an issue for me.  Unfortunately one of the magnets in one of the corners was unglued, but that's an easy fix.  

 Overall, I'd definitely recommend this cube. I'm impressed with how good it feels given its price. Personally, I think the Kylin V2M feels better than the YuXin Little Magic M.

 This cube was sandy and slow out of the box, and even after lubing and breaking in, it's surprisingly slow. Maybe I'm just bad at lubing cubes, but I don't know how one gets this cube from what it is out of the box to one that you can finger trick enough to set records. 

 To add insult to injury, out of the box, my cube appeared dirty and scratched, like it was someone's old used cube. Makes unboxing kind of a letdown, and definitely makes this something I'd never give as a gift. Gross.

The down side of it is that the corner cutting is not quite 45 degress, and this is a PIAN to dissasemble and reassemble. you can barley pop a edge out even on lose tentions. It is really stable, tho and on lose tentions will not pop or corner twist, so that is a plus. Over all, i recemend for beginners looking for a upgrade form something like a little magic, or a cyclone boys.

They have the classic look, tiles, and magnets. It's hard handing a speedcube to a beginner because they are so fast and really meant to be used with finger tricks. These Kylin V2's are around the same price as a Rubik's but better in every way.  

 Yes, I know Rubik's now has a stickerless magnetic cube, basically a Swift Block, but I'm talking about being able to give a Rubik's looking cube to a kid and them not having to suffer with a Rubik's. There are not many options for a tiled magnetic these days.  

 I stocked up on the Kylin V2's when I had the chance. They serve their purpose. With the right lube and break-in they become a decent speed cube. I keep one in the living room next to my chair for practicing algorithms. And I have plenty to keep handing out to the children of friends who will fidget with them using wrist turns, but they will still be an adequate cube for finger tricks if the kid wants to learn real solving later on.

review_title: Little Magic 2x2 M: Great option for beginners and intermediate cubers
review_text:
The Yuxin Little Magic 2x2 M is a great budget 2x2 option, especially for beginner cubers looking for a solid 2x2 that won't break the bank.  

 Out of the box it feels somewhat dry and scratchy, but after breaking in, it becomes exceptionally smooth, and is effortless to turn. The speed is a middle ground between fast and controllable, which I personally really like. The magnets are on the weaker side, but they are strong enough to notice and do a good job at keeping the cube stable. The stickerless shades are also nice and contrast quite well.  

 My only complaint is that the corner cutting isn't fantastic, and as a result, lockups tend do happen from time to time. It can corner cut 45 degrees and reverse corner cut a decent amount if your tensions are right, but requires more effort to do so than some other 2x2s. It's also worth noting that this cube feels slightly heavier than other similar budget 2x2s, like the QiYi MS and the YJ Yupo V2 M, but overall isn't a big deal and doesn't affect the cube's performance.  

 Overall, the Yuxin Little Magic 2x2 M is a great budget option, and I'd highly recommend it for beginners and intermediate cubers. For the price of 7 dollars, you definitely can't go wrong with this puzzle.

Contrary to the name of the cube, "little magic", it seems the overall design seems to have been derived from the YuXin Kylin v2 rather than the original Little Magic or HuangLong 3x3, which is what I'll compare it to for this review. In my opinion that's not actually a bad move, the Kylin V2 was also a great cube, it was just a bit slow and it corner twisted more often than I'd like. 

 The Little Magic V2 does improve on many aspects from the Kylin V2: the cube is a lot faster and it corner cuts better, and I generally find the plastic responds far better to lubes than the Kylin V2, which are traits I enjoyed from the original Little Magic. The cube also has a spring-adjustment system, which is great for a cube aiming to compete with the RS3M 2020/2021; however, in adding the spring-adjustment system, it seems that's where designers at YuXin tried to do too much with the cube. The cube has a very bad catching problem, even after using heavy and gummy lubes on the tracks. While this was highlighted in TheCubicle's review, the main areas of catching have nothing to do with the design of the center, rather the corner and edge stock. 

 MoYu's corner stock on the RS3M/WRM, WRM2020/2021 all have a portion that is squared off to prevent corner-twisting, which in my opinion has essentially been perfected. Gan also has a similar mechanism in their Gan SM, X, and XS cubes along with their respective variants, and the MF3RS2 had a squared off corner stock and rounded edge stock. YuXin's implementation is what causes the first catching issue, where the bottom squared-off track protrudes so far into the cube that it actually catches on part of the plastic core during reverse corner cutting, and either results in a catch, or even a corner twist. The edge stock meanwhile has a very short bottom track, which makes it seem like it's more part of a double-torpedo than a secondary track, and since that is squared off, a severe enough corner-cut results in catching from the corner stock as well, which also causes catching, and sometimes corner-twisting. 

 I was able to somewhat mitigate the core-catching issue by replacing the core with one from the spare-parts of a WeiLong WRM, which is smaller. The problem with that is, not everybody has spare parts laying around like that, and while these catching issues can be further mitigated through modding, you might as well find a different cube, as the RS3M 2020 is straight-up better, not to mention having to mod cubes should forever be a relic of shengshou big cubes from the past. If YuXin would have just simplified the design of the corner and edge tracks similar to how YJ designed their ZhiLong Mini 3x3 (because they're also really similar in shape), this could have been a top-tier cube. 

 In conclusion, while the cube is fast and feature-rich, the catching and corner-twisting issues prevent me from getting anywhere close to my usual sub-20 times,. I end up performing better on my Little Magic V1, and even my Thunderclap V3 than I do this cube, which is a shame because this cube had so much potential going into it, and I would have definitely been able to switch to this cube if not for the problems which I presented earlier. I certainly don't blame YuXin for trying though, clearly MoYu set the bar very high with the RS3M 2020, which I think is a cube that's going to be very hard to beat in the coming years.

review_title: Should have been called the Huanglong 2x2
review_text:
This cube could have been part of the Huanglong series and twice its price and I would still be happy with this cube. I believe this cube feels more like the Hanglong 3x3 than the Little magic. This cube does not feel like a budget cube _at all_. But I'm glad its at a budget price!

The cube is fairly light but it feels like it has built in weight on the tips of the corners (Another similarity of the Hanglong, kind of like the ball bearings you can put in the corners) which adds to the speed of the turning. It doesn't have the same catching problem that the White had when it was tight, or a popping problem like the White had when it was loose. 

 The cube came a bit tight and didn't cut too well. I loosened it by a two turn on each screw and shoved a liberal amount weight 1 down the gap between the internal middle layer and a corner. The cube cuts like butter now. It actually cuts 45 occasionally when I was testing it out, but cuts about 40 with ease. Reverse is the same as any other 2x2. 

 If you like fast and effortless turning cubes, this is the one to get! If Yuxin comes out with a Huanglong 2x2, I will have extremely high expectations.

So, how does the 2x2 stack up? Out of the box, this cube is somewhat light, scratchy, and airy. It is also extremely fast and a little unstable. Because of these two factors, it's at the point of uncontrollability for some solvers. It's corner cutting is admittedly sub-par for a 2x2, though it's cost of $4.99 gives it some slack. OOTB, I'd rate this 4 stars, a pretty good cube. However, after set up and magnetization, it turns into a completely new cube. It gets a bit heavier, loses the scratchy and airy feeling. It keeps its speed and increases its stability. The feeling can be described as heavy, loud, mushy, smooth, and fast. I recommend this if you are willing to set it up - it is my main, though my MGC comes in at a close second.

review_title: Very Similar to the Little Magic
review_text:
The Yuxin Black Kirin is a more well-rounded package than the Little Magic, being more stable and controllable is great, but if you don't like and slippery matte plastic and corner twists, I'll look somewhere else, other than that this is the best budget cube, in my opinion, it's better than the Little Magic. 

 I'm sure everyone has said this but the pieces look and the cube feels like a Little Magic. The only differences is that the Black Kirin is actually more stable than the Little Magic and I feel like the Black Kirin is a more rounded and a more finished package than the Little Magic. Along with being more stable, the plastic may be thinner, but the feel it gives makes it feel like the plastic is more thick and nice to feel, and it's less fast and uncontrollable than the Little Magic.
      Looking at the pieces, you can see why this is true, as the tracks on the edges are smaller, adding friction, and the corner stalk is longer and has protrusions,adding stability. Even so, when corner cutting, those protrusions can be caught on and makes the Black Kirin more catchy, even so the corner cutting is actually easier than the Little Magic. 
     The only downside I see with this cube is the plastic, it's more matte and less frosted than the Little Magic, and this may be the only cube that has slipped out of my hands while solving, and corner twists can happen as the corners are more rounded off than the Little Magic, and the shades are more dark and bland than the picture suggests.

Get some lube with it. It comes very dry, so get some weight 1-3 and some dnm-37. If it's too fast, and silicone lube. If it's too slow, add dnm-37. In my eyes, if you get the lubes too, you pay less than with the other top 5x5s and get it magnetic with perfect (for me) tensions tight out of the box. Low effort and low cost without missing a single performance mark. 

 Stats for those who care:
 Stability: very good on tighter tensions (OOTB) but loosening doesn't change that. Not hugely flexible, but you want that on 5x5
 Corner cutting: good, up to par with 50 dollar cubes
 Speed: if you do what I mentioned up above,  it's whatever you want it to be.
 Feeling: it is a little sandy ootb, but after doing 5 or so solves it went away. Very smooth and crisp (like the 3x3)
 Plastic: Excellent. It's light enough to not make me tired yet thick enough to feel solid.
 Magnets: only complaint is that they are the same strength on the inner layers as on the outers. That's fine though, it's easy to adjust to. 

 To sum up: I think this is a very competitive cube with the high end cubes. It is 99% there, but if you're really that picky, get a cubicle labs 5x5M or go on youtube and look up some reviews. This is a very appealing choice to many of us who don't have the money to buy the angstrom for $70. The only downside is that you have to set it up. If you buy the weight 1-3 and DNM, it costs less than a non-magnetic Wushuang, and setup takes 5 min and some breaking in.  

 TLDR: Worth it 100%!

review_title: Amazing 4x4, definitely top 5 in my opinion
review_text:
The Yuxin Little Magic 4x4 is one of the best 4x4s in my opinion. Here’s why. 

 Out of the box I could already tell that the cube had mad potential. The cube is so smooth, even without set up. For set up, I put a combination of Weight 5 and Mystic on the pieces, and Wight 3 on the inner layers. However, one day a magnet got dislodged, but this is easy to fix. I found the 2 pieces that had the dislodged magnets, and I just put another one there. Now for the cons. This cube makes a small snap sound when doing reverse corner cuts, which is not that much of an issue, I just don’t like the sound. What is an issue, though, is the reverse corner cutting. Like our god, J Perm has said,  

 “I think that no budget 4x4 is good.” 

 He’s not totally wrong, but most budget 4x4s lack reverse corner cutting, and so does this one. It can cut around 1/2 a cubie, but no more than that. In the title, I did say that this was in the top 5, so here’s my list. 

 1. AoSu GTS 2
 2. WuQue
 3. Mini WuQue (Has a different feel due to the primary internals)
 4. Thunderclap 4x4
 5. Yuxin Little Magic 4x4 

 I would recommend this 4x4 to whoever has an accurate or light turning style. That’s my review.

Whilst the Yuxin Little Magic 3x3 was a phenomenal cube as well as the factory magnetic Yuxin Little Magic 3x3, the 4x4 really disappointed me. The outer pieces seem like they would be able to accommodate excellent corner cutting, but there are many inner pieces that just seem to get in the way all the time, and there are quite a few internal catches while turning inner layers. I tried loosening the cube a half-turn, and while the corner cutting did improve somewhat, it only revealed more problems, such as how slow and unstable the puzzle managed to be at the same time, not to mention the cube is extremely sensitive to what lubricant you use. I tried using a small amount of Weight-3 on the inner edge tracks, and that made the cube feel extremely sluggish, even after a generous application of DNM-37, so I had to clean out the cube and start all over, only to end up stripping 4 out of the 6 screws using a YJ screwdriver to undo the tensions while reassembling. I settled on using exclusively Lubicle-1, which made the cube fast and smooth enough, but when you can find the RS4M or YJ MGC for not much more for exponentially better performance, this becomes extremely hard to recommend, and it's really unfortunate given how good the Little Magic 3x3 is, and it's a shame that the quality and performance from the 3x3 wasn't able to be extended up to the 4x4, though I can't speak on any of the other Little Magics as of this review.

I've never had my hands on a fancy speedcube, but with all the push that speedcubing has put on the twisty puzzle industry, not only are 6x6x6 and bigger possible to construct, and in a non-delicate manner, they are amazingly affordable!  That is exactly what I was looking for with my first 6x6x6 cube. 

 I'm amazed it is much smaller than I expected it to be.  It's almost too small for my larger hands, as it feels like I'm solving a golfball sized 3x3x3 (my pinky is the width of two of the layers, so there is a lot of two part moves to rotate a layer for me)...  The movement is amazingly smooth compared to what I've been used to, but I suspect speedcubers will have much different criteria to judge this on...  I never had any issues with this while solving or making patterns - no pops, no lockups, etc, etc... all layers seem about the strength of magnet that I'd want (wasn't even sure it had magnets at first they are so passive feeling) to keep it just that little bit more solidly clustered while turning it... 

 Overall, I'm delighted with this cube!  If you want a 6x6x6 that will just function like the reliable puzzle you want to pass time with at a price that is reasonable, this will fit that nicely! 🙋‍♀️

review_title: One of the best after setup
review_text:
The reason why i bought this is because i want a 6x6 that performs well and doesnt break the bank. I was about to immediately buy the mgc but when i saw a review about the ylm that randomly appears in my recommendation i decided to buy this instead of the mgc. Like any yuxin big cubes. Ootb it was sluggish and the square off corner. My mind was like uhhhh why did I buy this should have chosen the mgc. And the cube covered in lube but the lube didn't make the cube any better. So decided to break in about 100 sloves and then set up. The more broken in the cube the faster the cube is. After 100 sloves the cube turned way faster than oo tb. Then I cleaned up the factory lube and lube with silk dor the smoothness, break in and dnm for the speed because the speed is not so fast. And I relied that I tensioned the cube like Ootb (I thought it was too tight at first). 6x6 and up sould be tensioned tight in order not to pop. Break in the cube and boom. One of the best 6x6. I average 5 mind in old shengshou and this cube just broke it. In first sloves I got 4:40 because I was not used to the cube and it also super slow. Now I'm average 3:10 with this cube.
 Pros:
 -Very good anti pop mechanism, never get any single pop during sloves.
 -Feel premium to me. Feel like a 40$ cube
 -Good corner cut, everything (second layer coner cut, third layer corner cut,...) always cut less one cubie, regular coner cut more than 1 cubie, reverse less half a cubie. 
 -Cheap
 -The third layer is not slow
 Cons: 
 -Lock up is the major problem in this cube. Although the cube is tight it still happens but not too often. Some of them can be easily fixed but sometimes the lockup very bad and it affect the times badly (not often).
 -The cube itself is not very fast. It maybe pretty slow for some people but dnm will fix it.
 -The magnet in second and third too strong for me.
 Summarize, it is a very good cube with a cheap price. I have had this cube for months and completely satisfied with it. Just give this cube a try. I would recommend this over yushi (100%), mgc (when you hate pops and super fast speed), shadow ( when you hate slow big cubes). Although it's not perfect but yuxin did a Good job on this cube.

YuXin Little Magic 3x3 M

Having never tried the original Yuxin Little Magic as of this review, I can't really relate to some of the frustrations former Little Magic solvers seem to be expressing; that being said, I think there is more good than bad with this cube, and there's not too much that can't be fixed with a little bit of setup. Without any setup however, the cube is very uncontrollable, and overshooting is a common problem, but that can usually be fixed with Angstrom Gravitas on the tracks; however it seemed on my end that the cube did not respond well to the Gravitas, I'm not sure if it has something to do with the minuscule size of the tracks themselves, or if it's just the nature of this particular design. I ended up settling on Weight-3 and Lubicle-1, and that preserved much of the speed of the cube while increasing the amount of control. It's unfortunate that the design of the edge piece doesn't accommodate the RS3M+ Upgrade Kit so well, and thus the magnet setup doesn't seem to add much to the overall performance of the cube. But all these are mostly just nitpicks and not huge problems, perhaps the way the cube can quickly run its lubricant dry within 10 solves may be an issue, in which case I would just go with heavier lube, nor am I a particular fan of the hard-plastic feel, but as a wise man once said, "you really can't be too picky at this price point". I'd reckon someone who likes to setup their cube would be better off magnetizing a non-magnetic Little Magic, and perhaps swapping the primary internals from this cube, and thus making a far better cube that way, but if you just want a decent magnetic 3x3, you can't really go wrong with this, though I would pick the RS3M 2020 all day every day over this cube for just an extra dollar.

The Yuxin Little Magic M is a very good cube. Before I bought this cube, I had only tried a little magic once so I didnt remember what it felt like. Out of the box, it had a nice sandy feel that has since gone away just a bit. The performance is good except it can get these weird lockups. Overall, I would recommend this cube to people who like fast, sandy cubes. The little magic is another example of how budget cubes are becoming better than most flagships.

My previous main was the Gan 356 M. I actually switched because i just liked the more clicks and smooth feel. When i had to do a lot of corner cutting, for like an E perm, it would perform much better than the Gan.

My son was doing fast turning on the first day he got it and cube broke; 2-3 edge pieces fell out. He was able to put it back but he’s not too thrilled with this cube. The other ones he has are durable even with him constantly practicing the turning.
